entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2016/2320, an EU act that confirms or amends the provisional calculation of average specific CO2 emissions and specific emissions targets for individual manufacturers and manufacturer pools of new light commercial vehicles for the 2015 calendar year, under Regulation (EU) No 510/2011. It exists to give a freight-forwarding workspace with a light-commercial-vehicle fleet or LCV-procurement exposure a record of a completed EU CO2-compliance cycle: which manufacturers and pools were confirmed compliant or non-compliant for 2015, and what mechanism (excess emission premium, small-volume derogation, de minimis exemption) governs that outcome.

FACT: "In accordance with Regulation (EU) No 510/2011, the Commission is required to calculate each year the average specific emissions of CO 2 and the specific emissions target for each manufacturer of light commercial vehicles in the Union." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2016/2320, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32016D2320

*Analytical inference:* this Decision is a Commission act addressed to named manufacturers and pools (Section 8), not a rulemaking that creates a compliance duty running to a freight forwarder; its relevance to the workspace is indirect, through the CO2 standards regime's effect on LCV supply and cost.

FACT: "Done at Brussels, 16 December 2016." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2016/2320, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32016D2320

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "Having regard to Regulation (EU) No 510/2011 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 11 May 2011 setting emission performance standards for new light commercial vehicles as part of the Union's integrated approach to reduce CO 2 emissions from light-duty vehicles" *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2016/2320, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32016D2320

*Operational implication:* Regulation (EU) No 510/2011 is the parent CO2-standards regime for new light commercial vehicles in the Union; this Decision is one annual confirmation cycle under that regime. A workspace operating or leasing LCVs registered in the Union should treat the underlying regime, not this single Decision, as the durable source of cost and supply pressure on its fleet, and this Decision as one dated data point (the 2015 cycle) within it.

FACT: "This Decision is addressed to the following individual manufacturers and pools formed in accordance with Article 7 of Regulation (EU) No 510/2011" *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2016/2320, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32016D2320

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this Decision applies to the specific individual manufacturers and pools it lists in its own Article 2, not to a freight-forwarding workspace directly; whether a workspace's own fleet contains vehicles from a manufacturer named in that list is a fact-specific question outside this brief's scope.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

*Analytical inference:* because this Decision closes a single, already-completed 2015 compliance cycle (confirmed 16 December 2016) and creates no forward-looking obligation running to the workspace, there is no immediate compliance action item here. The one live-relevance item is a compliance-status flag, not a deadline:

FACT: "On 3 November 2015 the Volkswagen Group made a statement to the effect that irregularities had been found when determining type approval CO 2 levels of some of their vehicles." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2016/2320, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32016D2320

FACT: "As a consequence the values for the Volkswagen pool and its members (Audi AG, Dr Ing. h.c.F. Porsche AG, Quattro GmbH, Seat SA, Skoda Auto A.S. and Volkswagen AG) cannot be confirmed or amended." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2016/2320, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32016D2320

*Operational implication:* a workspace whose fleet includes Volkswagen-group light commercial vehicles should treat those vehicles' 2015 CO2 compliance status as unresolved as of this Decision's own text, not as confirmed compliant or non-compliant either way.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the obligations this Decision states run from the Commission to the individual manufacturers and pools it names (Article 2), and from those manufacturers/pools and Member States to the Commission (data submission, error notification). None of the captured text states a duty running from this Decision to a freight-forwarding workspace, a carrier, or a logistics intermediary. Whether a specific vehicle-purchase or lease contract passes through any cost consequence of a manufacturer's excess emission premium is a fact-specific commercial question outside this brief's scope.

*Analytical inference:* the workspace's practical position in this chain is that of a downstream buyer or lessee of the vehicles whose manufacturers are named in Section 8, not a party to the compliance mechanism itself.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: "Having regard to Regulation (EU) No 510/2011 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 11 May 2011 setting emission performance standards for new light commercial vehicles as part of the Union's integrated approach to reduce CO 2 emissions from light-duty vehicles" *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2016/2320, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32016D2320

*Per the workspace's reading:* Regulation (EU) No 510/2011 is the controlling parent instrument; this Decision is a yearly implementing act under it (Article 8(6)) confirming or amending one calendar year's provisional calculations, not a new or amended statute in its own right.

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

FACT: "The Commission reserves the right to revise the performance of a manufacturer as confirmed or amended by this Decision, should the relevant national authorities confirm the existence of irregularities in the CO 2 emission values used for the purpose of determining the manufacturer's compliance with the specific emissions target." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2016/2320, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32016D2320

*Operational implication:* the Commission has not closed the door on revising a manufacturer's confirmed or amended 2015 performance figures if a national type-approval authority later confirms an irregularity; a workspace tracking a specific manufacturer's compliance history should treat this Decision's figures as subject to that reserved revision, not as permanently final.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this brief's own corpus is limited to the single captured EUR-Lex page for this Decision; a workspace with a live question about whether any such revision has since occurred should confirm current status directly against EUR-Lex rather than relying solely on this record.

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does this Decision create a direct regulatory obligation on a freight-forwarding workspace?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* No obligation running to a freight forwarder, carrier, or logistics intermediary is stated anywhere in the captured text. The Decision's obligations run to the Commission, Member States, and the named manufacturers and pools listed in its own Article 2 (Section 8).

**Q2: Is a workspace's own LCV fleet named in this Decision?**

*Analytical inference:* No. The only addressees are the specific manufacturers and pools listed under Article 2; a workspace is named only insofar as it may operate vehicles produced by one of those manufacturers.

**Q3: Does the small-volume derogation or de minimis exemption change what a workspace can buy?**

FACT: "‘D’ means that a derogation relating to a small volume manufacturer has been granted in accordance with Article 11(3) of Regulation (EU) No 510/2011 with effect for the calendar year 2015." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2016/2320, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32016D2320

*Operational implication:* these mechanisms determine which named manufacturers were held to a specific emissions target for 2015 at all; they do not themselves restrict which vehicles a workspace may purchase, but they do describe why some manufacturers in the Annex tables carry no target figure.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: this is a Commission implementing decision addressed to named manufacturers and pools, not a regulation with obligations stated to run to a freight forwarder. "Substantive requirements" below means the Decision's own stated obligations and consequences (running to the Commission, Member States, and the named manufacturers/pools) plus the mechanisms (premium, derogation, exemption) that shape LCV market outcomes a workspace may observe.*

**1. Annual Commission calculation duty.** FACT: "In accordance with Regulation (EU) No 510/2011, the Commission is required to calculate each year the average specific emissions of CO 2 and the specific emissions target for each manufacturer of light commercial vehicles in the Union." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2016/2320, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32016D2320

**2. 75% calculation methodology.** FACT: "Pursuant to Article 4 of Regulation (EU) No 510/2011 the average specific emissions of manufacturers for 2015 are calculated in accordance with the third paragraph of that Article and take into account 75 % of the manufacturer's new light commercial vehicles registered in that year." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2016/2320, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32016D2320

**3. Member State data submission.** FACT: "All Member States submitted the 2015 data the Commission in accordance with Article 8(2) of Regulation (EU) No 510/2011." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2016/2320, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32016D2320

**4. Manufacturer error-notification deadline.** FACT: "Manufacturers were asked to verify the data and to notify the Commission of any errors within three months of receipt of the notification." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2016/2320, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32016D2320

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this deadline ran from the Commission to individual manufacturers in 2016 and has already lapsed; it does not create a recurring or forward-looking duty for a freight-forwarding workspace.

**5. Confirmation-by-default for non-responding manufacturers.** FACT: "For the remaining 39 manufacturers that did not notify any errors in the datasets or respond otherwise, the provisional data and provisional calculations of the average specific emissions and the specific emissions targets should be confirmed." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2016/2320, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32016D2320

**6. Operative confirmation/amendment of manufacturer and pool values (Article 1).** FACT: "The values relating to the performance of manufacturers, as confirmed or amended for each manufacturer of light commercial vehicles and for each pool of manufacturers of light commercial vehicles in respect of the 2015 calendar year in accordance with Article 8(6) of Regulation (EU) No 510/2011, are specified in the Annex to this Decision." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2016/2320, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32016D2320

*Operational implication:* a workspace tracking a specific manufacturer's or pool's 2015 CO2 performance can rely on this Decision's own Annex as the confirmed record, subject to the reserved-revision caveat in Section 6.

**7. Addressee designation (Article 2).** FACT: "This Decision is addressed to the following individual manufacturers and pools formed in accordance with Article 7 of Regulation (EU) No 510/2011" *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2016/2320, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32016D2320

**8. Compliance determination test.** FACT: "a manufacturer should be considered as compliant with its specific emissions target referred to in Article 4 of that Regulation where the average emissions indicated in this Decision are lower than the specific emissions target, expressed as a negative distance to target." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2016/2320, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32016D2320

**9. Excess emission premium consequence.** FACT: "Where the average emissions exceed the specific emissions target, an excess emission premium are to be imposed, unless the manufacturer concerned benefits from an exemption from that target or is a member of a pool and the pool complies with its specific emissions target." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2016/2320, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32016D2320

*Operational implication:* a manufacturer's excess emission premium liability is a cost the manufacturer bears directly under Regulation (EU) No 510/2011; whether and how it is reflected in the purchase or lease price of a specific LCV model is a commercial question this Decision's own text does not address.

**10. Small-volume manufacturer derogation.** FACT: "‘D’ means that a derogation relating to a small volume manufacturer has been granted in accordance with Article 11(3) of Regulation (EU) No 510/2011 with effect for the calendar year 2015." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2016/2320, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32016D2320

**11. De minimis exemption.** FACT: "‘DMD’ means that a de minimis exemption applies in accordance with Article 2(4) of Regulation (EU) No 510/2011, i.e. a manufacturer which together with all its connected undertakings was responsible for fewer than 1 000 new registered vehicles in 2015 does not have to meet a specific emissions target." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2016/2320, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32016D2320

**12. Volkswagen pool hold.** FACT: "As a consequence the values for the Volkswagen pool and its members (Audi AG, Dr Ing. h.c.F. Porsche AG, Quattro GmbH, Seat SA, Skoda Auto A.S. and Volkswagen AG) cannot be confirmed or amended." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2016/2320, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32016D2320

**13. Commission's reserved right to revise.** FACT: "The Commission reserves the right to revise the performance of a manufacturer as confirmed or amended by this Decision, should the relevant national authorities confirm the existence of irregularities in the CO 2 emission values used for the purpose of determining the manufacturer's compliance with the specific emissions target." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2016/2320, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32016D2320

No exceptions are stated in Articles 1 and 2.

No scope limits are stated in Articles 1 and 2.

Obligations surveyed: 15; workspace-adjacent: 8; extracted as FACT: 13.

# 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

FACT: "On 17 May 2016, the Commission published the provisional data and notified 60 manufacturers of the provisional calculations of their average specific emissions of CO 2 in 2015 and their specific emissions targets." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2016/2320, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32016D2320

FACT: "21 manufacturers submitted notifications of errors." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2016/2320, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32016D2320

FACT: "For the remaining 39 manufacturers that did not notify any errors in the datasets or respond otherwise, the provisional data and provisional calculations of the average specific emissions and the specific emissions targets should be confirmed." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2016/2320, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32016D2320

FACT: "‘P’ means that the manufacturer is a member of a pool (listed in Table 2) formed in accordance with Article 7 of Regulation (EU) No 510/2011 and the pooling agreement is valid for the calendar year 2015." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2016/2320, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32016D2320

*Operational implication:* of the 60 manufacturers originally notified, 21 disputed their provisional figures and 39 had their provisional figures confirmed by default; the Annex's own "P" pool-membership code identifies which manufacturers' figures were calculated jointly with a pool rather than individually, which affects how a single vehicle model's compliance status should be read.

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

FACT: "All Member States submitted the 2015 data the Commission in accordance with Article 8(2) of Regulation (EU) No 510/2011." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2016/2320, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32016D2320

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this reporting obligation runs from Member States to the Commission; it does not create a registration or reporting duty for a freight-forwarding workspace, carrier, or logistics intermediary.

# 11. Operational System Requirements

*Analytical inference:* this Decision's own text does not call for the workspace to operate any reporting, monitoring, or registration system; the only system-shaped mechanism in this record (Member State data submission to the Commission) is a government-to-Commission channel with no private-party analogue stated.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

FACT: "‘D’ means that a derogation relating to a small volume manufacturer has been granted in accordance with Article 11(3) of Regulation (EU) No 510/2011 with effect for the calendar year 2015." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2016/2320, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32016D2320

FACT: "‘DMD’ means that a de minimis exemption applies in accordance with Article 2(4) of Regulation (EU) No 510/2011, i.e. a manufacturer which together with all its connected undertakings was responsible for fewer than 1 000 new registered vehicles in 2015 does not have to meet a specific emissions target." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2016/2320, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32016D2320

FACT: "As a consequence the values for the Volkswagen pool and its members (Audi AG, Dr Ing. h.c.F. Porsche AG, Quattro GmbH, Seat SA, Skoda Auto A.S. and Volkswagen AG) cannot be confirmed or amended." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2016/2320, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32016D2320

*Operational implication:* three edge cases sit outside the ordinary confirm-or-amend outcome: a small-volume manufacturer may be derogated entirely (item 10 above), a manufacturer under the 1,000-vehicle de minimis threshold need not meet any target at all (item 11 above), and the Volkswagen pool's own 2015 figures remain neither confirmed nor amended pending further clarification (item 12 above).

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

*No content for this section: this record's captured pool contains only the instrument text of Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2016/2320 and its own explanatory Annex; no adjacent industry research, comparative program, or alternative body is discussed in the captured source.*

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 3 November 2015: Volkswagen Group made a public statement regarding irregularities found in determining type-approval CO2 levels for some of its vehicles.
- 17 May 2016: The Commission published the provisional 2015 data and notified 60 manufacturers of their provisional average specific emissions and targets.
- 16 December 2016: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2016/2320 adopted, confirming or amending the 2015 calendar year's average specific emissions and specific emissions targets for light commercial vehicle manufacturers and pools.

*Source for timeline entries: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2016/2320, EUR-Lex (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32016D2320).*

metadata.why_matters: It closes one annual CO2-compliance cycle for the LCV manufacturers named in its own Article 2, including which manufacturers face an excess emission premium, which qualify for a small-volume derogation or de minimis exemption, and which (the Volkswagen pool) remain unresolved.

metadata.cost_mechanism: Excess emission premium imposed on a manufacturer whose average specific emissions exceed its specific emissions target, unless the manufacturer benefits from an exemption from that target or is a member of a compliant pool.

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks The Waste and Emissions Trading Act 2003 (Commencement No.1) (England) Order 2004, a UK statutory instrument that brings specified sections of the Waste and Emissions Trading Act 2003 into force in England, establishing when the Act's landfill allowance allocation scheme and its monitoring-authority provisions take legal effect.

FACT: "The Waste and Emissions Trading Act 2003 (Commencement No.1) (England) Order 2004" *Source: The Waste and Emissions Trading Act 2003 (Commencement No.1) (England) Order 2004, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2004/3181

FACT: "This Order may be cited as the Waste and Emissions Trading Act 2003 (Commencement No.1) (England) Order 2004." *Source: The Waste and Emissions Trading Act 2003 (Commencement No.1) (England) Order 2004, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2004/3181

*Analytical inference:* this Order's own substance is confined to bringing specific sections of the parent Act into force on specific dates; it creates no new substantive duty beyond commencing provisions the parent Act itself already states.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the duties this Order commences run to "allocating authorities" (the Secretary of State, for England) and "waste disposal authorities" (local government bodies responsible for municipal waste collection and disposal) under the Waste and Emissions Trading Act 2003's landfill allowance scheme. The captured text states no duty running to a freight forwarder, carrier, customs broker, or other private logistics intermediary.

FACT: "The Secretary of State is the allocating authority for England (section 24(1)(a) of the Act)." *Source: The Waste and Emissions Trading Act 2003 (Commencement No.1) (England) Order 2004, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2004/3181

*Operational implication:* a freight-forwarding workspace does not itself hold biodegradable municipal waste landfill allowances and is not named as a duty-holder anywhere in this Order or the sections of the Act it commences; relevance to the workspace, if any, is limited to general awareness of the UK's municipal waste and landfill regulatory landscape.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

*Analytical inference:* both commencement dates this Order sets (3rd December 2004 for sections 4, 5 and 10(1); 1st April 2005 for sections 9 and 10(2)) are long past as of this record's capture, and the Order itself is a closed, historical commencement instrument. There is no immediate action item for the workspace.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the compliance chain this Order commences runs from the Secretary of State (the allocating authority for England) to waste disposal authorities (section 9(1)) and from those authorities' own appointed monitoring authorities (section 10). None of the captured text places a freight-forwarding workspace anywhere in that chain.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: "The Secretary of State, in exercise of the powers conferred upon her by section 40(2)(a) of the Waste and Emissions Trading Act 2003( 1 ) hereby make the following Order:" *Source: The Waste and Emissions Trading Act 2003 (Commencement No.1) (England) Order 2004, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2004/3181

*Per the workspace's reading:* this Order is made under section 40(2)(a) of the parent Waste and Emissions Trading Act 2003; it is a commencement instrument, not an amendment to that Act's own substantive terms.

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

*No content for this section: this record's own two commencement dates (3rd December 2004 and 1st April 2005) are both already historical as of this record's capture, and the captured source states no further pending guidance or regulatory event.*

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does this Order create a direct regulatory obligation on a freight-forwarding workspace?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* No. Every obligation stated in the captured text runs to an allocating authority or a waste disposal authority, both government bodies, not to a private freight forwarder, carrier, or logistics intermediary.

**Q2: Is a freight-forwarding workspace itself a "waste disposal authority" under this scheme?**

*Analytical inference:* No, unless a specific workspace happens to also hold that statutory local-government role, which the captured text gives no indication of for any named party.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: this Order and the sections of the parent Act it commences state obligations running to government bodies (the Secretary of State as allocating authority for England, and local waste disposal authorities), not to a freight-forwarding workspace. "Substantive requirements" below means those government-to-government obligations as stated in the captured text; none is workspace-adjacent.*

**1. Two-stage commencement.** FACT: "As respects England— (a) sections 4, 5 and 10(1) of the Waste and Emissions Trading Act 2003 shall come into force on the day after the day on which this Order is made; and (b) sections 9 and 10(2) of the Waste and Emissions Trading Act 2003 shall come into force on 1st April 2005." *Source: The Waste and Emissions Trading Act 2003 (Commencement No.1) (England) Order 2004, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2004/3181

**2. Commencement dates restated in the Explanatory Note.** FACT: "As respects England only, this Order brings sections 4, 5 and 10(1) of the Waste and Emissions Act 2003 (“the Act”) into force on 3rd December 2004, and sections 9 and 10(2) of the Act into force on 1st April 2005." *Source: The Waste and Emissions Trading Act 2003 (Commencement No.1) (England) Order 2004, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2004/3181

**3. Section 4(1) allocation duty.** FACT: "An allocating authority must make an allocation among waste disposal authorities in its area for each scheme year that is a target year, and for each other scheme year for which an amount has been specified under section 2 of the Act for its area (section 4(1))." *Source: The Waste and Emissions Trading Act 2003 (Commencement No.1) (England) Order 2004, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2004/3181

**4. Section 4(3) and (4) publication duty.** FACT: "Allocations must be made before the beginning of the year to which they relate, and as soon as an authority has made an allocation it must publish a statement detailing what allowances have been allocated to each waste disposal authority (section 4(3) and (4))." *Source: The Waste and Emissions Trading Act 2003 (Commencement No.1) (England) Order 2004, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2004/3181

**5. Section 24(1)(a) designation of the allocating authority for England.** FACT: "The Secretary of State is the allocating authority for England (section 24(1)(a) of the Act)." *Source: The Waste and Emissions Trading Act 2003 (Commencement No.1) (England) Order 2004, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2004/3181

**6. Section 5(1) alteration power.** FACT: "Section 5 of the Act enables an allocating authority to alter an allocation under section 4 at any time (section 5(1))." *Source: The Waste and Emissions Trading Act 2003 (Commencement No.1) (England) Order 2004, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2004/3181

**7. Section 5(4) publication-on-alteration duty.** FACT: "As soon as an authority has altered an allocation again it must publish a statement detailing what allowances have been allocated to each waste disposal authority (section 5(4))." *Source: The Waste and Emissions Trading Act 2003 (Commencement No.1) (England) Order 2004, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2004/3181

**8. Section 9(1) landfill-allowance compliance duty.** FACT: "section 9 of the Act places a duty on each waste disposal authority in the allocating authority’s area to secure that the amount of biodegradable waste sent to landfills in that year by the waste disposal authority does not exceed the amount authorised by the landfill allowances available to that authority (section 9(1))." *Source: The Waste and Emissions Trading Act 2003 (Commencement No.1) (England) Order 2004, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2004/3181

**9. Section 9(2) to (4) penalty consequence.** FACT: "A waste disposal authority that fails to comply with this duty is liable to a penalty (section 9(2)) and in certain circumstances to supplementary penalties as well (section 9(3) and (4))." *Source: The Waste and Emissions Trading Act 2003 (Commencement No.1) (England) Order 2004, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2004/3181

**10. Section 10(1) monitoring-authority appointment duty.** FACT: "Allocating authorities must by regulations appoint a person to be the monitoring authority for its area (section 10(1))." *Source: The Waste and Emissions Trading Act 2003 (Commencement No.1) (England) Order 2004, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2004/3181

**11. Section 10(2) monitoring-authority duties.** FACT: "Any person so appointed is subject to the duties set out in section 10(2) of the Act." *Source: The Waste and Emissions Trading Act 2003 (Commencement No.1) (England) Order 2004, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2004/3181

*Legal Confirmation Required:* every "must"/"shall" duty quoted in the eleven items above runs to an allocating authority or a waste disposal authority under the Waste and Emissions Trading Act 2003; none is stated to run to, or to require action of, a freight-forwarding workspace, carrier, or logistics intermediary.

No exceptions are stated in Articles 1 and 2 of this Order.

No scope limits are stated in Articles 1 and 2 of this Order.

Obligations surveyed: 11; workspace-adjacent: 0; extracted as FACT: 11.

# 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*No content for this section: this instrument concerns municipal biodegradable waste landfill allowances administered by government waste disposal authorities; it states no product-specific, vehicle-specific, or shipment-specific compliance status.*

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

FACT: "Allocations must be made before the beginning of the year to which they relate, and as soon as an authority has made an allocation it must publish a statement detailing what allowances have been allocated to each waste disposal authority (section 4(3) and (4))." *Source: The Waste and Emissions Trading Act 2003 (Commencement No.1) (England) Order 2004, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2004/3181

FACT: "As soon as an authority has altered an allocation again it must publish a statement detailing what allowances have been allocated to each waste disposal authority (section 5(4))." *Source: The Waste and Emissions Trading Act 2003 (Commencement No.1) (England) Order 2004, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2004/3181

*Legal Confirmation Required:* both publication duties run from an allocating authority to the waste disposal authorities in its area; neither creates a registration or reporting duty for a freight-forwarding workspace.

# 11. Operational System Requirements

FACT: "Section 10 of the Act concerns monitoring authorities." *Source: The Waste and Emissions Trading Act 2003 (Commencement No.1) (England) Order 2004, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2004/3181

FACT: "Allocating authorities must by regulations appoint a person to be the monitoring authority for its area (section 10(1))." *Source: The Waste and Emissions Trading Act 2003 (Commencement No.1) (England) Order 2004, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2004/3181

*Operational implication:* the only "system" this Order requires is each allocating authority's own appointment of a monitoring authority for its area; this is a government-to-government administrative requirement with no operational system requirement stated for a private freight-forwarding workspace.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

*No content for this section: the captured source states no exemption, derogation, or edge case beyond the two-stage commencement already recorded in Section 8.*

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

*No content for this section: the captured pool contains only the Order's own instrument text and Explanatory Note, plus legislation.gov.uk navigation furniture; no adjacent industry research, comparative program, or alternative body is discussed.*

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 2004: Enacted (legislation.gov.uk identifier year).
- 2nd December 2004: The Order was made by the Secretary of State.
- 3rd December 2004: Sections 4, 5 and 10(1) of the Waste and Emissions Trading Act 2003 come into force in England.
- 1st April 2005: Sections 9 and 10(2) of the Waste and Emissions Trading Act 2003 come into force in England.

*Source for timeline entries: The Waste and Emissions Trading Act 2003 (Commencement No.1) (England) Order 2004, legislation.gov.uk (https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2004/3181).*

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks Commission Regulation (EU) No 837/2010, which amends the Annex to Commission Regulation (EC) No 1418/2007 -- the EU's country-by-country control list governing which categories of non-hazardous waste may be exported from the Union for recovery to specific non-OECD countries. This 2010 amendment updates the entries for Andorra, China, Croatia and India, and inserts a new entry for Liberia.

FACT: "The Commission has also received further information relating to Andorra, China, Croatia and India." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 837/2010, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32010R0837

*Operational implication:* a freight forwarder arranging the export of scrap metal, waste plastics, or other recovery-bound waste from an EU Member State to any of these five countries must check the current version of this Annex before booking the shipment; this record documents the 2010 update, not necessarily the current live text.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "The Annex to Regulation (EC) No 1418/2007 is amended in accordance with the Annex to this Regulation." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 837/2010, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32010R0837

*Operational implication:* this Regulation itself creates no new export duty; it swaps in an updated Annex under the parent framework, Regulation (EC) No 1013/2006 on shipments of waste. A freight forwarder handling a waste-for-recovery export to Andorra, China, Croatia, India, or Liberia is directly affected by which waste categories that Annex lists for the destination country.

FACT: "Having regard to Regulation (EC) No 1013/2006 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 14 June 2006 on shipments of waste ( 1 ) , and in particular the third subparagraph of Article 37(2) thereof," *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 837/2010, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32010R0837

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

*Analytical inference:* this Regulation entered into force and became applicable in 2010 (Section 14); there is no immediate action item as of this record's capture. The recurring action item for any workspace with ongoing waste-export operations is to verify, at booking time, that the specific waste category and destination country combination is still listed as exportable under the CURRENT version of Regulation (EC) No 1418/2007's Annex, since this 2010 amendment is itself one of a series of updates to that Annex.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the underlying export-control obligation runs under Regulation (EC) No 1013/2006's own Article 36 (whether an export is "prohibited"); this 2010 Regulation only updates the Annex list that operationalises which non-OECD destination/waste combinations are not prohibited. A freight forwarder acting as the exporter's or notifier's logistics agent sits downstream of this list: it does not create the underlying legal test, but a shipment booked outside what the Annex allows would not have valid legal cover under Regulation (EC) No 1013/2006's own control-procedure regime.

FACT: "The Commission has received a reply from Liberia to its written requests seeking confirmation in writing that certain waste which is listed in Annex III or IIIA to Regulation (EC) No 1013/2006 and the export of which is not prohibited under its Article 36 may be exported from the European Union for recovery in that country and requesting an indication from it as to which control procedure, if any, would be followed there." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 837/2010, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32010R0837

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

*Per the workspace's reading:* Regulation (EC) No 1013/2006 (on shipments of waste) is the controlling parent instrument; Regulation (EC) No 1418/2007 is the implementing Annex-list regulation this 2010 Regulation amends. This record's own corpus does not include the full text of either parent instrument beyond the citation above; a workspace confirming a specific country/waste combination should consult the CURRENT consolidated Annex on EUR-Lex directly.

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

*No content for this section: this record's own captured text states no further pending amendment, review clause, or anticipated guidance beyond the single 2010 update it documents.*

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does this Regulation apply to a freight forwarder directly, or only to the exporter/notifier?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the captured text names no duty-holder class by role (exporter, notifier, carrier, or freight forwarder); it states only which waste/country combinations are, and are not, within the Annex's control-procedure list. Whether a specific freight-forwarding workspace bears its own compliance duty as opposed to acting on an exporter's instructions is a fact-specific question under Regulation (EC) No 1013/2006 outside this brief's scope.

**Q2: Does the Liberia entry allow the export of any recovery-bound waste, or only a specific category?**

FACT: "After the entry for Lebanon, the following entry is inserted: ‘ Liberia (a) (b) (c) (d) B3020’" *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 837/2010, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32010R0837

*Operational implication:* the Liberia entry is limited to waste code B3020 only, unlike the Andorra/Croatia/India entries, which cover all waste listed in Annex III of Regulation (EC) No 1013/2006.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: this Regulation is an Annex-amending instrument, not a new duty-creating regulation in its own right. "Substantive requirements" below means the Regulation's own operative provisions plus the country-by-country waste-category entries the amended Annex now states.*

**1. Annex amendment operative provision.** FACT: "The Annex to Regulation (EC) No 1418/2007 is amended in accordance with the Annex to this Regulation." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 837/2010, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32010R0837

**2. Entry into force.** FACT: "This Regulation shall enter into force on the fourteenth day following its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union ." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 837/2010, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32010R0837

**3. Applicability from entry into force.** FACT: "It shall apply from the date of entry into force." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 837/2010, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32010R0837

**4. Binding and directly applicable in all Member States.** FACT: "This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 837/2010, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32010R0837

**5. Liberia export-eligibility confirmation.** FACT: "The Commission has received a reply from Liberia to its written requests seeking confirmation in writing that certain waste which is listed in Annex III or IIIA to Regulation (EC) No 1013/2006 and the export of which is not prohibited under its Article 36 may be exported from the European Union for recovery in that country and requesting an indication from it as to which control procedure, if any, would be followed there." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 837/2010, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32010R0837

**6. Andorra entry (all Annex III waste).** FACT: "The entry for Andorra is replaced by the following: ‘ Andorra (a) (b) (c) (d) all waste listed in Annex III of Regulation (EC) No 1013/2006’" *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 837/2010, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32010R0837

**7. Croatia entry (all Annex III waste).** FACT: "The entry for Croatia is replaced by the following: ‘ Croatia (a) (b) (c) (d) all waste listed in Annex III of Regulation (EC) No 1013/2006’" *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 837/2010, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32010R0837

**8. India entry (all Annex III waste).** FACT: "The entry for India is replaced by the following: ‘ India (a) (b) (c) (d) all waste listed in Annex III of Regulation (EC) No 1013/2006’" *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 837/2010, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32010R0837

**9. Liberia entry (limited to B3020 only).** FACT: "After the entry for Lebanon, the following entry is inserted: ‘ Liberia (a) (b) (c) (d) B3020’" *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 837/2010, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32010R0837

**10. China precious-metals carve-out.** FACT: "The entry for China ... From B1010: Precious metals (except for gold, platinum)" is stated in the amended Annex's China entry. *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 837/2010, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32010R0837

*Legal Confirmation Required:* items 1 through 10 above state a country-by-country and waste-category-specific export-eligibility list; none names a freight forwarder as its own duty-holder, and a workspace with a live export booking should confirm the CURRENT Annex text rather than rely on this 2010 record alone.

No phase-in is stated in Articles 1 and 2.

No scope limits are stated in Articles 1 and 2.

Obligations surveyed: 11; workspace-adjacent: 10; extracted as FACT: 10.

# 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

FACT: "The entry for Andorra is replaced by the following: ‘ Andorra (a) (b) (c) (d) all waste listed in Annex III of Regulation (EC) No 1013/2006’" *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 837/2010, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32010R0837

FACT: "The entry for Croatia is replaced by the following: ‘ Croatia (a) (b) (c) (d) all waste listed in Annex III of Regulation (EC) No 1013/2006’" *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 837/2010, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32010R0837

FACT: "The entry for India is replaced by the following: ‘ India (a) (b) (c) (d) all waste listed in Annex III of Regulation (EC) No 1013/2006’" *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 837/2010, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32010R0837

FACT: "After the entry for Lebanon, the following entry is inserted: ‘ Liberia (a) (b) (c) (d) B3020’" *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 837/2010, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32010R0837

*Operational implication:* Andorra, Croatia, and India each carry an identical status ("all waste listed in Annex III of Regulation (EC) No 1013/2006" is exportable for recovery), while Liberia's status is narrower (only waste code B3020), and China's status (Section 12) carries its own detailed, waste-code-by-waste-code list with named carve-outs.

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

*No content for this section: the captured text describes a Commission-to-country consultation and confirmation process (the Liberia recital, Section 4) that precedes an Annex update; it states no registration or reporting duty running to a freight-forwarding workspace.*

# 11. Operational System Requirements

*Analytical inference:* the only "system" implied by this record is the workspace's own need to check the current Annex to Regulation (EC) No 1418/2007 against the specific waste code and destination country of each recovery-bound export before booking; the captured text itself states no technical or reporting system requirement.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

FACT: "The entry for China is replaced by the following: ... From B1010: Precious metals (except for gold, platinum)" *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 837/2010, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32010R0837

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks The Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme (Amendment) Regulations 2014, a UK statutory instrument implementing EU Regulation No 421/2014 into the Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme Regulations 2012. It amends the monitoring, reporting, and allowance-surrender duties that apply to UK administered aircraft operators under the EU Emissions Trading Scheme's aviation provisions, and introduces temporary derogations for non-EEA and small-emitter flights for the 2013 to 2016 scheme years.

FACT: "These Regulations may be cited as the Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme (Amendment) Regulations 2014 and come into force on 22nd December 2014." *Source: The Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme (Amendment) Regulations 2014, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2014/3125

FACT: "Made 20th November 2014 Laid before Parliament 26th November 2014 Coming into force 22nd December 2014" *Source: The Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme (Amendment) Regulations 2014, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2014/3125

*Operational implication:* an aircraft operator administered by the UK -- including one carrying air cargo -- is directly within scope of these amendments; a freight-forwarding workspace that itself operates aircraft, or whose principal is a UK administered operator, should read this record as governing its own aviation-emissions compliance calendar.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "This regulation applies to a UK administered operator (“B”) who commences aviation activities other than excluded aviation activities during the scheme years 2015 (“the 2015 activities”) or 2016 (“the 2016 activities”)." *Source: The Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme (Amendment) Regulations 2014, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2014/3125

*Operational implication:* the duty-holder class is explicitly "a UK administered operator" -- an aircraft operator, which may include a freight-forwarding business that itself operates aircraft for air cargo, rather than every logistics intermediary generically.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

*Analytical inference:* every commencement, application, and surrender date in this record (22nd December 2014 through 30th April 2015 and the ongoing annual 30th April cycle) is long past as of this record's capture. The recurring, still-live obligation pattern is the annual allowance-surrender cycle (Section 8, item 14): a UK administered operator must surrender allowances by 30th April each year for the preceding scheme year's emissions.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

*Legal Confirmation Required:* every duty in this record runs to "a UK administered operator" (labelled A, B, or C across the amended regulations) reporting to "the regulator" under the Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme Regulations 2012. A freight-forwarding workspace that books cargo space on an aircraft, without itself being the UK administered operator for that aircraft, is not itself the duty-holder; a workspace that IS such an operator (for example, operating its own charter aircraft for high-value or time-sensitive cargo) sits squarely inside this chain.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

*Per the workspace's reading:* this instrument implements EU Regulation No 421/2014 (amending Directive 2003/87/EC) into the UK's Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme Regulations 2012, which in turn consolidated and replaced the earlier Aviation Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme Regulations 2010. This record's own corpus does not include the full text of the 2012 Regulations or the EU Regulation beyond the citations and Explanatory Note quoted in this record; a workspace with a live compliance question should consult the current consolidated 2012 Regulations directly.

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

*No content for this section: this record's own corpus documents a single 2014 amendment whose own commencement, application, and surrender dates are all historical as of this record's capture; the captured text states no further pending guidance or regulatory event.*

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does this instrument create a direct duty on a freight-forwarding workspace that does not itself operate aircraft?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* No duty in the captured text is stated to run to a party other than "a UK administered operator." Whether a specific freight-forwarding workspace qualifies as a UK administered operator (as opposed to a customer of one) is a fact-specific question outside this brief's scope.

**Q2: Does the small-emitter or excluded-activity exemption remove a UK administered operator from the scheme entirely?**

FACT: "“exempt non-commercial air transport operator” means a UK administered operator who— (a) is a non-commercial air transport operator; and (b) has annual reportable emissions of less than 1,000 tonnes;" *Source: The Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme (Amendment) Regulations 2014, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2014/3125

*Analytical inference:* No. An exempt non-commercial air transport operator (annual reportable emissions under 1,000 tonnes) and an operator carrying only excluded aviation activities are relieved of specific duties (monitoring, reporting, verification, or surrender) for specific scheme years, not removed from the scheme's definitions or its notification duty entirely.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: every duty below runs to "a UK administered operator" reporting to "the regulator" under the amended Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme Regulations 2012; none is stated to run to a freight forwarder generically, only to an operator of aircraft administered by the UK.*

**1. Citation and commencement.** FACT: "These Regulations may be cited as the Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme (Amendment) Regulations 2014 and come into force on 22nd December 2014." *Source: The Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme (Amendment) Regulations 2014, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2014/3125

**2. Exempt non-commercial air transport operator definition.** FACT: "“exempt non-commercial air transport operator” means a UK administered operator who— (a) is a non-commercial air transport operator; and (b) has annual reportable emissions of less than 1,000 tonnes;" *Source: The Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme (Amendment) Regulations 2014, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2014/3125

**3. Monitoring-plan duty scope (2015/2016 commencers).** FACT: "This regulation applies to a UK administered operator (“B”) who commences aviation activities other than excluded aviation activities during the scheme years 2015 (“the 2015 activities”) or 2016 (“the 2016 activities”)." *Source: The Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme (Amendment) Regulations 2014, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2014/3125

**4. Monitoring-plan application duty.** FACT: "Subject to paragraphs (3) to (7), B must apply to the regulator for a monitoring plan by the application date." *Source: The Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme (Amendment) Regulations 2014, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2014/3125

**5. Six-week fallback deadline where the commencement date could not be foreseen.** FACT: "no later than 6 weeks after the date on which the 2015 activities or the 2016 activities commence" *Source: The Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme (Amendment) Regulations 2014, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2014/3125

**6. Application-date definition (2015 activities).** FACT: "in the case of 2015 activities, the later of 31st January 2015 or the date which is 4 months before the date on which the 2015 activities are due to commence" *Source: The Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme (Amendment) Regulations 2014, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2014/3125

**7. Monitoring-plan exemption for 2015/2016-only commencers under the pre-existing regulation 32.** FACT: "This regulation does not apply to a UK administered operator who commences aviation activities during the scheme years 2015 or 2016." *Source: The Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme (Amendment) Regulations 2014, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2014/3125

**8. Notify-the-regulator duty where no monitoring plan is required.** FACT: "B must, by the relevant date, notify the regulator in accordance with paragraph (2)." *Source: The Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme (Amendment) Regulations 2014, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2014/3125

**9. Monitoring-duty exemption for excluded aviation emissions.** FACT: "The obligation to monitor aviation emissions does not apply in respect of excluded aviation emissions for the scheme years 2015 and 2016." *Source: The Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme (Amendment) Regulations 2014, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2014/3125

**10. Report-verification exemption for small emitters.** FACT: "The obligation for the report to be verified in accordance with the Verification Regulation does not apply where— (a) A has annual reportable emissions of less than 25,000 tonnes; and (b) A has determined its emissions using the small emitters tool approved under the Small Emitters Tool Regulation and populated with data by Eurocontrol." *Source: The Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme (Amendment) Regulations 2014, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2014/3125

**11. 2013 scheme-year verified-report deadline.** FACT: "The verified report for the scheme year 2013 must be submitted to the regulator by 31st March 2015." *Source: The Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme (Amendment) Regulations 2014, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2014/3125

**12. Revocation savings clause (no civil penalty for the revoked regulation 42).** FACT: "no civil penalty applies to P in respect of the non-compliance." *Source: The Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme (Amendment) Regulations 2014, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2014/3125

*Legal Confirmation Required:* item 12 is a SAVINGS clause following the revocation of the prior regulation 42 -- it states that no civil penalty applies for a pre-revocation non-compliance with the now-revoked provision. It is not itself a live, currently-enforceable penalty and must not be read as one; the genuinely live penalty for late or non-reporting is item 15 below.

**13. Allowance surrender duty for 2013 and 2014 emissions.** FACT: "by 30th April 2015, a UK administered operator (“A”) must surrender a number of allowances or aviation allowances equal to the sum of A’s annual reportable emissions in the scheme years 2013 and 2014." *Source: The Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme (Amendment) Regulations 2014, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2014/3125

**14. Ongoing annual allowance surrender duty from 2015 onward.** FACT: "for each scheme year beginning with 2015, A must, by the following 30th April, surrender a number of allowances or aviation allowances equal to A’s annual reportable emissions in that scheme year." *Source: The Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme (Amendment) Regulations 2014, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2014/3125

**15. Civil penalty for late or non-reporting of aviation emissions.** FACT: "a UK administered operator (“A”) is liable to the civil penalties in paragraph (2) where A fails to report (or to report on time) aviation emissions" *Source: The Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme (Amendment) Regulations 2014, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2014/3125

**16. Special reserve allocation cap.** FACT: "An allocation of allowances to be issued from the special reserve under Article 3f of the Directive in any trading period must not exceed 1,000,000 allowances." *Source: The Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme (Amendment) Regulations 2014, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2014/3125

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

FACT: "Subject to paragraphs (3) to (7), B must apply to the regulator for a monitoring plan by the application date." *Source: The Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme (Amendment) Regulations 2014, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2014/3125

FACT: "B must, by the relevant date, notify the regulator in accordance with paragraph (2)." *Source: The Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme (Amendment) Regulations 2014, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2014/3125

FACT: "The verified report for the scheme year 2013 must be submitted to the regulator by 31st March 2015." *Source: The Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme (Amendment) Regulations 2014, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2014/3125

*Operational implication:* a UK administered operator has three distinct registration-shaped touchpoints with the regulator across the scheme year lifecycle: applying for a monitoring plan (or notifying the regulator that none is required), then submitting a verified emissions report by the applicable deadline.

# 11. Operational System Requirements

FACT: "The obligation for the report to be verified in accordance with the Verification Regulation does not apply where— (a) A has annual reportable emissions of less than 25,000 tonnes; and (b) A has determined its emissions using the small emitters tool approved under the Small Emitters Tool Regulation and populated with data by Eurocontrol." *Source: The Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme (Amendment) Regulations 2014, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2014/3125

*Operational implication:* an operator below the 25,000-tonne annual reportable emissions threshold may use the Small Emitters Tool (approved under Commission Regulation (EU) No 606/2010 and populated with Eurocontrol fuel-consumption data) instead of a fully verified report, which is a materially lighter operational system requirement than full third-party verification.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

FACT: "“exempt non-commercial air transport operator” means a UK administered operator who— (a) is a non-commercial air transport operator; and (b) has annual reportable emissions of less than 1,000 tonnes;" *Source: The Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme (Amendment) Regulations 2014, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2014/3125

*Operational implication:* three separate exemption/edge-case mechanisms apply, on different tests: the sub-1,000-tonne non-commercial operator exemption (by emissions volume), the excluded-aviation-emissions exemption (by route, e.g. flights to or from outside the EEA), and the 2015/2016-only-commencer exemption from the pre-existing monitoring-plan duty (by operator start date).

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2022/601, which recognises the "Better Biomass" voluntary scheme as demonstrating compliance with the sustainability and greenhouse gas emissions-saving criteria of Directive (EU) 2018/2001 (the Renewable Energy Directive) for biofuels, bioliquids, biomass fuels, and related renewable and recycled carbon fuels used in transport.

FACT: "Member States may use voluntary schemes." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2022/601, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0601

FACT: "Done at Brussels, 8 April 2022." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2022/601, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0601

FACT: "The request to the Commission for recognition under Article 30(4) of the Directive from the ‘Better Biomass’ voluntary scheme was first submitted to the Commission on 19 December 2020." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2022/601, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0601

*Operational implication:* a freight forwarder handling biofuel, bioliquid, or biomass fuel cargo, or purchasing such fuels for its own transport operations, can rely on a supplier's "Better Biomass" certification as evidence of sustainability compliance without needing separately-produced proof, to the extent this recognition decision covers.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "Where an economic operator provides proof of or data on compliance with the sustainability and greenhouse gas emissions saving criteria, obtained in accordance with a voluntary scheme that has been recognised by the Commission, to the extent covered by the recognition decision, a Member State should not require the supplier to provide further evidence." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2022/601, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0601

*Operational implication:* this is the direct workspace-facing consequence of the recognition: once a supplier's fuel consignment is certified under a Commission-recognised voluntary scheme like "Better Biomass," a Member State authority should not demand further sustainability evidence from that supplier for the elements the recognition covers.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

*Analytical inference:* this Decision was adopted in 2022 and is a closed recognition act; there is no immediate action item for the workspace as of this record's capture. The recurring item to track is the recognition's own 5-year validity window and the reassessment the Commission has already flagged (Section 6).

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the Decision's own duties (annual reporting, auditing standards, notifying the Commission of scheme changes) run from the "Better Biomass" scheme itself to the Commission, not from a freight-forwarding workspace to either party. A workspace's own position in this chain is as a beneficiary of the recognition (Section 2) when dealing with a supplier certified under the scheme, not as a direct duty-holder under this Decision.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

*Per the workspace's reading:* Directive (EU) 2018/2001 (the Renewable Energy Directive) is the controlling parent instrument; this Decision is a Commission recognition act under its Article 30(4). This record's own corpus does not include the full text of the Directive beyond the citations quoted in this record; a workspace with a live sustainability-criteria question should consult Directive (EU) 2018/2001 directly.

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

FACT: "This assessment does not take into account the forthcoming implementing act to be adopted in accordance with article 30(8) of Directive (EU) 2018/2001, on rules to verify sustainability and greenhouse gas emissions saving criteria and low indirect land-use change-risk criteria as well as the delegated acts to be adopted in accordance with article 28(5) of Directive (EU) 2018/2001. The 'Better Biomass' voluntary scheme will therefore be re-assessed when such implementing and delegated acts will be adopted." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2022/601, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0601

*Operational implication:* a workspace relying on this recognition should expect the Commission to re-assess (and potentially adjust the terms of) the "Better Biomass" recognition once the Article 30(8) implementing act and the Article 28(5) delegated acts are adopted; this record's own corpus does not state a date for either.

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does this Decision itself create a compliance duty on a freight-forwarding workspace?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* No. Every duty this Decision states (annual reporting, independent auditing, notification of scheme changes) runs to the "Better Biomass" scheme's own administrators, reporting to the Commission. The workspace-facing consequence is a right, not a duty: reduced evidentiary burden when dealing with a certified supplier (Section 2).

**Q2: How long does this recognition remain valid?**

FACT: "The Decision is valid for a period of 5 years after it enters into force." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2022/601, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0601

*Analytical inference:* the recognition's own stated 5-year validity period is counted from its own entry into force (Section 14), subject to earlier repeal under Article 3's own conditions (Section 8, items 5 to 7) or reassessment under Section 6; the captured text does not itself state the resulting expiry date, only the 5-year duration.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: this Decision is a scheme-recognition act. Its own operative duties run to the "Better Biomass" scheme's administrators reporting to the Commission, not to a freight-forwarding workspace; the workspace-facing consequence is the evidentiary benefit described in Section 2.*

**1. Sustainability-criteria compliance element (Article 1(a)).** FACT: "compliance of the consignments of biofuels, bioliquids and biomass fuels with the sustainability criteria laid down in Article 29(2) to (5) and (10) of Directive (EU) 2018/2001" *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2022/601, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0601

**2. Database-entry compliance element (Article 1(b)).** FACT: "compliance of economic operators with the obligation to enter accurate information into the Union or national database on renewable fuels and recycled carbon fuels used in transport in accordance with Article 28(4) of Directive (EU) 2018/2001" *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2022/601, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0601

**3. Five-year validity period (Article 2).** FACT: "The Decision is valid for a period of 5 years after it enters into force." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2022/601, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0601

**4. Notify-the-Commission-without-delay duty (Article 2).** FACT: "In the event that the contents of the scheme, as submitted for recognition to the Commission on 2 July 2021, change in a way that might affect the basis of this Decision, such changes shall be notified to the Commission without delay." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2022/601, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0601

**5. Repeal condition: failure to implement important elements or severe structural breach (Article 3(a)).** FACT: "if it has been clearly demonstrated that the scheme has not implemented elements considered to be important for this Decision or if severe and structural breach of those elements has occurred" *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2022/601, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0601

**6. Repeal condition: failure to submit annual reports (Article 3(b)).** FACT: "if the scheme fails to submit annual reports to the Commission pursuant to Article 30(5) of Directive (EU) 2018/2001" *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2022/601, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0601

**7. Repeal condition: failure to implement independent-auditing standards (Article 3(c)).** FACT: "if the scheme fails to implement standards of independent auditing and other requirements specified in implementing acts referred to in Article 30(8) of Directive (EU) 2018/2001 or improvements to other elements of the scheme considered to be important for a continued recognition" *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2022/601, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0601

**8. Entry into force (Article 4).** FACT: "This Decision shall enter into force on the day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union ." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2022/601, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0601

**9. Member States may use voluntary schemes (Recital 3).** FACT: "Member States may use voluntary schemes." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2022/601, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0601

**10. No further evidence required from a certified supplier (Recital 4).** FACT: "Where an economic operator provides proof of or data on compliance with the sustainability and greenhouse gas emissions saving criteria, obtained in accordance with a voluntary scheme that has been recognised by the Commission, to the extent covered by the recognition decision, a Member State should not require the supplier to provide further evidence." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2022/601, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0601

No exceptions are stated in Articles 1 to 4.

No scope limits are stated in Articles 1 to 4.

Obligations surveyed: 10; workspace-adjacent: 7; extracted as FACT: 10.

# 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*No content for this section: this Decision recognises a certification SCHEME, not a specific product, vehicle, or fuel batch; product-level compliance status is a matter for the scheme's own audits, which this record's corpus does not include.*

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

FACT: "if the scheme fails to submit annual reports to the Commission pursuant to Article 30(5) of Directive (EU) 2018/2001" *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2022/601, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0601

FACT: "In the event that the contents of the scheme, as submitted for recognition to the Commission on 2 July 2021, change in a way that might affect the basis of this Decision, such changes shall be notified to the Commission without delay." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2022/601, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0601

*Legal Confirmation Required:* both reporting duties run from the "Better Biomass" scheme's own administrators to the Commission; neither creates a registration or reporting duty for a freight-forwarding workspace using fuel certified under the scheme.

# 11. Operational System Requirements

*Analytical inference:* this Decision states no technical or reporting system requirement for a freight-forwarding workspace; the only system-shaped mechanism (the Union or national database entry duty, Article 1(b)) runs to "economic operators" within the scheme's own audited chain of custody, a category this record's corpus does not confirm includes a freight forwarder acting only as a logistics intermediary.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

FACT: "if it has been clearly demonstrated that the scheme has not implemented elements considered to be important for this Decision or if severe and structural breach of those elements has occurred" *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2022/601, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0601

*Operational implication:* the one edge case a workspace relying on "Better Biomass" certification should track is repeal risk: the Commission may withdraw this recognition under any of the three Article 3 conditions (Section 8, items 5 to 7), at which point a supplier's certification under the scheme would no longer carry the evidentiary benefit described in Section 2.

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

*No content for this section: the captured pool contains only this Decision's own instrument text; no adjacent industry research, comparative voluntary scheme, or alternative certification body is discussed (beyond the general statement in Recital 3 that Member States may use voluntary schemes generally).*

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 19 December 2020: The "Better Biomass" scheme's initial request for recognition was first submitted to the Commission.
- 2 July 2021: The scheme's resubmission, addressing issues the Commission had identified, was submitted.
- 8 April 2022: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2022/601 adopted at Brussels, recognising the "Better Biomass" voluntary scheme.
- The day following publication in the Official Journal of the European Union: the Decision enters into force.

*Source for timeline entries: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2022/601, EUR-Lex (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0601).*
