entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks the Control of Pollution Act 1974 (UK, 1974 c. 40), a 51-year-old statute covering waste disposal, water pollution, noise, and atmospheric pollution, as captured from its own consolidated, revised text on legislation.gov.uk. It exists to give a freight-forwarding workspace with UK depot, warehouse, or terminal operations a single place to see which of this Act's original provisions are still in force today, since most of the Act has since been repealed and replaced by later legislation.

FACT: "An Act to make further provision with respect to waste disposal, water pollution, noise, atmospheric pollution and public health; and for purposes connected with the matters aforesaid." *Source: Control of Pollution Act 1974, preamble. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1974/40

*Analytical inference:* the Act's own preamble describes its original 1974 scope; Section 2 below explains which parts of that original scope remain operative law today.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "Act applies to Great Britain with exceptions, see s. 109." *Source: Control of Pollution Act 1974, Extent Information note. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1974/40

*Per the workspace's reading:* the great majority of the Act's original waste-disposal-licensing (Part I), noise-abatement-zone, and much of its water-pollution machinery has since been repealed and superseded, chiefly by the Environmental Protection Act 1990; the captured text confirms this directly for each provision (see Section 12). The provisions this brief finds still operative and relevant to a freight-forwarding workspace are Sections 60 and 61 (control of noise on construction sites), which apply across England, Wales, and Scotland to a person who erects, constructs, alters, repairs, or demolishes buildings or structures, or carries out engineering construction, road works, or dredging -- work a workspace would undertake if it builds, alters, or demolishes a depot, warehouse, or terminal facility.

FACT: "This section applies to works of the following description, that is to say" *Source: Control of Pollution Act 1974, s. 60(1). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1974/40

*Operational implication:* a workspace planning to erect, alter, repair, or demolish premises, or to carry out engineering construction or road/dredging works connected with its UK operations, falls within the class of person Section 60 addresses.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

*Analytical inference:* the captured text states no compliance deadline currently due on a workspace that is not itself undertaking qualifying construction, alteration, or demolition works. The recurring, workspace-triggered obligation described in Section 8 (a local authority's 28-day decision window on a consent application) applies only once the workspace itself initiates such works.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

FACT: "This Act shall come into force on such day as the Secretary of State may by order appoint" *Source: Control of Pollution Act 1974, s. 109(2). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1974/40

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the Act was brought into force in stages, provision by provision, by a long series of commencement orders rather than on a single date; this capture does not itself state which commencement order brought Sections 60 and 61 into force, so a workspace relying on the precise commencement date of those two sections for a specific compliance question should confirm it directly against the relevant commencement Statutory Instrument rather than this summary.

FACT: "This Act, except sections F287 ... F288 ... 101 and this section, does not extend to Northern Ireland." *Source: Control of Pollution Act 1974, s. 109(3). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1974/40

*Analytical inference:* a workspace with only Northern Ireland UK operations sits outside this Act's compliance chain entirely, save the two named exceptions; a workspace with England, Wales, or Scotland operations sits inside it via Sections 60 and 61.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

*No content for this section as of 2026-09-13: the captured source is the primary legislative text itself (legislation.gov.uk's own consolidated, revised rendering of the Act); no separate authoritative guidance document accompanies this capture.*

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

*No content for this section as of 2026-09-13: the export for this item carries no forward_events, and the captured text states no anticipated guidance or pending regulatory event.*

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does merely operating a freight-forwarding business in Great Britain create an obligation under this Act?**

*Analytical inference:* No. The captured text's surviving substantive duties (Section 8) attach to a person carrying out specified construction, alteration, demolition, or engineering works -- not to freight-forwarding activity itself.

**Q2: When would this workspace first face a duty under this Act?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the duty is triggered the moment the workspace begins, or gives notice that it intends to begin, works of the kind Section 60(1) describes (see Section 8); whether a specific planned works project at a specific UK premises falls within that description is a fact-specific question a workspace should confirm with the relevant local authority and, where the answer is unclear, with counsel.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: most of this Act's original substantive machinery (waste-disposal licensing, noise abatement zones, most of the water-pollution/trade-effluent provisions) has been repealed since 1974; see Section 12 for the repeal history. This section surveys the Act's original obligation-shaped provisions and reports which of them the captured text still shows as operative and workspace-adjacent.*

**1. Local authority notice power over construction-site works.** FACT: "the local authority may serve a notice imposing requirements as to the way in which the works are to be carried out" *Source: Control of Pollution Act 1974, s. 60(2). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1974/40

*Operational implication:* once a workspace's premises works fall within Section 60(1), the local authority may serve a notice fixing how the works are carried out (permitted plant, hours, noise levels), before the workspace begins.

**2. Offence for breaching a Section 60 notice.** FACT: "If a person on whom a notice is served under this section without reasonable excuse contravenes any requirement of the notice he shall be guilty of an offence against this Part of this Act." *Source: Control of Pollution Act 1974, s. 60(8). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1974/40

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this capture does not itself state the specific fine or penalty scale attached to a Section 60(8) offence (see the penalty note below); a workspace served with such a notice should confirm the current penalty scale directly.

**3. Prior-consent alternative.** FACT: "A person who intends to carry out works to which the preceding section applies may apply to the local authority for a consent under this section." *Source: Control of Pollution Act 1974, s. 61(1). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1974/40

*Operational implication:* instead of waiting for a Section 60 notice, a workspace may pre-empt it by applying for consent before starting works, giving it more control over the terms it will operate under.

**4. 28-day local-authority decision window.** FACT: "The local authority shall inform the applicant of its decision on the application within twenty-eight days from receipt of the application" *Source: Control of Pollution Act 1974, s. 61(6). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1974/40

*Operational implication:* a workspace that applies for consent should build a 28-day local-authority response window into its own works schedule.

**5. Offence for breaching consent conditions.** FACT: "any person who knowingly carries out the works, or permits the works to be carried out, in contravention of any conditions attached to a consent under this section shall be guilty of an offence against this Part of this Act." *Source: Control of Pollution Act 1974, s. 61(5). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1974/40

*Legal Confirmation Required:* as with the Section 60(8) offence, this capture does not itself state the specific penalty scale for a Section 61(5) offence.

**6. Duty to notify a third-party works-executor of the consent.** FACT: "it shall be the duty of the applicant to take all reasonable steps to bring the consent to the notice of that other person; and if he fails to comply with this subsection he shall be guilty of an offence against this Part of this Act." *Source: Control of Pollution Act 1974, s. 61(10). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1974/40

*Operational implication:* where the workspace applies for consent but a contractor actually carries out the works, the workspace (as applicant) must take reasonable steps to pass the consent's terms on to that contractor.

**Qualification accounting.** No phase-in is stated in Sections 60 and 61. No exceptions are stated in Sections 60 and 61. No scope limits are stated in Sections 60 and 61.

Obligations surveyed: 8; workspace-adjacent: 6; extracted as FACT: 6.

# 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*No content for this section as of 2026-09-13: this instrument's surviving obligations (Sections 60 and 61) are procedural (works notices and consent applications), not tied to any product, commodity, or equipment specification.*

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

FACT: "An application under this section shall contain particulars of— (a) the works, and the method by which they are to be carried out; and (b) the steps proposed to be taken to minimise noise resulting from the works." *Source: Control of Pollution Act 1974, s. 61(3). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1974/40

*Operational implication:* a workspace choosing the Section 61 consent route must submit these two particulars with its application; there is no separate registration or licensing regime under this Act beyond this application.

# 11. Operational System Requirements

*Note: because the surviving obligations are procedural rather than technical, "operational system requirements" here means the coordination steps a workspace should build into its own premises-works planning process.*

FACT: "the application under this section must be made at the same time as, or later than, the request for the approval under building regulations" *Source: Control of Pollution Act 1974, s. 61(2). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1974/40

*Operational implication:* a workspace already coordinating a UK building-regulations (or, in Scotland, building-warrant) application for premises works should time its Section 61 noise-consent application to be no earlier than that building-control application.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

*Note: this section records which of the Act's original provisions the captured text shows as repealed, and therefore no longer a current workspace obligation.*

FACT: "S. 1 repealed (1.5.1994) by Environmental Protection Act 1990" *Source: Control of Pollution Act 1974, Textual Amendments note to s. 1. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1974/40

FACT: "S. 3 repealed (1.5.1994 save in respect of specified activities, as to which in force as provided by S.I. 1994/1096" *Source: Control of Pollution Act 1974, Textual Amendments note to s. 3. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1974/40

*Analytical inference:* Sections 1 to 3 (the original waste-disposal-arrangements, waste-disposal-plans, and unlicensed-waste-disposal-prohibition provisions) are repealed; a workspace's current waste-disposal-licensing obligations in Great Britain run under the Environmental Protection Act 1990's own regime, not this Act.

FACT: "S. 17 repealed (1.4.2015 for S.) by Environmental Protection Act 1990" *Source: Control of Pollution Act 1974, Textual Amendments note to s. 17. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1974/40

FACT: "penalty for the offence (which shall not exceed, on summary conviction, a fine of £400 and, on conviction on indictment, imprisonment for a term of two years and a fine)." *Source: Control of Pollution Act 1974, s. 17(1)(e). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1974/40

*Analytical inference:* Section 17's special-waste regulation-making power, and the penalty it authorised (a fine of up to £400 and, on indictment, up to two years' imprisonment for a contravention of special-waste regulations), is historic; hazardous-waste handling in Great Britain is now governed by later regulations made under the Environmental Protection Act 1990's own regime, not by this Act.

FACT: "Ss. 63-67 repealed (S.) (30.6.2014) by Regulatory Reform (Scotland) Act 2014" *Source: Control of Pollution Act 1974, Textual Amendments note to ss. 63-67. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1974/40

FACT: "Sch. 1 omitted (E.W.) (1.10.2015) by virtue of Deregulation Act 2015" *Source: Control of Pollution Act 1974, Textual Amendments note to Sch. 1. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1974/40

*Analytical inference:* the Act's noise-abatement-zone scheme (Sections 63 to 67 and Schedule 1) no longer applies anywhere in Great Britain; it was repealed for Scotland in 2014 and its Schedule 1 was separately omitted for England and Wales in 2015 (Section 14, Confirmed Regulatory Timeline).

FACT: "S. 58 wholly repealed (1.4.1996) by 1995 c. 25" *Source: Control of Pollution Act 1974, Textual Amendments note to s. 58. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1974/40

*Analytical inference:* Sections 58 to 59A (summary court proceedings for noise nuisance) are also repealed; a workspace facing a noise complaint today proceeds under the surviving Sections 60-61 machinery described in Section 8, not under these repealed summary-proceedings sections.

FACT: "This section does not apply to Scotland." *Source: Control of Pollution Act 1974, s. 14(12). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1974/40

*Analytical inference:* Section 14 (trade-effluent discharge to public sewers) also does not apply to Scotland even where it retains any effect in England and Wales, illustrating that this Act's surviving provisions can differ by jurisdiction within Great Britain; Sections 60 and 61, by contrast, apply uniformly across England, Wales, and Scotland.

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

FACT: "by Environmental Protection Act 1990 (c. 43, SIF 46:4)" *Source: Control of Pollution Act 1974, Textual Amendments note to s. 1. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1974/40

*Analytical inference:* the Environmental Protection Act 1990 is the successor waste-management-licensing regime a workspace should consult for current waste-disposal duties, since this Act's own Part I waste provisions no longer apply.

FACT: "in Scotland a [ F183 building warrant ] under [ F184 section 9 ] of the Building (Scotland) Act" *Source: Control of Pollution Act 1974, s. 61(2). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1974/40

*Analytical inference:* the Building (Scotland) Act 2003's building-warrant regime is the parallel Scottish building-control process a workspace's Section 61(2) timing obligation is keyed to, for premises works carried out in Scotland.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

The Act's own enacting words carry the bracketed date [31st July 1974], confirming the date of Royal Assent below.

- 31 July 1974: Control of Pollution Act 1974 receives Royal Assent, per the Act's own enacting bracket date.
- 1 May 1994: Section 1 (waste disposal arrangements) and, save specified activities, Section 3 (unlicensed waste disposal) are repealed by the Environmental Protection Act 1990.
- 1 April 1996: Sections 58 to 59A (summary noise proceedings) are repealed.
- 30 June 2014: Sections 63 to 67 (noise abatement zones) are repealed in Scotland by the Regulatory Reform (Scotland) Act 2014.
- 1 April 2015: Section 17 (special waste) and the remaining saved parts of Section 3 are repealed in Scotland.
- 1 October 2015: Schedule 1 (noise abatement zones) is omitted for England and Wales by the Deregulation Act 2015.

*Source for timeline entries: Control of Pollution Act 1974, legislation.gov.uk consolidated text and its own Textual Amendments notes to ss. 1, 3, 17, 58-59A, 63-67 and Sch. 1 (https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1974/40).*

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks the CRC Energy Efficiency Scheme (Allocation of Allowances for Payment) Regulations 2013 (UK SI 2013/3103), a Treasury statutory instrument that governs how a CRC scheme participant requests, pays for, and is issued carbon allowances. It exists to give a freight-forwarding workspace that is a CRC account holder (typically a large energy user, such as one running significant UK warehouse, depot, or cold-storage operations) a single place to see the request, payment, pricing, and consequence rules this instrument sets.

FACT: "Made 5th December 2013" *Source: The CRC Energy Efficiency Scheme (Allocation of Allowances for Payment) Regulations 2013, made/laid/in-force header. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/3103

FACT: "Laid before the House of Commons 9th December 2013" *Source: same header. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/3103

*Analytical inference:* this is a UK statutory instrument (secondary legislation) made under powers in the Finance Act 2008, not an Act of Parliament in its own right; Section 4 below identifies the specific enabling provision.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "PART 1 U.K. INTRODUCTORY" *Source: The CRC Energy Efficiency Scheme (Allocation of Allowances for Payment) Regulations 2013, Part 1 heading and its own U.K. extent marker. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/3103

*Per the workspace's reading:* legislation.gov.uk's own extent marker on every Part of this instrument is "U.K.", meaning the Regulations apply United-Kingdom-wide (England, Wales, Scotland, and Northern Ireland); the captured text states no narrower extent for any Part. A workspace that is a CRC scheme "account holder" (a defined term carrying the same meaning as under the CRC Energy Efficiency Scheme Order 2013) is directly bound by the request, payment, and consequence rules in Section 8.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

*Analytical inference:* the captured text states no compliance deadline currently due independent of the workspace's own CRC participation calendar. The recurring deadlines this instrument sets (Section 8: application-period timing, payment-period timing, and the special-allocation payment window) recur every scheme year for a workspace that is an active account holder.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

FACT: "The Treasury make the following Regulations in exercise of the powers conferred by section 21(1), (2) and (3) of the Finance Act 2008" *Source: enabling-powers recital. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/3103

FACT: "These Regulations may be cited as the CRC Energy Efficiency Scheme (Allocation of Allowances for Payment) Regulations 2013 and come into force on 1st February 2014." *Source: reg. 1. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/3103

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this instrument administers the mechanics of allowance allocation and payment; it does not itself define who must register as a CRC account holder (that eligibility test sits in the CRC Energy Efficiency Scheme Order 2013). Whether a specific workspace's UK energy use crosses the CRC participation threshold is a fact-specific question outside this brief's scope.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: "These Regulations revoke and replace the CRC Energy Efficiency Scheme (Allocation of Allowances for Payment) Regulations 2012" *Source: Explanatory Note (not part of the Regulations). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/3103

*Analytical inference:* the Explanatory Note is the instrument's own accompanying guidance; it confirms this 2013 instrument supersedes the 2012 version of the same Regulations (see Section 12 for the saving provision covering first-phase special allocations).

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

*No content for this section as of 2026-09-13: the export for this item carries no forward_events, and the captured text states no anticipated guidance or pending regulatory event beyond the amendment history already recorded in Section 14.*

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does this instrument itself determine whether the workspace must participate in the CRC scheme?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* No. It governs allocation and payment mechanics for an existing account holder; CRC participation eligibility is set by the CRC Energy Efficiency Scheme Order 2013, not by this instrument.

**Q2: What happens if the workspace, as an account holder, is late paying for allocated allowances?**

*Analytical inference:* Section 8 states the Environment Agency's remedy is to allocate only up to the value actually paid (regulation 6(2)) and, for a special allocation tied to an enforcement notice or civil penalty notice, a fixed short payment window (regulation 7(5)); Section 8 also states the consequence for excess allowances the workspace has already sold or dealt in.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: this instrument's obligations run to a CRC scheme "account holder" (the defined duty-holder), which a freight-forwarding workspace becomes only if it is an active CRC participant; the obligations below all attach to that role.*

**1. Duty to submit an allocation request.** FACT: "An account holder of a compliance account wishing to be allocated allowances must submit a request to the Environment Agency." *Source: reg. 5(1). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/3103

*Operational implication:* an account holder does not receive allowances automatically; it must actively request them.

**2. Request timing restriction.** FACT: "An account holder may only make a request to be allocated allowances" *Source: reg. 5(2). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/3103

*Operational implication:* outside a special allocation, a request may only be made during the defined application period for that allocation type, so a workspace must track its own scheme-year calendar.

**3. Request content requirement.** FACT: "A request for allowances to be allocated must specify" *Source: reg. 5(3). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/3103

*Operational implication:* the request must state the number of allowances sought, the account holder's name, the registry account to receive them, and whether it is a standard or special allocation.

**4. Allowance pricing.** FACT: "in relation to 2014 is £12" *Source: reg. 7(2)(a) (special allocation price table). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/3103

FACT: "in the compliance application period in 2019 is £18.30." *Source: reg. 7(1)(g) (as inserted, standard allocation price table). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/3103

*Operational implication:* the price per allowance is fixed by year and by allocation type/period in a table running from 2014 through 2019 (the full year-by-year series is captured in this record's requirement_trajectory metadata); a workspace budgeting for CRC compliance should use the rate for its own allocation year and period, not a flat assumption.

**5. Special-allocation payment deadline.** FACT: "no later than the date specified in the enforcement notice or within 5 working days of the effective date of a notice of a civil penalty" *Source: reg. 7(5)(a). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/3103

*Operational implication:* where a special allocation follows an enforcement notice or civil-penalty notice, the workspace has a short, fixed window (5 working days, or a longer date if one is stated in the notice) to pay for the allowances required.

**6. Fee for allocation.** FACT: "The Environment Agency may require the payment of a fee by an account holder who requests the allocation of allowances." *Source: reg. 8(1). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/3103

FACT: "Where an account holder has not paid, in full, a fee notified under this regulation, any outstanding amount is recoverable as a civil debt due to the Environment Agency." *Source: reg. 8(4). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/3103

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the fee amount itself is not fixed by this instrument (it may not exceed the Environment Agency's reasonable costs, per regulation 8(2)) and must be separately notified before the allocation; this capture does not state a current fee figure.

**7. Payment method rules.** FACT: "made by electronic transfer from an account with a credit institution" *Source: reg. 9(2)(a). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/3103

FACT: "Payments under these Regulations may not be made by credit card." *Source: reg. 9(2A). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/3103

*Operational implication:* a workspace must pay by electronic transfer in sterling from a credit institution account; a corporate credit card is not an accepted payment method.

**8. Consequence for excess allowances.** FACT: "Paragraph (1) does not apply where an account holder has sold or otherwise dealt in any excess allowances." *Source: reg. 10(2). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/3103

FACT: "may require that account holder to pay the amount which would have been payable for the allowances determined in accordance with regulation 7 multiplied by the number of excess allowances" *Source: reg. 10(3)(b). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/3103

FACT: "each member of a group is jointly and severally liable to comply with such a demand" *Source: reg. 10(4). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/3103

*Legal Confirmation Required:* if the Environment Agency issues an account holder more allowances than were validly requested and paid for, ordinarily it must cancel the excess; but where the account holder has already sold or dealt in the excess allowances, cancellation does not apply and the account holder must instead pay the regulation-7 price for the excess, recoverable as a civil debt on demand, with every member of a group jointly and severally liable.

**Qualification accounting.** Per-year trajectory: CAPTURED (see metadata.requirement_trajectory: the special-allocation price rises from £12 in 2014 to £18.30 in 2019, the last year this capture's price table states). Exceptions and carve-outs: CAPTURED below (Section 8 obligation 9, the fees exception in regulation 11). Scope limits: CAPTURED above (obligation 8, regulation 10(2)'s "does not apply" carve-out for already-sold excess allowances).

**9. Financial provision (routing of sums, with a fee exception).** FACT: "Except for any sums received by the Environment Agency by way of fees pursuant to regulation 8, any sums received by the Environment Agency under or by virtue of these Regulations shall be paid to the Secretary of State." *Source: reg. 11(1). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/3103

*Analytical inference:* this obligation runs from the Environment Agency to the Secretary of State (and onward to the Consolidated Fund, per regulation 11(2)); it is not itself a duty on the account holder, but it confirms fees under regulation 8 are the one sum category the Environment Agency retains rather than passing on.

Obligations surveyed: 10; workspace-adjacent: 8; extracted as FACT: 14.

# 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*No content for this section as of 2026-09-13: this instrument's obligations are financial and procedural (allocation requests, payment, pricing), not tied to any product, commodity, or equipment specification.*

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

FACT: "A request for allowances to be allocated must specify" *Source: reg. 5(3). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/3103

*Operational implication:* the Section 8 request-content requirement (number of allowances, account holder name, registry account, standard/special) is itself the closest thing to a registration or reporting duty this instrument imposes on an account holder; there is no separate registration regime beyond the underlying CRC account-holder status this instrument assumes.

# 11. Operational System Requirements

FACT: "Payments under these Regulations must be made into a bank account nominated" *Source: reg. 9(1). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/3103

*Operational implication:* a workspace should confirm the currently-nominated payment bank account (the Secretary of State's, for allowances; the Environment Agency's, for fees) before each payment cycle, since the nominated account is not itself fixed in this text.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

FACT: "Subject to paragraphs (2) and (3), the 2012 Regulations and the 2013 Amendment Regulations are revoked." *Source: reg. 13(1). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/3103

*Analytical inference:* the predecessor 2012 Regulations are revoked, but continue to have effect for special allocations relating to the scheme's first phase under the CRC Energy Efficiency Scheme Order 2010 (regulation 13(2)) -- a workspace with an outstanding first-phase special allocation should check the 2012 Regulations, not only this 2013 instrument.

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

FACT: "a notice of a civil penalty requiring allowances to be acquired for the purposes of articles 74(4)(b) and 77(2)(a)(i) of the 2013 Order" *Source: reg. 2(1) definition of "special allocation". https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/3103

*Analytical inference:* the CRC Energy Efficiency Scheme Order 2013 is the parallel instrument that actually defines and quantifies civil penalties and enforcement notices; this Regulations instrument only administers the resulting allowance-purchase mechanics once such a notice is issued, so a workspace facing an enforcement or civil-penalty notice should consult the 2013 Order directly for the penalty itself.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 5th December 2013: The Regulations are made and signed by two Lords Commissioners of Her Majesty's Treasury.
- 9th December 2013: The Regulations are laid before the House of Commons.
- 1st February 2014: The Regulations come into force (regulation 1).
- 1st April 2014: Regulation 7(2) (special-allocation pricing) is substituted by the 2014 amendment regulations (S.I. 2014/495).
- 1st April 2015: Regulations 7(A1), 7(1), 9(2A), and 9(6) are amended by the 2014 No. 2 amendment regulations (S.I. 2014/3262).
- 31st March 2017: Regulation 3 and regulation 7's pricing provisions are further amended by the amendment regulations (S.I. 2017/211), extending the price table through 2019.

The instrument's own Textual Amendments notes record these three amendment dates in numeric form: "Reg. 7(2) substituted (1.4.2014) by The CRC Energy Efficiency Scheme (Allocation of Allowances for Payment) (Amendment)"; "inserted (1.4.2015) by The CRC Energy Efficiency Scheme (Allocation of Allowances for Payment) (Amendment) (No. 2) Regul"; and "substituted (31.3.2017) by The CRC Energy Efficiency Scheme (Allocation of Allowances for Payment) (Amendment) Regulatio".

*Source for timeline entries: The CRC Energy Efficiency Scheme (Allocation of Allowances for Payment) Regulations 2013, its own made/laid/in-force header and Textual Amendments notes to regs. 3, 7 and 9 (https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/3103).*

# 15. Sources

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2024/1884 of 10 July 2024, a short, two-article EU instrument that amends one annex (Annex III) of an earlier Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2020/2126, adjusting the total quantities of cancelled EU ETS allowances two Member States (Malta and Sweden) may count toward their own compliance under the Effort Sharing Regulation (EU) 2018/842. It exists to give a workspace tracking EU climate-policy flexibility mechanisms a single place to see what this Decision changes and who it binds.

FACT: "COMMISSION IMPLEMENTING DECISION (EU) 2024/1884 of 10 July 2024 amending Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2020/2126 as regards the total quantities of cancelled EU ETS allowances that may be taken into account for certain Member States’ compliance under Regulation (EU) 2018/842 of the European Parliament and of the Council" *Source: instrument title. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024D1884

*Analytical inference:* the title itself states this Decision's full scope: it is a narrow, technical amendment to a compliance-accounting annex, not a new substantive climate obligation.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "Total quantities following reduction of EU ETS allowances that may be taken into account for certain Member States’ compliance under Article 9 of Regulation (EU) 2018/842" *Source: Annex, Annex III heading. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024D1884

*Per the workspace's reading:* this Decision's own operative text runs Commission-to-Member-State: it adjusts a compliance-accounting figure for two named Member States (Malta and Sweden) under the Effort Sharing Regulation. This capture states no obligation, deadline, or penalty running to a private freight-forwarding workspace; it is tracked here as macro-level EU climate-policy context (the Effort Sharing Regulation's own ETS-flexibility mechanism), not as a workspace compliance duty.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

*No content for this section as of 2026-09-13: the captured text states no action item running to a private party; both notification deadlines it references (Section 8) have already passed.*

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

FACT: "This Decision shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union" *Source: Article 2. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024D1884

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this Decision's addressees are the Member States whose Annex III figures it amends (Malta and Sweden); this capture states no addressee clause naming a private party, and a freight-forwarding workspace sits outside this Decision's own compliance chain entirely.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

*No content for this section as of 2026-09-13: the captured source is the operative legal instrument itself, published in the Official Journal; no separate authoritative guidance document accompanies this capture.*

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

*No content for this section as of 2026-09-13: the export for this item carries no forward_events, and the captured text states no anticipated guidance or pending regulatory event -- both notification deadlines it references are already in the past relative to this Decision's own 10 July 2024 adoption date.*

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does this Decision create an obligation running to a freight-forwarding workspace?**

*Analytical inference:* No. Every obligation-shaped statement in the captured text (Section 8) runs between a Member State and the European Commission under the Effort Sharing Regulation's own ETS-flexibility mechanism.

**Q2: Why does this narrow accounting amendment matter to the workspace at all?**

*Analytical inference:* it is one data point in the Effort Sharing Regulation's own binding annual national emission-reduction targets (Regulation (EU) 2018/842), which is the broader EU climate framework a workspace with EU operations tracks for macro-level regulatory direction, even though this specific instrument imposes no direct duty on it.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: this Decision's own operative provisions and recitals describe obligations and notifications running between Member States and the European Commission, not to a private freight-forwarding workspace. This section surveys those Member-State/Commission-level statements for completeness; none is workspace-adjacent.*

**1. Malta's increased ETS-flexibility percentage.** FACT: "Malta’s maximum percentage of ETS flexibility for the years 2025-2030 was increased from 2 % to 7 %" *Source: recital (3). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024D1884

*Analytical inference:* this is a Member-State-level percentage change to an EU accounting mechanism, not a duty on a private party.

**2. Original 2019 notification basis for Annex III.** FACT: "by 31 December 2019 pursuant to Article 6(3) of Regulation (EU) 2018/842 to the values of" *Source: recital (2). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024D1884

*Analytical inference:* this is background describing how the ORIGINAL Annex III figures (in the 2020 Decision this instrument amends) were calculated; the deadline itself has long since passed and is not a current action item for anyone.

**3. New 2023 notification and Malta/Sweden's confirmed use.** FACT: "some Member States were granted a new opportunity to notify the Commission by 31 December 2023 whether they intended to make use or further use of the ETS flexibility for the period 2025-2030" *Source: recital (3). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024D1884

FACT: "By 31 December 2023, Malta and Sweden notified the Commission of their intended use of this flexibility." *Source: recital (4). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024D1884

*Analytical inference:* this 31 December 2023 notification (also a Member-State-to-Commission deadline, and also already passed) is the direct trigger for this Decision's Annex III amendment; no equivalent notification duty runs to a private party.

**Qualification accounting.** No phase-in is stated in Articles 1 and 2. No exceptions are stated in Articles 1 and 2. No scope limits are stated in Articles 1 and 2.

Obligations surveyed: 3; workspace-adjacent: 0; extracted as FACT: 3.

# 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*No content for this section as of 2026-09-13: this Decision concerns a Member-State emissions-accounting figure, not any product, commodity, or equipment specification.*

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

*No content for this section as of 2026-09-13: the notification duties this Decision describes (Section 8) run from Member States to the European Commission; the captured text states no registration or reporting duty running to a private party.*

# 11. Operational System Requirements

*No content for this section as of 2026-09-13: this Decision imposes no operational or technical system requirement on a private party.*

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

*No content for this section as of 2026-09-13: the captured text states no exemption or edge case running to a private party; Malta's own increased flexibility percentage (Section 8, obligation 1) is a Member-State-level parameter change, not a workspace-facing exemption.*

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

FACT: "Regulation (EU) 2018/842 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 30 May 2018 on binding annual greenhouse gas emission reductions by Member States from 2021 to 2030 contributing to climate action to meet commitments under the Paris Agreement" *Source: recital, citing Regulation (EU) 2018/842. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024D1884

*Analytical inference:* the Effort Sharing Regulation (EU) 2018/842 is the parent instrument this Decision's Annex III amendment implements; a workspace tracking EU climate-policy direction should read that Regulation directly for the binding national targets themselves, since this Decision only adjusts one accounting annex under it.

FACT: "Regulation (EU) 2023/857 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 19 April 2023 amending Regulation (EU) 2018/842" *Source: footnote (3). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024D1884

*Analytical inference:* Regulation (EU) 2023/857 is the amending instrument that raised Malta's flexibility ceiling and created the new 2025-2030 notification window described in Section 8; it is the more substantive instrument to consult for the underlying policy change.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 31 December 2019: Member States notify the Commission of the percentages later used to calculate the original Annex III quantities.

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks Council Decision (EU) 2024/1873 of 24 June 2024, a short EU procedural instrument that sets the European Union's negotiating position for a Joint Committee meeting under the EU-Switzerland Emissions Trading System Linking Agreement, together with the attached draft Joint Committee Decision (technical amendments to Annex II, the Common Operational Procedures (COP), and the Linking Technical Standards (LTS) governing the registry link between the EU ETS and the Swiss ETS). It exists to give a workspace tracking EU-Swiss ETS linking a single place to see what this instrument changes and who it binds.

FACT: "COUNCIL DECISION (EU) 2024/1873 of 24 June 2024 on the position to be taken on behalf of the European Union within the Joint Committee established by the Agreement between the European Union and the Swiss Confederation on the linking of their greenhouse gas emissions trading systems as regards the amendment of Annex II to the Agreement and of the Common Operational Procedures and the Linking Technical Standards" *Source: instrument title. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024D1873

*Analytical inference:* the title states this instrument's full scope: it is the EU's own procedural position-setting Decision for a Joint Committee meeting, attaching a draft technical Decision, not a new substantive obligation on private parties.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "(Text with EEA relevance)" *Source: instrument subtitle marker. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024D1873

FACT: "The target audience of these COP are the EU and Swiss registry support teams." *Source: attached Common Operational Procedures, section 2.2 Addressees. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024D1873

*Per the workspace's reading:* the attached technical Common Operational Procedures state their own target audience explicitly: EU and Swiss REGISTRY SUPPORT TEAMS (i.e. the Swiss registry administrator and the Union central administrator), not private account holders such as aircraft operators or freight forwarders. This capture states no obligation, deadline, or penalty running to a private party; it is tracked here as macro-level EU-Swiss ETS-linking context, since a workspace operating flights or freight covered by the linked EU/Swiss aviation ETS is an indirect beneficiary of the registry link this instrument maintains, not a duty-holder under it.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

*No content for this section as of 2026-09-13: the captured text states no action item running to a private party; every recurring administrator-level duty in Section 8 runs between the Swiss registry administrator and the Union central administrator.*

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

FACT: "This Decision shall enter into force on the date of its adoption." *Source: Article 2 of Council Decision (EU) 2024/1873. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024D1873

FACT: "Done at Luxembourg, 24 June 2024." *Source: signature block. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024D1873

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this Council Decision's own addressee is the EU's Joint Committee delegation, not a private party; the attached draft Joint Committee Decision (once formally adopted, separately from this Council Decision) would bind the EU and Switzerland as Parties to the underlying Agreement, still not a private freight-forwarding workspace directly.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

*No content for this section as of 2026-09-13: the captured source is the operative legal instrument itself, together with its own attached technical annexes; no separate authoritative guidance document accompanies this capture.*

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

FACT: "The position to be taken on behalf of the Union during the seventh meeting of the Joint Committee, or earlier by means of the written procedure pursuant to Article 8(4) of the Rules of Procedure of the Joint Committee, shall be based on the draft Decision of the Joint Committee attached to this Decision." *Source: Article 1 of Council Decision (EU) 2024/1873. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024D1873

*Operational implication:* the attached draft Joint Committee Decision is the pending regulatory event this instrument anticipates; once the Joint Committee formally adopts it (at its seventh meeting or earlier by written procedure), Annex II, the COP, and the LTS take their amended, in-force form. This capture does not state whether or when that adoption occurred.

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does this instrument itself impose an obligation on a freight-forwarding workspace?**

*Analytical inference:* No. Every obligation-shaped statement in the captured text (Section 8) runs between the Swiss registry administrator and the Union central administrator, or between the EU and Switzerland as Parties to the Agreement.

**Q2: Why track a purely procedural, government-to-government instrument like this one?**

*Analytical inference:* because it maintains the technical registry link that lets an aircraft operator covered by both the EU ETS and the Swiss ETS receive its aviation allowances automatically across the linked systems (Section 8, obligation 5); a workspace operating EU-Swiss aviation routes is an indirect beneficiary of the link's continued operation, not a duty-holder under this instrument.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: this instrument's own obligation-shaped statements, and those of its attached Common Operational Procedures, run between the Swiss registry administrator and the Union central administrator (or between the EU and Switzerland as Parties). This section surveys those statements for completeness; none is workspace-adjacent.*

**1. Continuous link-availability duty.** FACT: "the administrators are to take all reasonable steps to ensure that the SSTL, the EUTL and the link are operational 24 hours a day and 7 days a week" *Source: attached Linking Technical Standards summary. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024D1873

*Analytical inference:* this duty runs to the two registry administrators, not to a private account holder.

**2. Security-incident reporting deadline.** FACT: "a report describing the incident (date, cause, impact, remedies) shall be shared between the Swiss registry administrator and the Union central administrator within 24 hours after a security incident is identified as a security breach." *Source: attached Linking Technical Standards summary. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024D1873

*Analytical inference:* a fixed, short reporting window, but again administrator-to-administrator only.

**3. Annual independent security assessment.** FACT: "The Parties shall provide evidence through the Swiss registry administrator and the Union central administrator that an independent security assessment of their systems has been performed in the previous 12 months" *Source: attached Linking Technical Standards summary. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024D1873

*Analytical inference:* a recurring annual duty on the EU and Switzerland as Parties, administered through the two registry administrators.

**4. Duty to suspend the link on suspected compromise.** FACT: "either Party shall immediately inform the other and suspend the link between the SSTL and the EUTL." *Source: attached Common Operational Procedures, Communication Provisions. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024D1873

*Analytical inference:* the closest thing to an enforcement-style consequence in this capture is this administrative suspension of the registry link between the two Parties' systems, never a penalty against a private party (see the penalty_summary note below).

**5. Automatic cross-system allowance transfer for aircraft operators.** FACT: "Aircraft Operators administered by one ETS with obligations on the other ETS and entitled to receive free allowances from that second ETS, will receive free aviation allowances, from the second ETS, by means of the international allocation transaction." *Source: attached Common Operational Procedures. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024D1873

*Operational implication:* this is the one place the captured text names aircraft operators directly; it describes a benefit the linked registries deliver automatically, not a duty the operator itself must perform.

**Qualification accounting.** No phase-in is stated in Sections 3 and 9 of the Common Operational Procedures. No exceptions are stated in Sections 3 and 9 of the Common Operational Procedures. No scope limits are stated in Sections 3 and 9 of the Common Operational Procedures.

Obligations surveyed: 5; workspace-adjacent: 0; extracted as FACT: 5.

# 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*No content for this section as of 2026-09-13: this instrument concerns a registry-linking IT procedure and allowance-accounting mechanism, not any product, commodity, or equipment specification.*

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

*No content for this section as of 2026-09-13: the reporting duties this instrument describes (Section 8, obligations 2-3) run between the Swiss registry administrator and the Union central administrator; the captured text states no registration or reporting duty running to a private party.*

# 11. Operational System Requirements

*No content for this section as of 2026-09-13: the operational and technical system requirements this instrument sets (Section 8) bind the two registry administrators' own IT systems (SSTL, EUTL), not a private party's systems.*

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

*No content for this section as of 2026-09-13: the captured text states no exemption or edge case running to a private party.*

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

FACT: "The Agreement between the European Union and the Swiss Confederation on the linking of their greenhouse gas emissions trading systems" *Source: recital (1). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024D1873

FACT: "The Agreement was concluded by Council Decision (EU) 2018/219" *Source: recital (2). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024D1873

*Analytical inference:* the underlying EU-Switzerland ETS Linking Agreement itself, and its concluding Council Decision (EU) 2018/219, are the substantive instruments a workspace tracking EU-Swiss aviation-ETS scope should read directly; this 2024 Decision only amends the linking agreement's technical registry annexes.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 23 November 2017: The EU-Switzerland ETS Linking Agreement is signed.
- 1 January 2020: The EU-Switzerland ETS Linking Agreement enters into force.
- 24 June 2024: Council Decision (EU) 2024/1873 is adopted at Luxembourg and enters into force the same day.
- 5 July 2024: Council Decision (EU) 2024/1873 is published in the Official Journal.

The captured source's own recitals confirm these two Agreement dates verbatim: the Agreement "was signed on 23 November 2017" and "entered into force on 1 January 2020."

*Source for timeline entries: Council Decision (EU) 2024/1873, its own recitals, footnotes, and Official Journal header (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024D1873).*

# 15. Sources

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks Commission Directive (EU) 2017/2096 of 15 November 2017, which replaces Annex II to the End-of-Life Vehicles Directive 2000/53/EC -- the list of vehicle materials and components exempted from that Directive's ban on lead, mercury, cadmium, and hexavalent chromium. It exists to give a workspace that trades, dismantles, or handles spare parts for end-of-life or older vehicles a single place to see the current exemption table, its vehicle-age cutoffs, and its review/expiry dates.

FACT: "COMMISSION DIRECTIVE (EU) 2017/2096 of 15 November 2017 amending Annex II to Directive 2000/53/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council on end-of life vehicles" *Source: instrument title. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32017L2096

*Analytical inference:* this is a Commission Directive amending one annex of the parent End-of-Life Vehicles Directive; it does not itself restate or change Article 4(2)(a)'s underlying prohibition, only the list of exemptions from it.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "(Text with EEA relevance)" *Source: instrument subtitle marker. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32017L2096

FACT: "This Directive is addressed to the Member States." *Source: Article 4. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32017L2096

*Per the workspace's reading:* as a Directive, this instrument's own addressee is Member States, who must transpose it into national law (Section 8); the substantive Annex II exemption table it sets, once transposed, is what a workspace handling end-of-life vehicles, spare parts, or vehicle recycling in the EEA must actually apply. A workspace's national compliance obligation flows from its own Member State's transposing law, not from this Directive directly.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

*Analytical inference:* the captured text's own Member State transposition deadline (6 June 2018, Section 8) has long since passed; a workspace should confirm its own Member State's current transposing legislation is up to date with this Directive's Annex II, rather than treating the transposition deadline itself as a live action item.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

FACT: "This Directive shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union" *Source: Article 3. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32017L2096

FACT: "Done at Brussels, 15 November 2017." *Source: signature block. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32017L2096

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the underlying prohibition and penalty regime for non-compliant vehicle materials/components is set by each Member State's own national transposition of Directive 2000/53/EC (as amended by this Directive), not stated in this capture; a workspace with a specific compliance question should confirm the current national implementing measure in its own Member State.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

*No content for this section as of 2026-09-13: the captured source is the operative legal instrument itself, together with its own amended Annex II; no separate authoritative guidance document accompanies this capture.*

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

1. FACT: "Member States shall adopt and publish by 6 June 2018 the laws, regulations and administrative provisions necessary to comply with this Directive." *Source: Article 2(1). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32017L2096

*Operational implication:* this transposition deadline (6 June 2018) is now in the past relative to today; it is carried here per the exported forward-event record as the instrument's own stated compliance-deadline event, and cross-referenced in Section 14's timeline as a completed milestone rather than a pending one.

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does this Directive itself impose a duty directly on a workspace?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* No, not directly. As a Directive, it binds Member States to transpose it (Article 2); a workspace's actual compliance duty runs through its own Member State's national implementing law, which this capture does not itself state.

**Q2: Which vehicles does the amended Annex II exemption table apply to?**

*Analytical inference:* the exemption table's own "Scope and expiry date of the exemption" column (Section 8) ties most entries to a vehicle type-approval or market-placement date cutoff (for example, "before 1 January 2019"), so the answer depends on the specific vehicle or spare part's own type-approval date, not a single blanket rule.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: most entries below describe the amended Annex II exemption table (a workspace-facing technical standard, once transposed nationally); two describe the Member-State transposition process itself (not a private-party duty).*

**1. Base prohibition this Annex exempts from.** FACT: "Article 4(2)(a) of Directive 2000/53/EC prohibits the use of lead, mercury, cadmium and hexavalent chromium in materials and components of vehicles put on the market after 1 July 2003." *Source: recital (1). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32017L2096

*Operational implication:* every exemption below is a carve-out from this base prohibition; a material or component not listed in Annex II is not exempt.

**2. General homogeneous-material concentration tolerance.** FACT: "A maximum concentration value up to 0,1 % by weight in homogeneous material for lead, hexavalent chromium and mercury and up to 0,01 % by weight in homogeneous material for cadmium shall be tolerated." *Source: Annex II, introductory tolerance note. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32017L2096

*Operational implication:* trace amounts below these thresholds are not treated as a prohibited "use" at all, separate from the named exemptions below.

**3. Spare-parts exemption for pre-2003 vehicles.** FACT: "Spare parts put on the market after 1 July 2003 which are used for vehicles put on the market before 1 July 2003, except for wheel balance weights, carbon brushes for electric motors and brake linings, shall be exempted from the provisions of Article 4(2)(a) of Directive 2000/53/EC." *Source: Annex II, introductory spare-parts note. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32017L2096

*Operational implication:* a workspace supplying spare parts for pre-2003 vehicles is broadly exempt from the base prohibition, except for the three named part categories, which remain subject to it.

**4. Aluminium-alloy exemption (recycled-content carve-out).** FACT: "Applies to aluminium alloys where lead is not intentionally introduced but is present due to the use of recycled aluminium." *Source: Annex II, entry 2(c) footnote (1a). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32017L2096

*Operational implication:* incidental lead from recycled-aluminium content does not itself disqualify an aluminium-alloy component from this exemption.

**5. Copper-alloy exemption with a set review date.** FACT: "Copper alloys containing up to 4 % lead by weight" *Source: Annex II, entry 3. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32017L2096

FACT: "This exemption shall be reviewed in 2021." *Source: Annex II, footnote to entries marked (1). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32017L2096

*Operational implication:* this exemption's own review date (2021) has passed; a workspace relying on it should confirm whether a later amending Directive has since narrowed or removed it (this capture does not itself state the outcome of that 2021 review).

**6. High-voltage battery exemption with a vehicle-age cutoff.** FACT: "Vehicles type-approved before 1 January 2019 and spare parts for these vehicles" *Source: Annex II, entry 5(a) scope column. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32017L2096

*Operational implication:* this exemption (lead in high-voltage propulsion batteries) only covers vehicles type-approved, and spare parts for vehicles type-approved, before 1 January 2019; a newer vehicle's high-voltage battery is not covered.

FACT: "This exemption shall be reviewed in 2019." *Source: Annex II, footnote to entries marked (3). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32017L2096

FACT: "This exemption shall be reviewed in 2024." *Source: Annex II, footnote to entries marked (2). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32017L2096

*Analytical inference:* other Annex II entries carry their own review dates of 2019 and 2024, distinct from entry 3's 2021 review date above; this capture does not state the outcome of any of these reviews.

**7. Dismantling threshold for certain electronic-component exemptions.** FACT: "Dismantling if, in correlation with entry 10(a), an average threshold of 60 grams per vehicle is exceeded." *Source: Annex II, footnote (5) (also mirrored at footnote (4) for entries 8(a)-8(j)). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32017L2096

*Operational implication:* an end-of-life vehicle dismantler must dismantle and separately treat the named lead-containing electronic components once the average 60-gram-per-vehicle threshold is exceeded, rather than leaving them in the general waste stream.

**8. Member State transposition deadline.** FACT: "Member States shall adopt and publish by 6 June 2018 the laws, regulations and administrative provisions necessary to comply with this Directive." *Source: Article 2(1). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32017L2096

*Analytical inference:* this duty runs to Member States, not to a private workspace directly.

**9. Member State reporting to the Commission.** FACT: "Member States shall communicate to the Commission the text of the main provisions of national law which they adopt in the field covered by this Directive." *Source: Article 2(2). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32017L2096

*Analytical inference:* also a Member-State-to-Commission duty, not a workspace duty.

**Qualification accounting.** Per-year trajectory: CAPTURED (see metadata.requirement_trajectory: the exemption review/expiry dates run 2018 (transposition), 2019 (entry 5(a) vehicle-age cutoff), 2021 (entry 3 review), and 2024 (a further exemption review), each a distinct milestone rather than a single phase-in). Exceptions and carve-outs: CAPTURED above (obligation 3, the wheel-balance-weights/carbon-brushes/brake-linings exception). Scope limits: CAPTURED via the Annex's own "Scope and expiry date of the exemption" table column (Source: Annex II, column heading. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32017L2096), which ties nearly every entry above to a vehicle-age or market-placement cutoff.

Obligations surveyed: 9; workspace-adjacent: 7; extracted as FACT: 13.

# 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*Analytical inference:* the amended Annex II table (Section 8) IS this Directive's own product-specific compliance status list, keyed to specific vehicle materials, components, and type-approval dates; a workspace should read Section 8's obligations 3 through 7 as the current, narrowest statement of which components remain exempt.

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

FACT: "Member States shall communicate to the Commission the text of the main provisions of national law which they adopt in the field covered by this Directive." *Source: Article 2(2). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32017L2096

*Analytical inference:* this reporting duty runs Member-State-to-Commission; the captured text states no separate registration or reporting duty running to a private party.

# 11. Operational System Requirements

FACT: "Dismantling if, in correlation with entry 10(a), an average threshold of 60 grams per vehicle is exceeded." *Source: Annex II, footnote (5). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32017L2096

*Operational implication:* a workspace operating an end-of-life-vehicle dismantling facility should maintain a per-vehicle tracking process for the named electronic-component categories against this 60-gram average threshold.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

FACT: "This exemption does not cover the use of lead in: — glass in bulbs and glaze of spark plugs, — dielectric ceramic materials of components listed under 10(b), 10(c) and 10(d)." *Source: Annex II, entry 10(a) footnote. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32017L2096

*Analytical inference:* entry 10(a)'s own exemption for lead in glass/ceramic electronic components carries its own internal carve-out for spark-plug glass and certain other components' dielectric ceramic materials -- those remain subject to the base prohibition even though the general 10(a) exemption might otherwise seem to cover them.

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

FACT: "Directive 2000/53/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 18 September 2000 on end-of life vehicles" *Source: recital, citing the parent Directive. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32017L2096

*Analytical inference:* Directive 2000/53/EC itself (the parent End-of-Life Vehicles Directive) is the substantive instrument a workspace should read for the base prohibition, vehicle-scope definitions, and recovery/recycling targets; this 2017 Directive only replaces its Annex II exemption table.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 18 September 2000: Directive 2000/53/EC (the parent End-of-Life Vehicles Directive) is adopted.
- 1 July 2003: the base prohibition on lead, mercury, cadmium, and hexavalent chromium in vehicle materials/components takes effect for vehicles placed on the market from that date.
- 15 November 2017: Commission Directive (EU) 2017/2096 is adopted at Brussels.
- 16 November 2017: Commission Directive (EU) 2017/2096 is published in the Official Journal.
- 6 June 2018: Member States' own deadline to adopt and publish national transposition measures (now passed).
- 1 January 2019: the vehicle type-approval cutoff for the high-voltage-battery lead exemption (Annex II entry 5(a)).
- 2019: the review date for exemptions marked footnote (3).
- 2021: the review date for the copper-alloy exemption (Annex II entry 3) and other entries marked footnote (1).
- 2024: the review date for exemptions marked footnote (2).

*Source for timeline entries: Commission Directive (EU) 2017/2096, its own recitals, articles, signature block, and Annex II footnotes (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32017L2096).*

# 15. Sources

|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Commission Directive (EU) 2017/2096 of 15 November 2017 (with amended Annex II) | EU Official Journal instrument (EUR-Lex) | https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32017L2096 |

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2016/2321, the instrument that fixes the standard format of the ready for recycling certificate under Regulation (EU) No 1257/2013 on ship recycling. It exists to give a workspace with EU-flagged or EU-recycled vessel exposure a single record of the certificate's own required content, and of the entry-into-force date of the format itself.

FACT: "COMMISSION IMPLEMENTING DECISION (EU) 2016/2321 of 19 December 2016 on the format of the ready for recycling certificate issued in accordance with Regulation (EU) No 1257/2013 of the European Parliament and of the Council on ship recycling (Text with EEA relevance)" *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32016D2321. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32016D2321

*Analytical inference:* this is a narrow, format-only implementing decision; it does not create new substantive ship recycling duties beyond those already set by Regulation (EU) No 1257/2013 itself.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

This Decision implements Regulation (EU) No 1257/2013 of the European Parliament and of the Council on ship recycling, an EU-wide instrument. It applies to the workspace only indirectly: a freight-adjacent workspace with EU-flagged or EU-recycled vessel exposure encounters this Decision through the certificate a ship must carry before recycling, not through a duty running to the workspace's own core forwarding operations.

FACT: "Regulation (EU) No 1257/2013 of the European Parliament and of the Council on ship recycling (Text with EEA relevance)" *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32016D2321. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32016D2321

*Operational implication:* the "Text with EEA relevance" marking means the certificate format also reaches the EEA states beyond the EU-27, widening the set of jurisdictions where this exact format is the recognised one.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The Decision itself carries no compliance duty running to the workspace; its only direct legal effect is fixing when the format becomes the one administrations and recognised organisations must use.

FACT: "This Decision shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union" *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32016D2321. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32016D2321

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the pool captured here does not itself state the Official Journal publication date needed to compute the exact calendar day the twentieth-day period runs from; a workspace needing the precise in-force date should confirm it against the Official Journal's own publication record for L 345, 20 December 2016.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: this Decision is a certificate-format implementing act, not a standalone compliance regime; "substantive requirements" here means the format's own stated content obligations, which run to the administration or recognised organisation issuing the certificate rather than to a private freight forwarder directly.*

**1. Certificate format compliance (core obligation).** FACT: "Ready for recycling certificates issued in accordance with Article 9(9) and endorsed in accordance with Article 10(5) of Regulation (EU) No 1257/2013 shall comply with the format set out in the Annex to this Decision." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32016D2321. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32016D2321

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this obligation runs to the administration or recognised organisation issuing or endorsing the certificate under Regulation (EU) No 1257/2013, not directly to a freight forwarder; a workspace handling an EU ship recycling case should confirm which party in its chain bears this duty.

**2. Inventory of hazardous materials annexed to the certificate.** FACT: "In accordance with Article 9(9) of Regulation (EU) No 1257/2013, the inventory of hazardous materials is annexed to the ready for recycling certificate." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32016D2321. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32016D2321

*Analytical inference:* this is a paperwork-completeness condition on the certificate itself, not a separate obligation running to the workspace.

**3. Ship recycling plan annexed to the certificate.** FACT: "In accordance with Article 9(9) of Regulation (EU) No 1257/2013, the ship recycling plan is annexed to the ready for recycling certificate." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32016D2321. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32016D2321

*Analytical inference:* the same paperwork-completeness logic as obligation 2 above applies here.

**4. Recycling facility must be on the EU's European List (workspace-adjacent).** FACT: "that the ship recycling facility(ies) where this ship is to be recycled is listed in the European list in accordance with Article 16 of Regulation (EU) No 1257/2013" *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32016D2321. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32016D2321

*Operational implication:* a workspace advising on or arranging an EU-jurisdiction ship recycling case should confirm the receiving facility's own European List status before the certificate can be validly completed, since the certificate itself certifies this fact.

**5. Single-voyage endorsement for extended validity (workspace-adjacent).** FACT: "This certificate shall, in accordance with Article 10(5) of Regulation (EU) No 1257/2013 on ship recycling, be accepted as valid for a single point to point voyage from the port of" *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32016D2321. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32016D2321

*Operational implication:* this endorsement is the only mechanism this Decision provides for a ship to reach the recycling facility's port under a certificate that would otherwise have expired; a workspace planning the final voyage should treat it as the fallback where a period of grace is needed.

No verbatim penalty summary statement was located in the captured source text for this record-grade item; no source in this item's pool states a fine, compliance deadline, or penalty running to a private freight forwarder, carrier, or logistics intermediary under this Decision. No verbatim primary deadline statement was located in the captured source text either, beyond the format's own entry-into-force timing already stated in Section 4.

No phase-in is stated in Articles 1 to 2. No exceptions are stated in Articles 1 to 2. No scope limits are stated in Articles 1 to 2.

Obligations surveyed: 8; workspace-adjacent: 3; extracted as FACT: 5.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 19 December 2016: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2016/2321 adopted.

*Source for timeline entry: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32016D2321 (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32016D2321).*

# 15. Sources
