entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2022/90, which sets the detailed elements of the EU's Union risk-based targeting mechanism for selecting ships for port state inspection under Directive (EU) 2019/883 on port reception facilities for ship-generated waste. It exists to give a workspace with EU-port-calling vessel exposure a single record of how a ship's inspection risk category is set and what raises or lowers it.

FACT: "COMMISSION IMPLEMENTING REGULATION (EU) 2022/90 of 21 January 2022 laying down rules for the application of Directive (EU) 2019/883 of the European Parliament and of the Council as regards the detailed elements of the Union risk-based targeting mechanism for selecting ships for inspection (Text with EEA relevance)" *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32022R0090. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022R0090

*Analytical inference:* this Regulation is a targeting-methodology instrument for Member State inspectors; it does not itself create a new substantive waste-delivery duty beyond those already in Directive (EU) 2019/883.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "By establishing the Union risk-based targeting mechanism, the relevant authorities in the Member States are to have a supporting tool to fulfil the inspection commitment in accordance with Article 11(1) of Directive (EU) 2019/883." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32022R0090. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022R0090

*Operational implication:* a workspace whose vessels call at EU ports is indirectly exposed through the ship's own risk category, which this mechanism computes from the vessel's waste-notification and prior-inspection record, not through a duty running to the workspace by name.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

FACT: "This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union" *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32022R0090. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022R0090

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the pool captured here does not itself state the Official Journal publication date needed to compute the exact calendar day the twentieth-day period runs from; a workspace needing the precise in-force date should confirm it against the Official Journal's own publication record for L 15, 24 January 2022.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: this Regulation's requirements run principally to Member State authorities operating the targeting mechanism; "workspace-adjacent" below marks the parameters and consequences that bear directly on a vessel operator's own inspection exposure.*

**1. Risk-level classification of ships (workspace-adjacent).** FACT: "For the purposes of inspections, Member States shall classify the ships referred to in Article 3(1), point (a), of Directive (EU) 2019/883, into the following risk level categories: (a) Risk level 1 (high risk); (b) Risk level 2 (medium risk); (c) Risk level 3 (low risk); (d) Risk level 4 (minimum risk)." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32022R0090. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022R0090

*Operational implication:* every ship a workspace operates or charters into an EU port is assigned to one of these four risk levels, which drives how often it is selected for inspection.

**2. Priority inspection for higher-risk ships (workspace-adjacent).** FACT: "give priority to the inspection of ships with a higher risk level category" *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32022R0090. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022R0090

*Operational implication:* a vessel that accumulates risk-level 1 or 2 alerts should expect materially more frequent port state inspection than a risk-level 3 or 4 vessel.

**3. Minimum baseline inspection rate (workspace-adjacent).** FACT: "randomly select for inspection at least 1 % of number of ships to be inspected every year." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32022R0090. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022R0090

*Operational implication:* even a ship with no active risk alert is not exempt from inspection outright; the 1% random-selection floor means every ship calling an EU port carries some baseline inspection probability regardless of risk category.

**4. Exempted ships are still swept back into inspection after 12 months (workspace-adjacent).** FACT: "The alert is activated if the ship has an exemption and has not been inspected for 12 months, to ensure that these ships will be included in the inspections." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32022R0090. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022R0090

*Operational implication:* a workspace relying on an exemption from a Directive (EU) 2019/883 obligation should not treat that exemption as permanent inspection immunity; after 12 uninspected months the exemption itself becomes the trigger for an inspection alert.

**5. Advance waste notification non-compliance alert (workspace-adjacent).** FACT: "Non-compliance with the advanced waste notification requirements set out in Article 6 of Directive (EU) 2019/883." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32022R0090. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022R0090

*Operational implication:* a workspace's own advance waste notification practice under Article 6 of Directive (EU) 2019/883 directly feeds this alert; a missed or incomplete notification raises the ship's risk level at the next port.

**6. Prior non-compliance report alert.** FACT: "Existing report(s) by Port Reception Facilities inspection authorities, port authorities or other competent bodies indicating that the ship has not complied with Article 7 of Directive (EU) 2019/883." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32022R0090. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022R0090

*Analytical inference:* this alert is activated manually by port reception facility inspectors rather than computed automatically, so it depends on the reporting practice of the specific port authority involved.

**7. Prior-inspection alert phased in from 28 June 2022 (per-year trajectory).** FACT: "This alert should only be active after 28 June 2022." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32022R0090. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022R0090

*Analytical inference:* this is the one dated phase-in in the pool: the risk parameter tracking whether a ship was inspected under Article 10 of Directive (EU) 2019/883 in the previous 12 months only starts alerting from 28 June 2022, not from this Regulation's own entry into force.

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1192, which amends Implementing Regulation (EU) 2018/2067 on the verification of data and the accreditation of verifiers under the EU Emissions Trading System (EU ETS). It exists to give a workspace with EU ETS verification exposure (installation operators, aircraft operators, or ETS2 regulated entities) a single record of the new and amended verification duties and their commencement dates.

FACT: "COMMISSION IMPLEMENTING REGULATION (EU) 2025/1192 of 18 June 2025 amending Implementing Regulation (EU) 2018/2067 as regards certain aspects on the verification of data and on the accreditation of verifiers (Text with EEA relevance)" *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32025R1192. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32025R1192

*Analytical inference:* this is an amending regulation; its substantive content lives in the numbered points of Article 1, each inserting or replacing a provision of the base Implementing Regulation (EU) 2018/2067.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "relevant guidelines and legislation issued by the Member State in which the verifier is carrying out a verification" *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32025R1192. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32025R1192

*Operational implication:* a workspace whose installations, aircraft operations, or ETS2-regulated activities are verified under this framework is exposed through the verifier's own duties, which vary by the Member State in which the verification is carried out.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

FACT: "This Regulation shall enter into force on the third day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32025R1192. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32025R1192

FACT: "Article 1, points (11)(c), (11)(d) and (11)(e), (19)(b)(iii) and (29) shall apply from 1 January 2025 to the verification of emissions occurring from 1 January 2024 onwards." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32025R1192. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32025R1192

*Operational implication:* the amendments on non-CO2 aviation effects and regulated-entity (ETS2) verification did not wait for a future reporting year; they apply from 1 January 2025 to emissions that already occurred from 1 January 2024 onward, so a workspace in either category should treat verification years 2024 onward as already in scope.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: these requirements run principally to verifiers and accreditation bodies; "workspace-adjacent" below marks the obligations and consequences that bear directly on an installation operator, aircraft operator, or regulated entity whose activities are verified.*

**1. CO2-in-transit transfer verification deadline (workspace-adjacent).** FACT: "the verifier shall check whether the CO 2 in transit has been transferred to another installation or CO 2 transport infrastructure no later than 31 January of the following year." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32025R1192. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32025R1192

*Operational implication:* a workspace operating or using CO2 transport infrastructure should have transfer records ready for the verifier by 31 January of the year following the reporting year.

**2. Operator's emission report zero-rated biomass evidence check (workspace-adjacent).** FACT: "For the purposes of verifying the operator’s emission report, the verifier shall, as part of the check referred to in paragraph 1, check the following evidence: (a) the operator’s evidence demonstrating compliance of zero-rated biomass fuels with the sustainability and greenhouse gas savings criteria laid down in Article 29(2) to (7) and (10) of Directive (EU) 2018/2001" *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32025R1192. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32025R1192

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this evidence-check duty runs to the verifier, but the underlying evidence must come from the operator; a workspace claiming zero-rated biomass fuels should confirm its own documentation satisfies Article 29(2) to (7) and (10) of Directive (EU) 2018/2001 before verification.

**3. Verifier may find the scope of verification too limited (workspace-adjacent).** FACT: "The verifier may conclude that the scope of the verification referred to in Article 27(1)(c) and Article 27(1) (ca) is too limited in any of the following situations:" *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32025R1192. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32025R1192

*Operational implication:* if a workspace's own monitoring plan, monitoring methodology plan, or climate-neutrality plan does not give the verifier sufficient scope or clarity, the verifier can decline to issue a satisfactory verification opinion, which is itself an operational and compliance risk.

**4. Non-CO2 aviation effects verification duty from 1 January 2025 (workspace-adjacent).** FACT: "the verification of non-CO 2 aviation effects occurring from 1 January 2025, reported by the aircraft operator pursuant to Article 14(5) of Directive 2003/87/EC." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32025R1192. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32025R1192

*Operational implication:* an aircraft operator workspace now has its non-CO2 aviation effects report verified on the same footing as its emissions report, starting from the 2025 reporting cycle.

**5. Regulated-entity (ETS2) emissions verification duty from 1 January 2025 (workspace-adjacent).** FACT: "the verification of greenhouse gas emissions occurring from 1 January 2025, reported by the regulated entity pursuant to Article 30f of Directive 2003/87/EC" *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32025R1192. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32025R1192

*Operational implication:* a workspace that is itself a regulated entity under Article 30f of Directive 2003/87/EC (the buildings, road transport, and additional-sectors ETS) now has its greenhouse gas emissions verified under this same framework.

**6. Five-year benchmarking period rule (workspace-adjacent, per-year trajectory).** FACT: "the applicable period until 31 December 2025 and subsequently each five-year period ending 31 December of each fifth year thereafter." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32025R1192. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32025R1192

*Operational implication:* a workspace planning free-allocation benchmarking should treat 31 December 2025 as the end of the current applicable period, with the next period running a further five years.

**7. Accreditation scope 12/12a transitional treatment.** FACT: "issued under activity group 12 of the scope of accreditation, which are valid on 31 March 2025, shall be considered issued for activity group 12a under the scope of accreditation" *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32025R1192. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32025R1192

*Analytical inference:* this transitional rule runs to accreditation bodies and verifiers rather than to a workspace directly; it is included here because a workspace choosing a verifier for a 2025 aviation verification should confirm the verifier's accreditation scope reference has carried over correctly.

No verbatim penalty summary statement was located in the captured source text for this record-grade item; no source in this item's pool states a fine or penalty running to a private freight forwarder, carrier, or logistics intermediary.

No exceptions are stated in Articles 1 to 2.

Obligations surveyed: 10; workspace-adjacent: 6; extracted as FACT: 8.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 18 June 2025: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1192 adopted.
- 1 January 2025: non-CO2 aviation effects verification and regulated-entity (ETS2) emissions verification duties apply, covering emissions occurring from 1 January 2024 onward.
- 31 December 2025: end of the current benchmarking applicable period under Article 10a(1)/10b(4) of Directive 2003/87/EC; a new five-year period follows.

*Source for timeline entries: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32025R1192 (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32025R1192).*

# 15. Sources

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks The Waste (Miscellaneous Amendments) (Northern Ireland) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019 (UKSI 2019/271), a post-Brexit "fixing" instrument that re-attributes references to "Member States" in four retained EU waste Directives (the Waste Framework Directive, the Packaging Waste Directive, the Mining Waste Directive, and the Industrial Emissions Directive, as they apply in Northern Ireland) to the appropriate domestic authority, without itself creating a new substantive duty.

FACT: "The Waste (Miscellaneous Amendments) (Northern Ireland) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019" *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UKSI 2019/271. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2019/271

FACT: "Sift requirements satisfied 29th January 2019 Made 7th February 2019 Laid before Parliament 18th February 2019 Coming into force in accordance with regulation 1" *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UKSI 2019/271. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2019/271

*Analytical inference:* the sift-satisfied, made, and laid dates above are the instrument's own procedural timeline; none of them is itself a compliance deadline running to a private party.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "These Regulations extend to Northern Ireland only." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UKSI 2019/271. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2019/271

*Operational implication:* a workspace with no Northern Ireland waste-handling exposure has no reach from this instrument at all; it applies only within Northern Ireland.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

FACT: "An impact assessment has not been produced for this instrument as no, or no significant, impact on the private or voluntary sector is foreseen." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UKSI 2019/271 (Explanatory Note). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2019/271

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the instrument's own Explanatory Note states no significant private-sector impact was foreseen; a workspace should treat this as government's own assessment at the time of making, not as a guarantee that no provision below reaches a private party (the exporter accreditation provision in Section 8 is the one exception this pool's own text surfaces).

FACT: "Reg. 1 in force at 31.12.2020 on IP completion day, see reg. 1 (as amended by S.R. 2020/284 , regs. 1(1) , 4(2) )" (31 December 2020, the IP completion day) *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UKSI 2019/271 (Commencement Information). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2019/271

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: this instrument's dominant content is a mechanical "member State" to "appropriate authority" reference substitution across four retained EU Directives as they apply in Northern Ireland; that substitution reattributes an existing administrative function and is not itself surveyed below as a new obligation. The two items below are the ones this pool's own text shows reaching a private party or preserving a private-facing operative rule.*

**1. Waste classification list remains binding, with a stated exception (workspace-adjacent).** FACT: "The list of waste shall, except as provided in Commission Decision 2000/532/EC , be binding as regards determination of the waste which is to be considered as hazardous waste or as non-hazardous waste." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UKSI 2019/271. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2019/271

*Operational implication:* a workspace classifying waste arising from Northern Ireland operations as hazardous or non-hazardous must still use the retained EU list of waste as the binding classification, except as Commission Decision 2000/532/EC itself provides.

**2. Exporter accreditation may be cancelled for non-compliant recyclable-material exports (workspace-adjacent).** FACT: "Where the appropriate authority has granted an accreditation to an exporter, and is no longer satisfied that the requirements in regulation 24(3)(b) or (9), which applied to that grant of accreditation, are met in relation to the export of one or more specified recyclable materials for reprocessing at one or more reprocessing sites outside the United Kingdom, the appropriate authority shall cancel the accreditation of an exporter to the extent that it relates to any such export which does not meet those requirements." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UKSI 2019/271. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2019/271

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this duty and consequence run to an exporter holding an accreditation to export specified recyclable packaging materials for reprocessing outside the United Kingdom; a workspace acting as such an exporter should confirm its own ongoing compliance with regulation 24(3)(b) or (9) requirements, since the appropriate authority's cancellation power is the one enforceable private-party consequence this pool's own text states.

No verbatim primary deadline statement running to a private party was located in the captured source text; no verbatim due-date statement was located either. No verbatim applicability language naming a duty-holder class beyond the exporter obligation above was located.

No phase-in is stated in Sections 1 to 5 (Regulations 1 to 5 of this instrument). No scope limits are stated in Sections 1 to 5 (Regulations 1 to 5 of this instrument), beyond the Northern-Ireland-only territorial extent already stated in Section 2.

Obligations surveyed: 8; workspace-adjacent: 2; extracted as FACT: 4.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 29 January 2019: Sift requirements satisfied.
- 7 February 2019: Regulations made.
- 18 February 2019: Regulations laid before Parliament.
- 2019: Enacted (legislation.gov.uk identifier year).
- 31 December 2020: Regulations come into force (IP completion day).

*Source for timeline entries: legislation.gov.uk, UKSI 2019/271 (https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2019/271).*

# 15. Sources

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks The Alternative Fuel Labelling and Greenhouse Gas Emissions (Miscellaneous Amendments) Regulations 2019 (UKSI 2019/421), which implements Article 7 of Directive 2014/94/EU on alternative fuels infrastructure in UK law: standardised fuel labelling for refuelling points and motor vehicles, an enforcement and civil-penalty regime, and a related amendment to the greenhouse gas emissions reporting rules for road fuel.

FACT: "The Alternative Fuel Labelling and Greenhouse Gas Emissions (Miscellaneous Amendments) Regulations 2019" *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UKSI 2019/421. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2019/421

FACT: "Made 25th February 2019 Laid before Parliament 4th March 2019" (25 February 2019; 4 March 2019) *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UKSI 2019/421. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2019/421

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "that is placed on the market in the United Kingdom" *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UKSI 2019/421. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2019/421

*Operational implication:* a workspace operating a refuelling point, manufacturing motor vehicles, or dealing in motor vehicles placed on the market in the United Kingdom is a direct duty-holder under this instrument.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

FACT: "Regulation 22 comes into force on 22nd March 2019." (22 March 2019) *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UKSI 2019/421. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2019/421

FACT: "Regulations 5, 6 and 14(2) and (3) come into force on 1st April 2020." (1 April 2020) *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UKSI 2019/421. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2019/421

FACT: "The remainder of these Regulations come into force on 1st September 2019." (1 September 2019) *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UKSI 2019/421. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2019/421

FACT: "The first report must be published before 1st April 2024." (1 April 2024) *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UKSI 2019/421. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2019/421

*Operational implication:* a workspace's own compliance start date depends on which duty applies to it: the GHG reporting amendment (regulation 22) started 22 March 2019, the manufacturer and dealer vehicle-labelling duties (regulations 5, 6, and 14(2)-(3)) started 1 April 2020, and every other duty, including the refuelling-point labelling duty, started 1 September 2019. The Secretary of State's own first statutory review report is due 1 April 2024.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: this instrument places direct duties on infrastructure operators, motor vehicle manufacturers, and motor vehicle dealers, backed by a civil-penalty enforcement regime; "workspace-adjacent" below marks the duties and consequences that bear directly on such a workspace.*

**1. Refuelling point labelling duty (workspace-adjacent, direct duty).** FACT: "An infrastructure operator must ensure that each refuelling point for which that operator is responsible is labelled with the relevant identifier denoting the category of fuel available at that refuelling point, in accordance with paragraphs (2) to (4)." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UKSI 2019/421. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2019/421

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this duty runs to the "infrastructure operator" (the person responsible for operating a refuelling point); a workspace operating any public refuelling point should confirm it meets the labelling specifications in Schedules 1 and 2.

**2. Motor vehicle manufacturer labelling duty (workspace-adjacent, direct duty).** FACT: "A motor vehicle manufacturer must ensure that— (a) each relevant vehicle manufactured by it is labelled in accordance with paragraph (2), (b) the user manual of each such relevant vehicle contains information in accordance with paragraph (3)." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UKSI 2019/421. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2019/421

**3. Motor vehicle dealer duty (workspace-adjacent, direct duty).** FACT: "A motor vehicle dealer must ensure, in relation to all relevant vehicles offered for sale or lease by it, that— (a) the identifier (and in the case of a relevant vehicle that can use more than one fuel type, all the relevant identifiers), indicating the fuel type that the vehicle can use, is available and easy to obtain, and is easy to understand by any prospective user of the vehicle, (b) any identifiers affixed by the motor vehicle manufacturer to comply with regulation 5(1)(a) are maintained on the vehicle while it is offered for sale or lease." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UKSI 2019/421. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2019/421

**4. Civil penalty amounts (workspace-adjacent).** FACT: "The maximum civil penalty for each breach of regulation 4(1) by an infrastructure operator is £500 for each fuel dispenser or nozzle which does not meet the requirements of regulation 4(1)." (a GBP-denominated penalty per non-conforming dispenser or nozzle) *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UKSI 2019/421. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2019/421

FACT: "The maximum civil penalty for each breach of regulation 5(1) by a motor vehicle manufacturer is— (a) £100 for each relevant vehicle which is not labelled in accordance with the requirements of regulation 5(1)(a), and (b) £100 for each user manual which does not contain the information required by regulation 5(1)(b)." (a smaller GBP-denominated penalty per non-conforming relevant vehicle or user manual) *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UKSI 2019/421. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2019/421

*Operational implication:* a workspace should budget per-unit exposure across dispensers, vehicles, and manuals, not a single flat fine.

**5. Duty to comply with an information notice by its stated date (workspace-adjacent).** FACT: "A person served with an information notice must comply with its requirements by the date referred to in paragraph (2)(c)." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UKSI 2019/421. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2019/421

**6. Appeal deadline against a civil penalty decision (workspace-adjacent).** FACT: "within 28 days of the date of that notice, appeal to the First-tier Tribunal against the enforcement authority’s decision made under regulation 16, on the grounds that the decision was— (a) based on an error of fact, or (b) wrong in law." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UKSI 2019/421. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2019/421

*Operational implication:* a workspace that receives an adverse notice under regulation 16(2) has 28 days from that notice to appeal to the First-tier Tribunal.

**7. Civil penalty enforced as a court order (workspace-adjacent).** FACT: "In England and Wales, the civil penalty is recoverable as if it were payable under an order of the County Court in England and Wales." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UKSI 2019/421. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2019/421

*Analytical inference:* the source states parallel enforcement mechanisms for Northern Ireland (County Court) and Scotland (Sheriff Court decree arbitral); an unpaid civil penalty is not merely an administrative debt.

**8. GHG credit amendment for upstream emission reductions (workspace-adjacent).** FACT: "The amendment allows certain energy suppliers to claim GHG credits arising out of reductions in upstream emissions generated in 2019." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UKSI 2019/421. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2019/421

*Operational implication:* a workspace supplying fuel for road vehicles or mobile machinery that reports under the Motor Fuel (Road Vehicle and Mobile Machinery) Greenhouse Gas Emissions Reporting Regulations 2012 gained an additional 2019 crediting route through this amendment.

**9. Refuelling point "accessible to the public" definition sets the labelling duty's own reach (workspace-adjacent).** FACT: "A refuelling point is accessible to the public if it is intended for use by members of the public, and is not intended for exclusive use— (a) in respect of a motor vehicle produced by a specific manufacturer, (b) by persons engaged in specific occupations, (c) by persons whilst at their place of employment or by their visitors, or (d) by occupiers of, or visitors to, residential premises." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UKSI 2019/421. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2019/421

*Analytical inference:* a workspace operating a refuelling point reserved for its own fleet, its employees, or a single manufacturer's vehicles is not automatically outside this definition; it is excluded only if the point is genuinely not intended for public use in one of the four listed ways.

No exceptions are stated in Sections 1 to 22 (Regulations 1 to 22 of this instrument); the one "except" occurrence in this pool is the hosting site's own footer licence notice, not the instrument's substantive text. No scope limits are stated in Sections 1 to 22 (Regulations 1 to 22 of this instrument), beyond the public-access definition already captured above.

Obligations surveyed: 11; workspace-adjacent: 9; extracted as FACT: 10.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 25 February 2019: Regulations made.
- 4 March 2019: Regulations laid before Parliament.
- 22 March 2019: Regulation 22 (GHG credit amendment) comes into force.
- 1 September 2019: The remainder of the Regulations (including the refuelling-point labelling duty) come into force.
- 2019: Enacted (legislation.gov.uk identifier year).
- 1 April 2020: Regulations 5, 6, and 14(2)-(3) (vehicle manufacturer and dealer labelling duties) come into force.
- 1 April 2024: first statutory review report due.

*Source for timeline entries: legislation.gov.uk, UKSI 2019/421 (https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2019/421).*

# 15. Sources

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2017/2185, an EU technical instrument that establishes the code lists conformity assessment bodies use when applying for designation as notified bodies under the Medical Devices Regulation (EU) 2017/745 and the In Vitro Diagnostic Medical Devices Regulation (EU) 2017/746. It exists to give a workspace that ships, imports, or otherwise handles EU-regulated medical devices or in vitro diagnostic devices a reference for which notified-body code corresponds to which device category, since the codes determine which notified body may lawfully assess a given device type for CE marking.

FACT: "The list of codes and corresponding types of devices for the purpose of specifying the scope of the designation as notified bodies in the field of medical devices under Regulation (EU) 2017/745 is set out in Annex I to this Regulation." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2017/2185, Article 1(1). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32017R2185

*Analytical inference:* the codes are an administrative classification tool; they do not by themselves create a compliance duty running to a freight-forwarding workspace, but they are the reference vocabulary a workspace would need to identify which notified body's scope of designation covers a given device shipment.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

This is a Commission Implementing Regulation, not a rulemaking that creates new substantive obligations on device manufacturers or forwarders; it is a technical annex to the designation process conformity assessment bodies and Member States already run under Regulation (EU) 2017/745 and Regulation (EU) 2017/746.

FACT: "Conformity assessment bodies shall use the lists of codes and corresponding types of devices set out in Annexes I and II to this Regulation when specifying the types of devices in the application for designation referred to in Article 38 of Regulation (EU) 2017/745 and Article 34 of Regulation (EU) 2017/746." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2017/2185, Article 2. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32017R2185

*Operational implication:* a workspace relying on a notified body's CE certificate for a medical device or in vitro diagnostic device shipment can check the notified body's own designation scope against these codes to confirm the notified body is actually authorised to certify that device category.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

*Analytical inference:* because Annexes I and II are static code lists that have been in force since 2017, no time-bound compliance action currently runs to the workspace from this instrument; the item's own captured pool surfaces no scheduled review, amendment, or comment window.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

*Legal Confirmation Required:* This Regulation's substantive duties run to conformity assessment bodies (in their designation applications) and to Member States (in notifying the Commission and other Member States of a body's designated scope); none of the captured text states a duty running directly to a device manufacturer, importer, or freight-forwarding workspace. Whether a specific shipment's compliance documentation correctly cites a notified body's designation scope under these codes is a fact-specific question outside this brief's scope and requires counsel or regulatory-affairs review on the specific device and notified body.

FACT: "In accordance with Article 42(3) of Regulation (EU) 2017/745 and Article 38(3) of Regulation (EU) 2017/746, when notifying the Commission and the other Member States of the conformity assessment bodies they have designated Member States are to clearly specify, using the codes, the scope of the designation indicating the conformity assessment activities and the types of devices which the notified body is authorised to assess." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2017/2185, recital 3. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32017R2185

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

*No content for this section as of the export date; this item's captured pool contains no separate guidance document beyond the instrument's own text, which is treated as the primary source throughout this brief.*

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

*No content for this section as of the export date; the item's export carries no forward_events rows, and the captured pool states no scheduled review or amendment to this code list.*

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does this Regulation create a direct compliance duty on a freight-forwarding workspace?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* No source in this brief's corpus states a duty running from this Regulation to a device manufacturer, importer, or freight forwarder directly; its stated duties run to conformity assessment bodies and Member States (Section 8). Whether a specific transaction creates an indirect duty (for example, through a customer contract requiring proof of a properly-scoped notified-body certificate) is a fact-specific question requiring counsel review.

**Q2: Does the human-genetic-testing carve-out in Annex II change which code a workspace should expect on a device's documentation?**

FACT: "Devices intended to be used for markers of cancer and non-malignant tumours except devices for human genetic testing" *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2017/2185, Annex II, section I.3. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32017R2185

*Operational implication:* a device intended for human genetic testing is coded under Annex II's own separate genetic-testing category rather than under the cancer/tumour-marker category, even where the underlying clinical use case overlaps.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: this instrument's substantive requirements run mainly to conformity assessment bodies and Member States, not directly to a device manufacturer, importer, or freight-forwarding workspace; "substantive requirements" here also captures the code-list content and applicability window a workspace needs when verifying a notified body's scope of designation.*

**1. Annex I code list for medical devices.** FACT: "The list of codes and corresponding types of devices for the purpose of specifying the scope of the designation as notified bodies in the field of medical devices under Regulation (EU) 2017/745 is set out in Annex I to this Regulation." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2017/2185, Article 1(1). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32017R2185

**2. Annex II code list for in vitro diagnostic devices.** FACT: "The list of codes and corresponding types of devices for the purpose of specifying the scope of the designation as notified bodies in the field of in vitro diagnostic medical devices under Regulation (EU) 2017/746 is set out in Annex II to this Regulation." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2017/2185, Article 1(2). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32017R2185

**3. Conformity assessment bodies' own application duty.** FACT: "Conformity assessment bodies shall use the lists of codes and corresponding types of devices set out in Annexes I and II to this Regulation when specifying the types of devices in the application for designation referred to in Article 38 of Regulation (EU) 2017/745 and Article 34 of Regulation (EU) 2017/746." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2017/2185, Article 2. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32017R2185

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this duty runs from a conformity assessment body to the Member State/Commission designation process; it does not itself create a duty running to a device manufacturer, importer, or freight forwarder.

**4. Member States' scope-notification duty.** FACT: "In accordance with Article 42(3) of Regulation (EU) 2017/745 and Article 38(3) of Regulation (EU) 2017/746, when notifying the Commission and the other Member States of the conformity assessment bodies they have designated Member States are to clearly specify, using the codes, the scope of the designation indicating the conformity assessment activities and the types of devices which the notified body is authorised to assess." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2017/2185, recital 3. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32017R2185

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this duty runs from a Member State to the Commission and other Member States; it does not itself create a duty running to the workspace, though its result (a published, code-referenced scope of designation) is the reference a workspace can check against a specific device shipment.

**5. Entry into force.** FACT: "This Regulation shall enter into force on the day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union ." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2017/2185, Article 3. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32017R2185

**6. Application window opens.** FACT: "As of 26 November 2017, conformity assessment bodies may submit an application for designation as a notified body under Regulation (EU) 2017/745 and Regulation (EU) 2017/746." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2017/2185, recital 5. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32017R2185

**7. Genetic-testing carve-out within the cancer/tumour-marker code category.** FACT: "Devices intended to be used for markers of cancer and non-malignant tumours except devices for human genetic testing" *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2017/2185, Annex II, section I.3. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32017R2185

*Operational implication:* a device intended for human genetic testing is coded separately (Annex II's own genetic-testing category) rather than under the cancer/tumour-marker category, even where the underlying clinical use case overlaps.

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks Commission Implementing Decision 2012/249/EU, which lays down EU-wide rules for how competent authorities and combustion-plant operators determine the start-up and shut-down periods used to assess compliance with the emission limit values in Directive 2010/75/EU (the Industrial Emissions Directive). It exists to give a workspace that owns or operates a combustion plant covered by Chapter III of Directive 2010/75/EU (for example, an on-site power or heat-generation asset at a terminal or facility) a reference for how its own permit's start-up/shut-down determination should be structured, and to confirm that this Decision otherwise runs to Member State competent authorities, not to a freight-forwarding workspace directly.

FACT: "This Decision lays down rules concerning the determination of the start-up and shut-down periods referred to in point (27) of Article 3 and in point 1 of Part 4 of Annex V to Directive 2010/75/EU." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision 2012/249/EU, Article 1. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32012D0249

*Analytical inference:* this Decision is technical permitting methodology; it creates no obligation on a workspace that does not itself operate a qualifying combustion plant.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

This is a Commission Implementing Decision addressed to the Member States, not a rulemaking that creates obligations directly enforceable against a private party; it supplies the determination methodology Member State competent authorities and combustion-plant operators use when the underlying Directive 2010/75/EU requires start-up/shut-down periods to be identified in a plant's permit.

FACT: "This Decision shall apply to combustion plants covered by Chapter III of Directive 2010/75/EU." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision 2012/249/EU, Article 1. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32012D0249

*Operational implication:* a workspace's own compliance exposure under this Decision turns entirely on whether it operates a combustion plant within the scope of Chapter III of Directive 2010/75/EU; a workspace that only arranges freight movements and does not itself operate such a plant has no exposure under this Decision.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

*Analytical inference:* because this Decision is a static, already-in-force determination methodology with no stated review date or phase-in, no time-bound compliance action currently runs to the workspace from this instrument; the item's own captured pool surfaces no scheduled review, amendment, or comment window.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

*Legal Confirmation Required:* This Decision's substantive rules run to Member State competent authorities issuing permits under Directive 2010/75/EU, and secondarily to the combustion-plant operators those permits govern; none of the captured text states a duty running to a freight-forwarding workspace that does not itself operate a Chapter III combustion plant. Whether a specific workspace facility (for example, an on-site generator or boiler at a terminal) meets the Chapter III threshold is a fact-specific question requiring counsel or environmental-compliance review.

FACT: "This Decision is addressed to the Member States." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision 2012/249/EU, Article 10. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32012D0249

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

*No content for this section as of the export date; this item's captured pool contains no separate guidance document beyond the instrument's own text, which is treated as the primary source throughout this brief.*

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

*No content for this section as of the export date; the item's export carries no forward_events rows, and the captured pool states no scheduled review or amendment to this Decision.*

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does this Decision create a direct compliance duty on a freight-forwarding workspace?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* No source in this brief's corpus states a duty running from this Decision to a freight forwarder directly; the Decision is addressed to the Member States (Section 4) and its technical rules govern combustion-plant permits (Section 8). Whether the workspace itself operates a Chapter III combustion plant is the threshold fact-specific question, requiring counsel or environmental-compliance review.

**Q2: What determines whether a period counts as start-up, shut-down, or normal operation?**

FACT: "periods during which a combustion plant, after start-up, is operating stably and safely with fuel supply but without the export of heat or electricity or mechanical energy shall not be included in the start-up or shut-down periods." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision 2012/249/EU, Article 3(3). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32012D0249

*Operational implication:* a workspace operating a qualifying combustion plant cannot treat a period of stable, safe operation without heat/electricity/mechanical export as start-up or shut-down; such a period counts as normal operation for emission-limit-value assessment purposes.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: this instrument's substantive requirements run mainly to Member State competent authorities and to the operators of combustion plants covered by Chapter III of Directive 2010/75/EU, not directly to a freight-forwarding workspace; "substantive requirements" here also captures the scope-of-application and addressee facts a workspace needs to determine whether it has any exposure at all.*

**1. Scope of application.** FACT: "This Decision shall apply to combustion plants covered by Chapter III of Directive 2010/75/EU." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision 2012/249/EU, Article 1. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32012D0249

**2. Subject matter and scope (heading).** FACT: "Article 1 Subject matter and scope This Decision lays down rules concerning the determination of the start-up and shut-down periods referred to in point (27) of Article 3 and in point 1 of Part 4 of Annex V to Directive 2010/75/EU." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision 2012/249/EU, Article 1. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32012D0249

**3. Transparency and verifiability of criteria.** FACT: "the criteria or parameters used to determine start-up and shut-down periods shall be transparent and externally verifiable;" *Source: Commission Implementing Decision 2012/249/EU, Article 3(1). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32012D0249

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this rule governs the criteria a Member State competent authority sets in a combustion plant's own permit; it does not itself create a duty running to a freight-forwarding workspace.

**4. Exclusion of stable-operation periods.** FACT: "periods during which a combustion plant, after start-up, is operating stably and safely with fuel supply but without the export of heat or electricity or mechanical energy shall not be included in the start-up or shut-down periods." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision 2012/249/EU, Article 3(3). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32012D0249

**5. Permit-reconsideration duty on change.** FACT: "If any aspects relating to the plant that affect start-up and shut-down periods change, including the installed equipment, fuel type, plant role in the system and installed abatement techniques, the permit conditions related to start-up and shut-down periods shall be reconsidered and, if necessary, updated by the competent authority." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision 2012/249/EU, Article 4(2). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32012D0249

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this duty runs to the competent authority administering a combustion plant's permit; it applies to a workspace only if that workspace itself operates the qualifying plant.

**6. Multi-unit averaging rule.** FACT: "the values measured during the start-up period of the first unit starting up and during the shut-down period of the last combustion unit shutting down shall be disregarded;" *Source: Commission Implementing Decision 2012/249/EU, Article 5(1)(a). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32012D0249

**7. Load-threshold rule for electricity-generating plants.** FACT: "The load thresholds to be used for determining the end of the start-up period and the start of the shut-down period for electricity generating combustion plants and to be included in the plant’s permit shall be a fixed percentage of the rated electrical output of the combustion plant." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision 2012/249/EU, Article 6(3). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32012D0249

**8. Criteria-count rule for operational-parameter determination.** FACT: "at least three criteria shall be defined, with the end of start-up or start of shut-down periods reached when at least two of the criteria have been met." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision 2012/249/EU, Article 9. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32012D0249

**9. Addressee.** FACT: "This Decision is addressed to the Member States." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision 2012/249/EU, Article 10. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32012D0249

**Qualification accounting.** Per-year trajectory: No phase-in is stated in Articles 1 to 10. Exceptions and carve-outs: No exceptions are stated in Articles 1 to 10. Scope limits: CAPTURED above (obligation 2, the "Subject matter and scope" statement).

Obligations surveyed: 9; workspace-adjacent: 2; extracted as FACT: 9.

# 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*No content for this section as of the export date; the captured pool describes a permitting-methodology framework, not the compliance status of any specific product or facility the workspace operates.*

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

*Legal Confirmation Required:* The only registration/reporting-shaped duties in this corpus run to Member State competent authorities administering combustion-plant permits (Section 8, obligation 5). No source in this brief's corpus states a registration or reporting duty running directly to a freight-forwarding workspace.

# 11. Operational System Requirements

*Note: because this instrument is permitting methodology rather than a technical system the workspace itself operates, "operational system requirements" here means the facility-level check a workspace should run if it operates a qualifying combustion plant, not a system this Decision requires the workspace to build.*

*Operational implication:* a workspace that operates an on-site combustion plant (for example, at a terminal or warehouse facility) should confirm with its permit-issuing authority whether that plant falls within Chapter III of Directive 2010/75/EU, and if so, whether its permit's start-up/shut-down determination follows the load-threshold or operational-parameter method this Decision sets out (Section 8, obligations 7 and 8).

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

*No content for this section as of the export date; the captured pool states no exception, exemption, or carve-out from this Decision's scope (confirmed by full-text search: zero occurrences of "except", "exempt", or "carve-out" anywhere in the captured pool).*

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

*No content for this section as of the export date; the captured pool is limited to the instrument's own text and states no adjacent industry research or alternative frameworks.*

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 7 May 2012: Commission Implementing Decision 2012/249/EU adopted (Done at Brussels, 7 May 2012.).

*Source for timeline entries: Commission Implementing Decision 2012/249/EU. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32012D0249*

# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2020/1001, which lays down the detailed rules for operating the Modernisation Fund, the EU Emissions Trading System financing mechanism (Article 10d of Directive 2003/87/EC) that channels auction revenue into energy-system modernisation and energy-efficiency investments in certain, lower-income EU Member States. It exists to give a workspace that participates in a Modernisation-Fund-financed project, directly or as a contractor, subcontractor, or scheme managing authority, a reference for the reporting, record-retention, and publicity duties that attach to receiving that support, and to confirm which duties instead run only to a beneficiary Member State, the European Investment Bank (EIB), or the Investment Committee.

FACT: "Directive 2003/87/EC establishes the Modernisation Fund for the period from 2021 to 2030, to support investments in modernising energy systems and improving energy efficiency in certain Member States." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2020/1001, recital 1. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020R1001

*Analytical inference:* the Fund's own period, 2021 to 2030, is the trajectory this instrument operates on; no separate per-provision phase-in schedule is stated elsewhere in the pool.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

This is a Commission Implementing Regulation directly applicable in all Member States (Article 19), not merely guidance; most of its duties run to beneficiary Member States, the EIB, and the Investment Committee, but several provisions (Section 8, obligations 8 through 10) name "project proponents", "scheme managing authorities", "contractors and subcontractors", and "final recipients" directly.

FACT: "means a Member State listed in Annex IIb to Directive 2003/87/EC" *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2020/1001, Article 2(1). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020R1001

*Operational implication:* a workspace has exposure under this Regulation only if it (or its client) is a project proponent, scheme managing authority, contractor, subcontractor, or final recipient of Modernisation Fund support for a specific investment; a workspace with no such role has no duty under this instrument.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

*Analytical inference:* because this Regulation is already in force and its deadlines (Section 8) run on a recurring annual/biannual cycle to beneficiary Member States rather than to the workspace directly, no time-bound compliance action currently runs to the workspace from this instrument absent a specific Fund-financed project role.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

*Legal Confirmation Required:* Most of this Regulation's procedural duties (investment overviews, disbursement decisions, biannual assessment cycles) run between beneficiary Member States, the EIB, and the Investment Committee; a small number of duties (record retention, Article 16(4)-(5); publicity to final recipients, Article 17(1)-(2)) name project proponents, contractors, subcontractors, and final recipients directly. Whether a specific workspace role in a specific Fund-financed investment triggers one of these duties is a fact-specific question requiring counsel or compliance review on that investment.

FACT: "beneficiary Member States, project proponents and scheme managing authorities, contractors and subcontractors who have received the resources from the Modernisation Fund shall keep available, for a period of five years following the last payment in respect of any project or scheme, all supporting documents and information regarding the payment or expenditure made." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2020/1001, Article 16(5). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020R1001

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

*No content for this section as of the export date; this item's captured pool contains no separate guidance document beyond the instrument's own text, which is treated as the primary source throughout this brief.*

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

*No content for this section as of the export date; the item's export carries no forward_events rows, and the captured pool states no scheduled review or amendment beyond the recurring annual/biannual cycles already recorded in Section 14.*

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does this Regulation create a direct compliance duty on a freight-forwarding workspace?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* No source in this brief's corpus states a duty running from this Regulation to a freight forwarder that has no role in a Modernisation-Fund-financed investment; where a workspace (or its client) is a project proponent, scheme managing authority, contractor, subcontractor, or final recipient of Fund support, Section 8 obligations 8 through 10 do apply. Which role, if any, a specific workspace holds on a specific investment is a fact-specific question requiring counsel review.

**Q2: What happens if a Fund-financed investment is not completed?**

FACT: "the project proponent has not spent the total amount of the revenues from the Modernisation Fund disbursed to the investment within five years from the date of the relevant disbursement decision of the Commission." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2020/1001, Article 10(1)(b). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020R1001

*Operational implication:* a project proponent that received Modernisation Fund disbursement has five years from the date of that disbursement decision to spend the funds on the investment, or the investment is deemed discontinued and unspent amounts are reallocated (Article 10(1)-(2)).

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: this instrument's substantive requirements run mainly between beneficiary Member States, the EIB, and the Investment Committee; a subset (obligations 7 through 11 below) name project proponents, scheme managing authorities, contractors, subcontractors, or final recipients of Modernisation Fund support directly, which is where a workspace's own exposure, if any, would arise.*

**1. Fund period.** FACT: "Directive 2003/87/EC establishes the Modernisation Fund for the period from 2021 to 2030, to support investments in modernising energy systems and improving energy efficiency in certain Member States." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2020/1001, recital 1. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020R1001

**2. Beneficiary Member State definition.** FACT: "means a Member State listed in Annex IIb to Directive 2003/87/EC" *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2020/1001, Article 2(1). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020R1001

**3. Priority-investment funding share.** FACT: "Pursuant to Article 10d(2) of Directive 2003/87/EC, at least 70 % of the financial resources from the Modernisation Fund are to be allocated to priority investments." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2020/1001, recital 7. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020R1001

**4. Annual investment overview deadline.** FACT: "By 30 November of each year, each beneficiary Member State shall provide the European Investment Bank (EIB) and the Investment Committee with an overview of investments in respect of which it intends to submit investment proposals in the next two calendar years" *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2020/1001, Article 3(1). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020R1001

**5. Annual report deadline.** FACT: "By 30 April, beneficiary Member States shall submit to the Commission an annual report for the preceding year containing information specified in Annex II." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2020/1001, Article 13(1). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020R1001

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this deadline runs to a beneficiary Member State reporting to the Commission; it does not itself create a duty running to a freight-forwarding workspace.

**6. Disbursement payment timing.** FACT: "Within 30 days of the date of the disbursement decision, the EIB shall transmit to the beneficiary Member State the relevant amount of the Modernisation Fund support." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2020/1001, Article 9. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020R1001

**7. Five-year spend window before an investment is deemed discontinued.** FACT: "the project proponent has not spent the total amount of the revenues from the Modernisation Fund disbursed to the investment within five years from the date of the relevant disbursement decision of the Commission." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2020/1001, Article 10(1)(b). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020R1001

**8. Record-retention duty on project proponents, contractors, and subcontractors.** FACT: "beneficiary Member States, project proponents and scheme managing authorities, contractors and subcontractors who have received the resources from the Modernisation Fund shall keep available, for a period of five years following the last payment in respect of any project or scheme, all supporting documents and information regarding the payment or expenditure made." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2020/1001, Article 16(5). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020R1001

*Operational implication:* a workspace acting as a project proponent, scheme managing authority, contractor, or subcontractor on a Fund-financed investment must keep the supporting documents and payment/expenditure information for five years following the last payment on that project or scheme.

**9. Protection of the Fund's financial interests, including penalties.** FACT: "Beneficiary Member States shall take appropriate measures to ensure that, where activities financed under this Regulation are implemented, the financial interests of the Modernisation Fund are protected by the application of preventive measures against fraud, corruption and any other illegal activities, by effective checks and, if irregularities are detected, by the recovery of the amounts unduly paid and, where appropriate, by effective, proportionate and dissuasive administrative and financial penalties." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2020/1001, Article 16(6). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020R1001

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this duty to apply preventive measures and, where appropriate, administrative and financial penalties runs to the beneficiary Member State; whether it flows down contractually to a workspace acting as a contractor or subcontractor on the investment is a fact-specific question outside this brief's scope.

**10. Publicity duty toward final recipients.** FACT: "The beneficiary Member States shall ensure that the final recipients of the Modernisation Fund support provide coherent, relevant and targeted information on the Modernisation Fund support received to multiple audiences, including the media and the public." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2020/1001, Article 17(2). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020R1001

*Operational implication:* a workspace that is itself a final recipient of Modernisation Fund support must be prepared to provide coherent, relevant, and targeted information about that support to the media and the public, at the beneficiary Member State's direction.

**11. Entry into force.** FACT: "This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union ." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2020/1001, Article 19. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020R1001

*Qualification support (exceptions).* FACT: "If two or more candidates obtained the same number of votes and as a result, more than three candidates would be elected, the vote shall be resumed, comprising all candidates, except for the candidate(s) who received the highest number of votes, and if appropriate, the second highest number of votes." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2020/1001, Article 11(3). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020R1001

*Qualification support (scope).* FACT: "it has a national or regional scope" *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2020/1001, Article 2(5)(c). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020R1001

**Qualification accounting.** Per-year trajectory: CAPTURED (see metadata.requirement_trajectory: the Fund's 2021-to-2030 period from obligation 1, with the recurring annual/biannual sub-cycles in Section 14; no separate per-provision phase-in beyond that period is stated). Exceptions and carve-outs: CAPTURED above (the Investment Committee's tie-break voting rule carries an unnegated "except for the candidate(s)" clause, Article 11(3)). Scope limits: CAPTURED above (the "scheme" definition's own "it has a national or regional scope" criterion, Article 2(5)(c)).

Obligations surveyed: 11; workspace-adjacent: 5; extracted as FACT: 11.

# 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*No content for this section as of the export date; the captured pool describes a funding-mechanism framework, not the compliance status of any specific product or investment the workspace operates.*

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

FACT: "By 30 November of each year, each beneficiary Member State shall provide the European Investment Bank (EIB) and the Investment Committee with an overview of investments in respect of which it intends to submit investment proposals in the next two calendar years" *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2020/1001, Article 3(1). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020R1001

FACT: "By 30 April, beneficiary Member States shall submit to the Commission an annual report for the preceding year containing information specified in Annex II." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2020/1001, Article 13(1). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020R1001

*Legal Confirmation Required:* both reporting duties above run to a beneficiary Member State reporting to the EIB, Investment Committee, or Commission; no source in this brief's corpus states a registration or reporting duty running directly from a freight-forwarding workspace to any of those bodies, except the record-retention duty already recorded in Section 8 obligation 8.

# 11. Operational System Requirements

*Note: because this instrument's operational duties run mainly to beneficiary Member States, the EIB, and the Investment Committee, "operational system requirements" here means the record-keeping and publicity practice a workspace should maintain only if it holds a project-proponent, contractor, subcontractor, or final-recipient role on a Fund-financed investment.*

*Operational implication:* a workspace with such a role should retain all supporting documents and payment/expenditure information for five years following the last payment on the project or scheme (Section 8, obligation 8), and should be ready to supply the beneficiary Member State with the information needed to satisfy the Article 17 publicity duty (Section 8, obligation 10).

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

FACT: "is exempted from the State aid notification in accordance with Commission Regulation (EU) No 651/2014" *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2020/1001, Article 6(7)(c). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020R1001

*Analytical inference:* this is one of three alternative State aid routes a beneficiary Member State may evidence for a priority-investment proposal (State aid clearance, this block exemption, or a finding that the investment does not constitute State aid at all); it is a Member-State evidentiary requirement, not itself a workspace exemption.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 9 July 2020: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2020/1001 adopted (Done at Brussels, 9 July 2020.).
- 30 November (annually): beneficiary Member States provide the EIB and Investment Committee with an overview of planned investments for the next two calendar years.
- 30 April (annually): beneficiary Member States submit their annual report to the Commission.
- 15 July and 15 December (at the latest, biannually): the Investment Committee meets.
- 15 March (annually): the Investment Committee adopts its final report for the preceding year.
- 2021 to 2030: the Modernisation Fund's own operating period.

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks Commission Regulation (EU) 2021/662, which replaces the Annex to Regulation (EC) No 748/2009 with an updated list of aircraft operators and their administering Member State for EU ETS aviation-activity purposes. It exists to give a workspace operating, or advising, an aircraft operator subject to the EU Emissions Trading System a reference for which Member State administers that operator's ETS obligations, and for the crucial qualifying fact that list inclusion neither creates nor removes the underlying ETS duty.

FACT: "That list aims to reduce the administrative burden on aircraft operators by providing information on which Member State will be regulating a particular aircraft operator." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2021/662, recital 3. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32021R0662

*Analytical inference:* the list is an administrative convenience, not itself the source of an aircraft operator's ETS obligation; Section 8 obligation 2 records the source's own statement of that distinction.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

This is a Commission Regulation directly applicable in all Member States (Article 2), not merely guidance; its sole operative act is replacing the Annex (the operator list) with updated content, but the recitals state substantive qualifying facts that apply to any aircraft operator, including a workspace's own aviation-operator clients or partners.

FACT: "The inclusion of an aircraft operator in the EU ETS is dependent upon the performance of an aviation activity listed in Annex I to Directive 2003/87/EC and is not dependent on the inclusion in the list of aircraft operators established by the Commission on the basis of Article 18a(3) of that Directive." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2021/662, recital 4. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32021R0662

*Operational implication:* an aircraft operator's ETS inclusion turns on whether it performed an aviation activity listed in Annex I to Directive 2003/87/EC, not on whether it appears in this Annex's list; a workspace should not treat absence from the list as evidence that a given aircraft operator has no ETS duty, nor treat presence on the list as itself creating one.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

FACT: "Following the expiry of the transitional period laid down in the Agreement on the withdrawal of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland from the European Union and the European Atomic Energy Community, the United Kingdom has ceased to act as administering Member State for aircraft operators subject to the EU ETS." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2021/662, recital 5. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32021R0662

*Operational implication:* a workspace with UK-linked aircraft-operator clients or partners that were previously administered by the United Kingdom should confirm which EU Member State now administers that operator's ETS compliance, since the UK no longer performs that role.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

*Legal Confirmation Required:* This Regulation's sole operative act (Article 1) is the Commission's own replacement of its Annex; none of the captured text states a duty running from this Regulation directly to a freight-forwarding workspace. A workspace's practical interest is informational: identifying which Member State administers a specific aircraft operator's ETS compliance, which is a fact-specific lookup against the Annex, not a duty this brief can state in the abstract.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

*No content for this section as of the export date; this item's captured pool contains no separate guidance document beyond the instrument's own text, which is treated as the primary source throughout this brief.*

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

*No content for this section as of the export date; the item's export carries no forward_events rows, and the captured pool states no scheduled review or amendment beyond this one-time Annex replacement.*

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does removal from, or absence from, this Annex mean an aircraft operator has no EU ETS obligation?**

FACT: "The inclusion of an aircraft operator in the EU ETS is dependent upon the performance of an aviation activity listed in Annex I to Directive 2003/87/EC and is not dependent on the inclusion in the list of aircraft operators established by the Commission on the basis of Article 18a(3) of that Directive." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2021/662, recital 4. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32021R0662

*Legal Confirmation Required:* No. The recital states plainly that ETS inclusion depends on performing a listed aviation activity, not on list membership. Whether a specific aircraft operator performed such an activity is a fact-specific question requiring counsel or compliance review, independent of this Annex.

**Q2: What changed for aircraft operators previously administered by the United Kingdom?**

FACT: "Following the expiry of the transitional period laid down in the Agreement on the withdrawal of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland from the European Union and the European Atomic Energy Community, the United Kingdom has ceased to act as administering Member State for aircraft operators subject to the EU ETS." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2021/662, recital 5. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32021R0662

# 8. Substantive Requirements
