entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks Directive (EU) 2018/849, which amends three EU waste directives directly relevant to a workspace handling end-of-life vehicles, batteries and accumulators, or waste electrical and electronic equipment (WEEE): Directive 2000/53/EC (end-of-life vehicles), Directive 2006/66/EC (batteries and accumulators), and Directive 2012/19/EU (WEEE). It exists to give a workspace in these verticals a reference for the reporting cycles, the vehicle-materials exemption mechanism, and the Commission's own scheduled review, and to confirm that this Directive's transposition and reporting duties run to Member States, not to the workspace directly.

FACT: "This Directive is addressed to the Member States." *Source: Directive (EU) 2018/849, Article 6. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32018L0849

*Analytical inference:* like the underlying directives it amends, this instrument's direct duties run to Member States; a workspace's exposure comes from the national transposition measures those Member States adopt, and from the specific substantive content this Directive inserts (Section 8).

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

This is a Directive requiring national transposition, not directly applicable EU law; it amends the reporting, delegated-powers, and review mechanisms of the end-of-life-vehicles, batteries, and WEEE directives, and inserts a vehicle-materials exemption power directly relevant to a workspace handling classic or end-of-life vehicles.

FACT: "exempt certain materials and components of vehicles from point (a) of this paragraph if the use of the substances referred to in that point is unavoidable" *Source: Directive (EU) 2018/849, Article 1(1) (amending Directive 2000/53/EC Article 4(2)(b)). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32018L0849

*Operational implication:* a workspace handling end-of-life or classic vehicles containing materials or components covered by Directive 2000/53/EC's hazardous-substance restriction should check whether a Commission delegated act has exempted that specific material or component under this power, since an exemption changes what counts as compliant handling.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

FACT: "By 31 December 2020, the Commission shall review this Directive, and to that end, shall submit a report to the European Parliament and to the Council, accompanied, if appropriate, by a legislative proposal." *Source: Directive (EU) 2018/849, Article 1(8) (inserting Article 10a into Directive 2000/53/EC). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32018L0849

*Operational implication:* the Commission's own review of Directive 2000/53/EC was due by 31 December 2020; a workspace tracking end-of-life-vehicle rules should watch for the resulting report and any legislative proposal it produced (Section 6).

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

*Legal Confirmation Required:* This Directive's transposition duty (Article 4), reporting duties (Section 8), and delegation-of-power mechanism run to Member States and the Commission; none of the captured text states a duty running directly to a workspace handling end-of-life vehicles, batteries, or WEEE. A workspace's actual compliance exposure comes from the national transposition measures its own Member State adopted to implement this Directive, which is a fact-specific question outside this brief's scope.

FACT: "Member States shall bring into force the laws, regulations and administrative provisions necessary to comply with this Directive by 5 July 2020." *Source: Directive (EU) 2018/849, Article 4(1). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32018L0849

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

*No content for this section as of the export date; this item's captured pool contains no separate guidance document beyond the instrument's own text, which is treated as the primary source throughout this brief.*

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

1. **31 December 2020: Commission review of Directive 2000/53/EC (end-of-life vehicles).** FACT: "By 31 December 2020, the Commission shall review this Directive, and to that end, shall submit a report to the European Parliament and to the Council, accompanied, if appropriate, by a legislative proposal." *Source: Directive (EU) 2018/849, Article 1(8) (inserting Article 10a into Directive 2000/53/EC). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32018L0849

*Operational implication:* a workspace handling end-of-life vehicles should check whether the Commission's report under this review, and any legislative proposal it produced, has since changed the substantive requirements this brief records in Section 8.

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does this Directive create a direct compliance duty on a freight-forwarding workspace?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* No source in this brief's corpus states a duty running from this Directive to a freight forwarder directly; its transposition and reporting duties run to Member States (Section 8). A workspace's exposure comes from its own Member State's national transposition measures, a fact-specific question requiring counsel review.

**Q2: Can a vehicle material or component be exempted from the hazardous-substance restriction?**

FACT: "exempt certain materials and components of vehicles from point (a) of this paragraph if the use of the substances referred to in that point is unavoidable" *Source: Directive (EU) 2018/849, Article 1(1) (amending Directive 2000/53/EC Article 4(2)(b)). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32018L0849

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the Commission may adopt a delegated act exempting a specific material or component if the use of the restricted substance is unavoidable; whether a specific material or component a workspace handles has actually been exempted requires checking the current delegated-act record, not just this enabling power.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: this instrument's transposition and reporting duties run to Member States and the Commission; the vehicle-materials exemption power (obligation 9) and the small-establishment simplification (obligation 10) are the provisions most directly relevant to a workspace handling end-of-life vehicles, batteries, or WEEE.*

**1. Transposition deadline.** FACT: "Member States shall bring into force the laws, regulations and administrative provisions necessary to comply with this Directive by 5 July 2020." *Source: Directive (EU) 2018/849, Article 4(1). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32018L0849

**2. Communication of national transposition measures.** FACT: "Member States shall communicate to the Commission the text of the main measures of national law which they adopt in the field covered by this Directive." *Source: Directive (EU) 2018/849, Article 4(2). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32018L0849

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this duty runs from a Member State to the Commission; it does not itself create a duty running to a freight-forwarding workspace.

**3. Entry into force.** FACT: "This Directive shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union ." *Source: Directive (EU) 2018/849, Article 5. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32018L0849

**4. Addressees.** FACT: "This Directive is addressed to the Member States." *Source: Directive (EU) 2018/849, Article 6. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32018L0849

**5. Annual data-reporting duty (end-of-life vehicles).** FACT: "Member States shall report the data concerning the implementation of Article 7(2) for each calendar year to the Commission. They shall report the data electronically within 18 months of the end of the reporting year for which the data are collected." *Source: Directive (EU) 2018/849, Article 1(6) (inserting Article 9(1a) into Directive 2000/53/EC). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32018L0849

**6. Recurring four-year Commission review of reported data.** FACT: "The report shall be drawn up after the first reporting of the data by the Member States and every four years thereafter." *Source: Directive (EU) 2018/849, Article 1(6) (inserting Article 9(1c) into Directive 2000/53/EC). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32018L0849

**7. Five-year delegation-of-power period.** FACT: "The power to adopt delegated acts referred to in point (b) of Article 4(2) and in Articles 5(5), 6(6) and 8(2) shall be conferred on the Commission for a period of five years from 4 July 2018." *Source: Directive (EU) 2018/849, Article 1(7) (inserting Article 9a(2) into Directive 2000/53/EC). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32018L0849

**8. Article 10a review (forward event).** FACT: "By 31 December 2020, the Commission shall review this Directive, and to that end, shall submit a report to the European Parliament and to the Council, accompanied, if appropriate, by a legislative proposal." *Source: Directive (EU) 2018/849, Article 1(8) (inserting Article 10a into Directive 2000/53/EC). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32018L0849

**9. Vehicle-materials exemption power.** FACT: "exempt certain materials and components of vehicles from point (a) of this paragraph if the use of the substances referred to in that point is unavoidable" *Source: Directive (EU) 2018/849, Article 1(1) (amending Directive 2000/53/EC Article 4(2)(b)). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32018L0849

**10. Small-establishment permitting/registration simplification.** FACT: "To reduce the regulatory burden on small establishments or undertakings, simplification of the permitting and registration requirements for small establishments or undertakings should be introduced." *Source: Directive (EU) 2018/849, recital 2. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32018L0849

*Operational implication:* a workspace that is itself a small establishment or undertaking handling end-of-life vehicles, batteries, or WEEE (for example, a small dismantling or take-back facility) may see simplified permitting and registration requirements once a Member State transposes this simplification.

**11. Waste-hierarchy economic-incentive mechanism.** FACT: "Member States may make use of economic instruments and other measures to provide incentives for the application of the waste hierarchy, such as those indicated in Annex IVa to Directive 2008/98/EC or other appropriate instruments and measures." *Source: Directive (EU) 2018/849, Article 2(4) (inserting Article 22a into Directive 2006/66/EC). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32018L0849

**Qualification accounting.** Per-year trajectory: CAPTURED (see metadata.requirement_trajectory: the delegation-of-power period from 4 July 2018, the 5 July 2020 transposition deadline, and the 31 December 2020 Commission review, with the recurring 18-month reporting and four-year review sub-cycles noted). Exceptions and carve-outs: CAPTURED above (obligation 9, the vehicle-materials exemption power, "exempt certain materials and components of vehicles..."). Scope limits: No scope limits are stated in Articles 1 to 6.

Obligations surveyed: 11; workspace-adjacent: 5; extracted as FACT: 11.

# 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*No content for this section as of the export date; the captured pool amends the reporting and delegated-powers framework for these three waste streams, not the compliance status of any specific product the workspace handles.*

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

FACT: "Member States shall report the data concerning the implementation of Article 7(2) for each calendar year to the Commission. They shall report the data electronically within 18 months of the end of the reporting year for which the data are collected." *Source: Directive (EU) 2018/849, Article 1(6) (inserting Article 9(1a) into Directive 2000/53/EC). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32018L0849

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this annual data-reporting duty runs to a Member State reporting to the Commission; no source in this brief's corpus states a registration or reporting duty running directly from a freight-forwarding workspace to the Commission under this Directive.

# 11. Operational System Requirements

*Note: because this instrument's operational duties run to Member States and the Commission, "operational system requirements" here means the monitoring practice a workspace in these verticals should maintain, not a technical system this Directive requires the workspace to build.*

*Operational implication:* a workspace handling end-of-life vehicles should monitor the current delegated-act record for vehicle-materials exemptions (Section 8, obligation 9) and the outcome of the Commission's Article 10a review (Section 6), since either could change which materials or components are compliant to handle.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

FACT: "exempt certain materials and components of vehicles from point (a) of this paragraph if the use of the substances referred to in that point is unavoidable" *Source: Directive (EU) 2018/849, Article 1(1) (amending Directive 2000/53/EC Article 4(2)(b)). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32018L0849

*Analytical inference:* this is the only genuine exemption mechanism identified in the captured pool; it is a delegated-act power the Commission may exercise, not a self-executing exemption a workspace can rely on without checking the current delegated-act record.

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

*No content for this section as of the export date; the captured pool is limited to the instrument's own text and states no adjacent industry research or alternative frameworks.*

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 30 May 2018: Directive (EU) 2018/849 adopted (Done at Strasbourg, 30 May 2018.).
- 4 July 2018: five-year delegation-of-power period to the Commission begins.
- 5 July 2020: Member State transposition deadline.
- 31 December 2020: Commission review of Directive 2000/53/EC due, per Article 10a.

*Source for timeline entries: Directive (EU) 2018/849. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32018L0849*

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document analyzes Council Decision (EU) 2019/638 of 15 April 2019 on the position to be taken on behalf of the European Union at the fourteenth meeting of the Conference of the Parties (COP14) to the Basel Convention on the Control of Transboundary Movements of Hazardous Wastes and their Disposal, regarding amendments to Annexes II, VIII and IX of the Convention concerning plastic waste. *Source: Council Decision (EU) 2019/638 of 15 April 2019, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32019D0638.* It is a procedural, position-setting instrument directed at the Council's own negotiating stance, not a rule that itself binds a private freight-forwarding operator. It matters to the workspace because the Annex amendments it supports were expected to reshape the Basel-based waste-shipment control system the Union implements through Regulation (EC) No 1013/2006, the regulation freight forwarders moving plastic waste internationally must observe. FACT: "entered into force in 1992 and was concluded by the Union by means of Council Decision 93/98/EEC ( 1 ) ." *Source: Council Decision (EU) 2019/638 of 15 April 2019, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32019D0638.* *Analytical inference:* this recital is background on the Basel Convention framework itself (in force since 1992), not a statement about this 2019 Decision's own obligations.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "Regulation (EC) No 1013/2006 of the European Parliament and of the Council ( 2 ) implements the Convention and Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) Council Decision C(2001)107/FINAL concerning the revision of Decision C(92)39/FINAL on the control of transboundary movements of wastes destined for recovery operations" *Source: Council Decision (EU) 2019/638 of 15 April 2019, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32019D0638.* *Per the workspace's reading:* Regulation (EC) No 1013/2006 is the Union instrument that actually governs waste shipments (including plastic waste) for operators moving such cargo; this Decision is one procedural step toward amending the Basel Convention Annexes that regulation implements, so a freight forwarder's practical exposure runs through Regulation 1013/2006 rather than through this Decision directly. FACT: "those amendments will be binding on the Union and are capable of decisively influencing the content of Union law, namely Regulation (EC) No 1013/2006" *Source: Council Decision (EU) 2019/638 of 15 April 2019, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32019D0638.* *Operational implication:* once adopted, the Annex II/VIII/IX amendments this Decision supports will feed directly into how Regulation 1013/2006 classifies and controls plastic waste shipments, which is the workspace-facing consequence of an otherwise internal Council position.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

**MONITORING.** FACT: "the Conference of the Parties is expected to consider and adopt, as required, amendments to the Annexes to the Convention." *Source: Council Decision (EU) 2019/638 of 15 April 2019, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32019D0638.* *Operational implication:* a workspace moving plastic waste (hazardous or non-hazardous) internationally should track whether the fourteenth meeting of the Conference of the Parties in fact adopted the supported amendments, since this captured text states only the Union's proposed position going into that meeting, not the meeting's outcome. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the Annex II, VIII and IX amendments described in Section 8 were actually adopted at the fourteenth meeting and subsequently transposed into Regulation (EC) No 1013/2006 is outside this brief's captured corpus and requires direct confirmation against the Convention's own amendment record.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this Decision's own duty holders are the Council and the Union's representatives at the Conference of the Parties; the captured text names no obligation running to a private freight forwarder, carrier, or logistics intermediary. *Analytical inference:* a workspace's practical position in this chain is indirect, through whichever future amendment to Regulation (EC) No 1013/2006 eventually implements the supported Annex changes, not through this Decision itself.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: "Regulation (EC) No 1013/2006 of the European Parliament and of the Council ( 2 ) implements the Convention and Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) Council Decision C(2001)107/FINAL concerning the revision of Decision C(92)39/FINAL on the control of transboundary movements of wastes destined for recovery operations" *Source: Council Decision (EU) 2019/638 of 15 April 2019, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32019D0638.* *Per the workspace's reading:* this recital identifies the controlling implementing instrument (Regulation 1013/2006) and the parallel OECD Council Decision framework, both of which sit between this position-setting Decision and any eventual change reaching a freight forwarder's own compliance obligations.

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

FACT: "the Conference of the Parties is expected to consider and adopt, as required, amendments to the Annexes to the Convention." *Source: Council Decision (EU) 2019/638 of 15 April 2019, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32019D0638.* *Operational implication:* the fourteenth meeting of the Conference of the Parties is the near-term event a workspace tracking Basel Convention plastic-waste controls should watch; this Decision fixes the Union's proposed position ahead of that meeting, described in full in Section 8.

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does this Decision itself create an obligation a freight forwarder must comply with?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* No obligation running to a private operator is stated in the captured text; see Section 4.

**Q2: Were the Annex II, VIII and IX amendments described in Section 8 actually adopted at the fourteenth meeting of the Conference of the Parties?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the captured text states only the Union's proposed position ahead of that meeting (Section 8); whether the meeting adopted the amendments as proposed, in an amended form, or not at all is outside this brief's corpus.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: this is a procedural, position-setting Council Decision, not a directly binding regulatory instrument. "Substantive requirements" here means the position commitments the Decision records for the Union's own negotiators, plus the operational implications those commitments carry for a freight forwarder as a future subject of whatever amendment to Regulation (EC) No 1013/2006 eventually implements them.*

**1. Overall negotiating position.** FACT: "shall be to support the adoption of the amendments to Annexes II, VIII and IX to the Convention to add and revise entries concerning plastic waste, subject to the following considerations:" *Source: Council Decision (EU) 2019/638 of 15 April 2019, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32019D0638.*

**2. Support for a new non-hazardous plastic waste entry in Annex II.** FACT: "the Union supports the amendments proposed by Norway to add a new entry for non-hazardous plastic waste" *Source: Council Decision (EU) 2019/638 of 15 April 2019, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32019D0638.*

**3. Support for a new hazardous plastic waste entry in Annex VIII.** FACT: "the Union supports the amendments proposed by Norway to add a new entry for hazardous plastic waste (which shall be subject to the control system) in Annex VIII to the Convention, provided that it is clarified that that entry also covers mixtures of hazardous plastic waste;" *Source: Council Decision (EU) 2019/638 of 15 April 2019, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32019D0638.*

**4. Support for revising entry B3010 in Annex IX, with a scope-clarification condition.** The Union's supported revision would leave qualifying non-hazardous plastic waste outside the control system "which shall not be subject to the control system, unless such waste contains a material belonging to a category in Annex I to the Convention to an extent causing it to exhibit a hazardous characteristic in Annex III to the Convention" *Source: Council Decision (EU) 2019/638 of 15 April 2019, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32019D0638.*, conditioned on: FACT: "clarifying the scope, so that only non-mixed plastic materials destined for recycling or preparation for reuse, preferably limited to operation R3 in Annex IV to the Convention, are included in the entry;" *Source: Council Decision (EU) 2019/638 of 15 April 2019, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32019D0638.*

**5. A later application date than the Convention's own default.** FACT: "the Union proposes and supports setting an appropriate later date for application of the amendments than the date foreseen in Article 18 of the Convention." *Source: Council Decision (EU) 2019/638 of 15 April 2019, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32019D0638.*

**6. Preserving current controls on intra-Union/EEA non-hazardous plastic waste shipments (jurisdictional scope).** FACT: "the current controls on shipments of non-hazardous plastic waste, including certain mixtures of non-hazardous plastic waste within the Union and the EEA, remain unaffected." *Source: Council Decision (EU) 2019/638 of 15 April 2019, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32019D0638.*

**7. The same preservation stated as the Union's own recital-level position.** FACT: "It is appropriate to maintain the current situation for shipments of non-hazardous plastic waste, including certain mixtures of non-hazardous plastic waste within the Union and the EEA, and therefore not to use the control system stemming from the addition of an entry in Annex II to the Convention for such shipments." *Source: Council Decision (EU) 2019/638 of 15 April 2019, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32019D0638.*

**8. Binding effect once adopted.** FACT: "those amendments will be binding on the Union and are capable of decisively influencing the content of Union law, namely Regulation (EC) No 1013/2006" *Source: Council Decision (EU) 2019/638 of 15 April 2019, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32019D0638.* *Legal Confirmation Required:* no fine, civil penalty, or enforcement mechanism running to any party (state or private) is stated anywhere in the captured text; this recital states only that the adopted amendments will bind the Union and shape Regulation (EC) No 1013/2006's own content.

**9. Decision's own entry into force.** FACT: "This Decision shall enter into force on the date of its adoption." *Source: Council Decision (EU) 2019/638 of 15 April 2019, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32019D0638.*

**Qualification accounting.** Per-year trajectory: No phase-in is stated in Articles 1 to 3. Exceptions and carve-outs: No exceptions are stated in Articles 1 to 3. Scope limits: CAPTURED above (obligation 4, the B3010 scope-clarification condition, and obligation 6, the intra-Union/EEA jurisdictional-scope statement).

Obligations surveyed: 10; workspace-adjacent: 8; extracted as FACT: 9.

# 11. Operational System Requirements

For a workspace moving plastic waste internationally: (1) monitor whether the fourteenth meeting of the Conference of the Parties adopted the Annex II, VIII and IX amendments described in Section 8, and (2) monitor Regulation (EC) No 1013/2006 for the implementing amendment once the Basel Convention text is finalized, since that regulation (not this Decision) is what will actually bind a private operator. *Operational implication:* neither step is triggered by this Decision alone; both depend on events outside its own text.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

FACT: "which shall not be subject to the control system, unless such waste contains a material belonging to a category in Annex I to the Convention to an extent causing it to exhibit a hazardous characteristic in Annex III to the Convention" *Source: Council Decision (EU) 2019/638 of 15 April 2019, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32019D0638.* *Analytical inference:* the practical edge case this creates is a plastic-waste shipment that is nominally "non-hazardous" under entry B3010 but contains a material meeting an Annex I/III hazardous-characteristic threshold, which would pull the shipment back into the control system this Decision otherwise supports keeping it out of.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 1992: The Basel Convention on the Control of Transboundary Movements of Hazardous Wastes and their Disposal enters into force, concluded by the Union via Council Decision 93/98/EEC. *Source: Council Decision (EU) 2019/638 of 15 April 2019, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32019D0638.*
- 15 April 2019: Council Decision (EU) 2019/638 is adopted (from the instrument title). FACT: "Done at Luxembourg, 15 April 2019." *Source: Council Decision (EU) 2019/638 of 15 April 2019, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32019D0638.*

# 15. Sources

- Council Decision (EU) 2019/638 of 15 April 2019, Official Journal of the European Union L 109/19, EUR-Lex (Tier 1, primary binding text). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32019D0638

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document analyzes Commission Decision of 5 November 2021 (2022/C 65/01) instructing the Central Administrator of the European Union Transaction Log (EUTL) to enter changes to the national allocation tables of Belgium, Czechia, Estonia, Greece, France, Croatia, Cyprus, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Portugal, Slovakia and Sweden into the EUTL. *Source: Commission Decision of 5 November 2021 (2022/C 65/01), EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0207(01).* It is an administrative, registry-maintenance act carrying free-allocation table corrections already notified by the twelve named Member States; it is not itself a rule that imposes a new compliance duty on a freight forwarder. This document is scoped to the recitals and operative provision the captured text grounds; the Annex's own installation-by-installation allocation quantities (Section 9) are outside this document's analytical scope given their scale.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/331 lays down the transitional Union-wide rules for harmonised free allocation of emission allowances pursuant to Article 10a of Directive 2003/87/EC for the fourth trading period from 2021 until 2030." *Source: Commission Decision of 5 November 2021 (2022/C 65/01), EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0207(01).* *Per the workspace's reading:* this Decision does not itself create or change the free-allocation framework; it is a downstream, technical step (entering already-notified national allocation table corrections into the registry) inside that framework. For a workspace whose clients operate installations covered by these national allocation tables, a change in free allocation can shift the client's own allowance-purchase cost, which can in turn feed into the pricing of goods the workspace moves on that client's behalf. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any specific workspace client's installation is among the ones whose allocation changed under this Decision requires checking the Annex directly against the client's own installation identity, which this brief does not itemize (Section 9).

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

**MONITORING.** FACT: "Pursuant to Article 23(2) of Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/331, Belgium notified to the Commission, by letter dated 14 October 2021, changes to its national allocation table to provide free allocation of emission allowances to new entrants and to adjust free allocation of emission allowances in incumbent installations." *Source: Commission Decision of 5 November 2021 (2022/C 65/01), EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0207(01).* *Operational implication:* a workspace with clients operating ETS-covered installations in any of the twelve named Member States should confirm, directly against the Annex, whether that client's own installation received a new-entrant or incumbent-adjustment allocation change under this Decision, since a change here can alter the client's near-term allowance cost.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the duty this Decision states runs to the Central Administrator of the European Union Transaction Log, not to any private party. *Analytical inference:* a freight forwarder is not itself a duty holder under this Decision; its relevance to the workspace runs only through a client's installation-level allowance position, which this Decision's Annex updates.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: "Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2019/1842 ( 2 ) lays down rules for the application of Directive 2003/87/EC as regards further arrangements for the adjustments to free allocation of emission allowances due to activity level changes." *Source: Commission Decision of 5 November 2021 (2022/C 65/01), EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0207(01).* FACT: "the Commission instructed the Central Administrator of the European Union Transaction Log to enter the national allocation tables of Belgium, Bulgaria, Czechia, Denmark, Germany, Estonia, Ireland, Greece, Spain, France, Croatia, Italy, Cyprus, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Hungary, the Netherlands, Austria, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovenia, Slovakia, Finland and Sweden into the European Union Transaction Log." *Source: Commission Decision of 5 November 2021 (2022/C 65/01), EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0207(01).* *Per the workspace's reading:* this earlier decision (2021/C 302/01) is the prior registry-entry act this Decision's own twelve-state subset amends; together they show the EUTL's national allocation tables are updated incrementally, state by state, as notifications arrive, not as a single one-time table.

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

*Analytical inference:* because national allocation tables under Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/331 are updated incrementally as Member States notify changes (Section 8), a workspace tracking a specific client's installation should expect further EUTL registry-entry decisions of this same kind for other Member States or later notification rounds within the fourth trading period; the captured text does not itself name a next scheduled decision.

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does this Decision create a new obligation on a freight forwarder?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* No. The duty stated (Section 8) runs to the Central Administrator of the EUTL, not to a private freight-forwarding operator.

**Q2: Which specific installations changed allocation under this Decision?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the Annex lists each affected installation by Member State, installation ID, Union registry ID, installation name and operator name (Section 9); this brief does not itemize those rows, so a workspace with a specific client concern should check the Annex directly.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: this is an administrative, registry-maintenance Decision, not a rulemaking that binds a private party directly. "Substantive requirements" here means the obligations and findings the Decision itself records for the Central Administrator and the Commission, plus the operational implications those carry for a freight forwarder whose clients operate the affected installations.*

**1. Central administrator's registry-entry duty (jurisdictional scope: the twelve named Member States).** FACT: "HAS DECIDED AS FOLLOWS: Sole Article The central administrator shall enter the changes to the national allocation tables of Belgium, Czechia, Estonia, Greece, France, Croatia, Cyprus, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Portugal, Slovakia and Sweden set out in the Annex into the European Union Transaction Log." *Source: Commission Decision of 5 November 2021 (2022/C 65/01), EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0207(01).* FACT: "Done at Brussels, 5 November 2021." *Source: Commission Decision of 5 November 2021 (2022/C 65/01), EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0207(01).* No separate entry-into-force clause is stated in the captured text; the Decision's own date and place of adoption is the only date the text ties to the Decision taking effect.

**2. The underlying free-allocation framework and trading-period window.** FACT: "Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/331 lays down the transitional Union-wide rules for harmonised free allocation of emission allowances pursuant to Article 10a of Directive 2003/87/EC for the fourth trading period from 2021 until 2030." *Source: Commission Decision of 5 November 2021 (2022/C 65/01), EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0207(01).* *Operational implication:* the 2021-2030 fourth trading period is the window within which this and any similar registry-entry decision sits.

**3. The activity-level adjustment mechanism this Decision's notified changes draw on.** FACT: "Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2019/1842 ( 2 ) lays down rules for the application of Directive 2003/87/EC as regards further arrangements for the adjustments to free allocation of emission allowances due to activity level changes." *Source: Commission Decision of 5 November 2021 (2022/C 65/01), EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0207(01).*

**4. The Commission's own compliance finding before deciding.** FACT: "The notified changes to national allocation tables are in accordance with Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/331 and Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2019/1842" *Source: Commission Decision of 5 November 2021 (2022/C 65/01), EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0207(01).*

**5. The per-Member-State notification mechanism (illustrated by Belgium; the other eleven named Member States notified similarly in October 2021, per the recitals).** FACT: "Pursuant to Article 23(2) of Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/331, Belgium notified to the Commission, by letter dated 14 October 2021, changes to its national allocation table to provide free allocation of emission allowances to new entrants and to adjust free allocation of emission allowances in incumbent installations." *Source: Commission Decision of 5 November 2021 (2022/C 65/01), EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0207(01).*

**Qualification accounting.** Per-year trajectory: No phase-in is stated in Article 1 (the Sole Article) of this Decision. Exceptions and carve-outs: No exceptions are stated in Article 1 (the Sole Article) of this Decision. Scope limits: No scope limits are stated in Article 1 (the Sole Article) of this Decision.

Obligations surveyed: 5; workspace-adjacent: 2; extracted as FACT: 5.

# 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

FACT: "ANNEX I National allocation table for the period 2021-2025 pursuant to Article 10a of Directive 2003/87/EC" *Source: Commission Decision of 5 November 2021 (2022/C 65/01), EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0207(01).* *Analytical inference:* the Annex tabulates, per Member State, each affected installation's ID, Union registry ID, installation name, operator name and allocation quantities; given the Annex's scale (over 130,000 characters of tabular data across twelve Member States), this brief does not itemize individual installation rows, and a workspace needing a specific installation's own figures should query the Annex or the Union Registry directly.

# 11. Operational System Requirements

For a workspace whose clients operate ETS-covered installations in Belgium, Czechia, Estonia, Greece, France, Croatia, Cyprus, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Portugal, Slovakia or Sweden: confirm directly against this Decision's Annex whether the specific client installation received a new-entrant or incumbent-adjustment allocation change, since the Annex (Section 9) is the only source of installation-level figures and this brief does not restate them.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 5 November 2021: Commission Decision (2022/C 65/01) is adopted. FACT: "Done at Brussels, 5 November 2021." *Source: Commission Decision of 5 November 2021 (2022/C 65/01), EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0207(01).*

# 15. Sources

- Commission Decision of 5 November 2021 instructing the Central Administrator of the European Union Transaction Log to enter changes to the national allocation tables of Belgium, Czechia, Estonia, Greece, France, Croatia, Cyprus, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Portugal, Slovakia and Sweden into the European Union Transaction Log (2022/C 65/01), Official Journal of the European Union C 65/1, EUR-Lex (Tier 1, primary binding text). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0207(01)

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document analyzes The Climate Change Levy (Combined Heat and Power Stations) Prescribed Conditions and Efficiency Percentages Regulations 2001 (S.I. 2001/1140), the UK statutory instrument prescribing the conditions and efficiency thresholds a combined heat and power (CHP) station must meet to qualify for a Climate Change Levy (CCL) full-exemption certificate or partial levy exemption. *Source: The Climate Change Levy (Combined Heat and Power Stations) Prescribed Conditions and Efficiency Percentages Regulations 2001 (S.I. 2001/1140), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2001/1140.* It does not itself regulate freight movement. *Legal Confirmation Required:* on its own terms it applies to combined heat and power station operators, not to a freight forwarder. For a workspace whose clients operate CHP stations in Great Britain (an energy source many industrial and warehousing sites rely on), whether a station meets these conditions determines the client's own CCL exposure on its energy supply, which can feed into the pricing of goods and shipment volumes the workspace handles on that client's behalf.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "The Treasury, in exercise of the powers conferred on them by section 30 of and paragraphs 15(4)(a), 16, 146(1), 146(7), 148(4) and 149 of Schedule 6 to the Finance Act 2000" *Source: The Climate Change Levy (Combined Heat and Power Stations) Prescribed Conditions and Efficiency Percentages Regulations 2001 (S.I. 2001/1140), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2001/1140.* *Per the workspace's reading:* this is a Treasury-made statutory instrument under the Finance Act 2000's Climate Change Levy schedule, not a duty running to a freight forwarder directly. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any workspace-controlled facility (a warehouse or distribution centre with an on-site CHP plant) is itself a "combined heat and power station" within the meaning of this instrument, or whether the relevant CHP station belongs only to a client whose energy costs the workspace does not control.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

**MONITORING.** FACT: "Until 1st April 2005, the threshold efficiency percentage for a combined heat and power station which was solely operating a steam engine or steam turbine on 1st November 2000 is 15 per cent." *Source: The Climate Change Levy (Combined Heat and Power Stations) Prescribed Conditions and Efficiency Percentages Regulations 2001 (S.I. 2001/1140), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2001/1140.* *Operational implication:* a workspace tracking a client's CHP-station CCL exemption status should confirm, ahead of any transitional deadline in Section 8, whether that station relies on the lower transitional threshold or the general 20 per cent threshold, since the transitional condition ceases to be available after the stated date.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the duty holder under this instrument is the operator of the combined heat and power station applying for or relying on the full or partial CCL exemption; the captured text names no obligation running to a freight forwarder, carrier, or logistics intermediary. *Analytical inference:* a workspace's own exposure runs only through a client's CHP-station exemption status, not through a duty this instrument places on the workspace itself.

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

FACT: "until 1st April 2005, the total power capacity of the station, as stated in its CHPQA certificate, is less than 2 megawatts of electricity." and FACT: "Until 1st April 2005, the threshold efficiency percentage for a combined heat and power station which was solely operating a steam engine or steam turbine on 1st November 2000 is 15 per cent." *Source: The Climate Change Levy (Combined Heat and Power Stations) Prescribed Conditions and Efficiency Percentages Regulations 2001 (S.I. 2001/1140), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2001/1140.* *Operational implication:* both transitional provisions in Section 8 (obligations 3 and 5) share the same 1st April 2005 cutoff; a workspace with a client relying on either transitional route should have already confirmed, by that date, whether the client's station met the general (non-transitional) conditions instead.

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does this instrument create an obligation a freight forwarder must comply with?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* No. The duty holder is the CHP station operator (Section 4); the captured text names no obligation running to a private freight-forwarding operator.

**Q2: Which of the two efficiency-threshold routes (general or transitional) applies to a given client's CHP station?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this depends on the station's own CHPQA certificate and, for the transitional route, whether it was solely operating a steam engine or steam turbine on 1st November 2000 (Section 8, obligation 5); a workspace cannot determine this from the regulation text alone.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

**1. Commencement.** FACT: "Made 22nd March 2001" and "shall come into force on the day after they are made." *Source: The Climate Change Levy (Combined Heat and Power Stations) Prescribed Conditions and Efficiency Percentages Regulations 2001 (S.I. 2001/1140), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2001/1140.*

**Jurisdictional scope.** FACT: "the second of which only applies to small stations which have been assessed in accordance with the simplified arrangements under the Standard, and are therefore not required to calculate the quantifying power output." *Source: The Climate Change Levy (Combined Heat and Power Stations) Prescribed Conditions and Efficiency Percentages Regulations 2001 (S.I. 2001/1140), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2001/1140.* *Analytical inference:* every condition below applies to the combined heat and power station itself (through its operator), not to a freight forwarder moving goods to or from the site.

**2. First condition for a full-exemption certificate: CHPQA assessment.** FACT: "The first condition is that a combined heat and power station has been assessed in accordance with CHPQA." *Source: The Climate Change Levy (Combined Heat and Power Stations) Prescribed Conditions and Efficiency Percentages Regulations 2001 (S.I. 2001/1140), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2001/1140.*

**3. Second condition, route (a): qualifying power output equals total power output.** FACT: "the qualifying power output of the station, as stated in its CHPQA certificate, is equal to its total power output as so stated" *Source: The Climate Change Levy (Combined Heat and Power Stations) Prescribed Conditions and Efficiency Percentages Regulations 2001 (S.I. 2001/1140), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2001/1140.*

**4. Second condition, route (b): transitional small-station capacity threshold (until 1st April 2005).** FACT: "until 1st April 2005, the total power capacity of the station, as stated in its CHPQA certificate, is less than 2 megawatts of electricity." *Source: The Climate Change Levy (Combined Heat and Power Stations) Prescribed Conditions and Efficiency Percentages Regulations 2001 (S.I. 2001/1140), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2001/1140.*, conditioned on: FACT: "The condition specified in sub-paragraph (3)(b) is only to be treated as being satisfied if the station has been assessed for the purposes of paragraph (2) in accordance with the simplified arrangements for small scale stations (which do not require the calculation of quantifying power output)." *Source: The Climate Change Levy (Combined Heat and Power Stations) Prescribed Conditions and Efficiency Percentages Regulations 2001 (S.I. 2001/1140), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2001/1140.*

**5. General threshold efficiency percentage.** FACT: "the threshold efficiency percentage for a combined heat and power station for the purposes of paragraph 15 of the Act is 20 per cent." *Source: The Climate Change Levy (Combined Heat and Power Stations) Prescribed Conditions and Efficiency Percentages Regulations 2001 (S.I. 2001/1140), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2001/1140.*

**6. Transitional threshold efficiency percentage (until 1st April 2005) for steam-engine or steam-turbine stations.** FACT: "Until 1st April 2005, the threshold efficiency percentage for a combined heat and power station which was solely operating a steam engine or steam turbine on 1st November 2000 is 15 per cent." *Source: The Climate Change Levy (Combined Heat and Power Stations) Prescribed Conditions and Efficiency Percentages Regulations 2001 (S.I. 2001/1140), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2001/1140.*

**7. Method of calculating the efficiency percentage.** FACT: "The efficiency percentage of a combined heat and power station for the purposes of paragraph 15 of the Act is calculated by multiplying by 100 the fraction" -- (a) whose numerator is the station's total annual power output measured in megawatt hours, and (b) whose denominator is the station's total annual fuel energy input measured in megawatt hours, as stated in its CHPQA certificate. *Source: The Climate Change Levy (Combined Heat and Power Stations) Prescribed Conditions and Efficiency Percentages Regulations 2001 (S.I. 2001/1140), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2001/1140.*

**8. Limit on levy-exempt supplies from a partly-exempt station.** FACT: "supplies of electricity from a partly exempt combined heat and power station exempt from levy if specified limit not exceeded" *Source: The Climate Change Levy (Combined Heat and Power Stations) Prescribed Conditions and Efficiency Percentages Regulations 2001 (S.I. 2001/1140), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2001/1140.* FACT: "That limit, in respect of a combined heat and power station, is the Qualifying Power Output for that station as stated in its CHPQA certificate." *Source: The Climate Change Levy (Combined Heat and Power Stations) Prescribed Conditions and Efficiency Percentages Regulations 2001 (S.I. 2001/1140), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2001/1140.*

**9. What counts toward that limit.** FACT: "any supplies made by a station to a utility or for domestic or non-business charity use shall be disregarded" but FACT: "the electrical equivalent of any mechanical output of the station produced otherwise than for the purpose of electricity generation shall be included." *Source: The Climate Change Levy (Combined Heat and Power Stations) Prescribed Conditions and Efficiency Percentages Regulations 2001 (S.I. 2001/1140), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2001/1140.*

**10. Calculating the electrical equivalent of mechanical output.** FACT: "the electrical equivalent of any mechanical output of a station is derived by multiplying that output by 1.05." *Source: The Climate Change Levy (Combined Heat and Power Stations) Prescribed Conditions and Efficiency Percentages Regulations 2001 (S.I. 2001/1140), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2001/1140.*

**Qualification accounting.** Per-year trajectory: CAPTURED via metadata.requirement_trajectory (the transitional 15 per cent / under-2-megawatt route available only until 1st April 2005, after which the general 20 per cent threshold and the ordinary qualifying-power-output condition apply). Exceptions and carve-outs: CAPTURED above (obligation 8, the partly-exempt-station levy exemption up to the specified limit). Scope limits: No scope limits are stated in Sections 1 to 5 of this instrument.

Obligations surveyed: 10; workspace-adjacent: 9; extracted as FACT: 9.

# 11. Operational System Requirements

For a workspace tracking a client's CHP-station CCL exemption: (1) confirm which efficiency-threshold route the station relies on (general 20 per cent or, until 1st April 2005, the transitional 15 per cent route for qualifying steam-engine/turbine stations), (2) confirm the station's CHPQA certificate states the qualifying power output and total power output figures the conditions in Section 8 turn on, and (3) confirm which supplies are disregarded or included when calculating the partly-exempt-station limit (Section 8, obligations 8 and 9). *Operational implication:* none of these is a system the workspace itself builds; each is a fact to verify against the client's own CHPQA certificate.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

FACT: "supplies of electricity from a partly exempt combined heat and power station exempt from levy if specified limit not exceeded" *Source: The Climate Change Levy (Combined Heat and Power Stations) Prescribed Conditions and Efficiency Percentages Regulations 2001 (S.I. 2001/1140), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2001/1140.* *Analytical inference:* the edge case this creates is a CHP station that is only "partly exempt" (its output exceeds the Qualifying Power Output limit in Section 8, obligation 8); supplies beyond that limit are not levy-exempt even though the station otherwise holds a full-exemption certificate.

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

FACT: "the second of which only applies to small stations which have been assessed in accordance with the simplified arrangements under the Standard, and are therefore not required to calculate the quantifying power output." *Source: The Climate Change Levy (Combined Heat and Power Stations) Prescribed Conditions and Efficiency Percentages Regulations 2001 (S.I. 2001/1140), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2001/1140.* *Analytical inference:* this Explanatory Note confirms the simplified, small-station assessment route (Section 8, obligation 4) exists specifically so small CHP stations are not required to calculate the more burdensome qualifying power output figure the general route (obligation 3) needs.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 22nd March 2001: The Regulations are made. FACT: "Made 22nd March 2001" *Source: The Climate Change Levy (Combined Heat and Power Stations) Prescribed Conditions and Efficiency Percentages Regulations 2001 (S.I. 2001/1140), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2001/1140.*
- 1st April 2005: The transitional small-station capacity threshold (Section 8, obligation 4) and the transitional 15 per cent efficiency threshold for qualifying steam-engine or steam-turbine stations (Section 8, obligation 6) cease to be available. *Source: The Climate Change Levy (Combined Heat and Power Stations) Prescribed Conditions and Efficiency Percentages Regulations 2001 (S.I. 2001/1140), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2001/1140.*

# 15. Sources

- The Climate Change Levy (Combined Heat and Power Stations) Prescribed Conditions and Efficiency Percentages Regulations 2001 (S.I. 2001/1140), UK Government, legislation.gov.uk (Tier 1, primary binding text). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2001/1140

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document analyzes The Energy Savings Opportunity Scheme (Amendment) Regulations 2026 (S.I. 2026/701), which amend the Energy Savings Opportunity Scheme Regulations 2014 (the mandatory UK energy-audit scheme for large undertakings, "ESOS"). *Source: The Energy Savings Opportunity Scheme (Amendment) Regulations 2026 (S.I. 2026/701), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/701.* FACT: "These Regulations make changes in relation to the Energy Savings Opportunity Scheme" *Source: The Energy Savings Opportunity Scheme (Amendment) Regulations 2026 (S.I. 2026/701), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/701.* Unlike a downstream client-facing framework, ESOS applies directly to any "large undertaking" as defined by the 2014 Regulations, which can include a freight-forwarding workspace itself if it meets ESOS's own size thresholds, not only a workspace's energy-intensive clients. This document is scoped to the amendments the captured text and its own Explanatory Note ground.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "The Secretary of State makes these Regulations in exercise of the powers conferred by sections 254 to 260 and 263 of the Energy Act 2023" *Source: The Energy Savings Opportunity Scheme (Amendment) Regulations 2026 (S.I. 2026/701), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/701.* *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the workspace itself meets the 2014 Regulations' own "large undertaking" definition (unchanged by this amending instrument) is the threshold question that determines whether any of the amendments in Section 8 apply to the workspace directly, or only to energy-intensive clients whose ESOS status the workspace tracks indirectly. *Operational implication:* either way, a workspace should confirm which of the compliance routes in Section 8 (general ESOS assessment, ISO 50001 deemed compliance, or the new zero-energy-consumption route) applies to its own or its client's position.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

**ACTION REQUIRED.** FACT: "These Regulations come into force on 22nd July 2026." *Source: The Energy Savings Opportunity Scheme (Amendment) Regulations 2026 (S.I. 2026/701), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/701.* *Operational implication:* a workspace that is itself an ESOS participant, or that tracks a client's ESOS status, should confirm before this date whether any of the amendments in Section 8 change its own compliance route, evidence-pack contents, or notification obligations.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the duty holders under the amended 2014 Regulations are "responsible undertakings" and "participants" as those terms are defined there (unchanged by this instrument); whether the workspace itself falls within either class depends on facts (headcount, turnover, balance sheet, and corporate group structure) outside this brief's captured corpus.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: "Part 6 of the 2014 Regulations is amended to remove Display Energy Certificates and Green Deal Assessments as alternative routes to compliance." *Source: The Energy Savings Opportunity Scheme (Amendment) Regulations 2026 (S.I. 2026/701), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/701.* *Per the workspace's reading:* this narrows the routes to ESOS compliance available under the 2014 Regulations as of the commencement date in Section 8; a workspace or client that previously relied on a Display Energy Certificate or Green Deal Assessment route should confirm which of the remaining routes (general assessment, ISO 50001, or zero energy consumption) it now falls under.

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

FACT: "for compliance periods ending on or after 5th December 2027, an ESOS progress update during the period starting on the three year anniversary of the first day of the relevant compliance period and ending on the day before the four year anniversary of the first day of the relevant compliance period" *Source: The Energy Savings Opportunity Scheme (Amendment) Regulations 2026 (S.I. 2026/701), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/701.* *Operational implication:* a workspace or client with an ESOS compliance period ending on or after 5th December 2027 should expect this new "final progress update" reporting obligation, in addition to the standard reporting the 2014 Regulations already require.

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does the workspace itself qualify as a "large undertaking" or "responsible undertaking" under ESOS?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this depends on facts (employee count, turnover, balance sheet total, corporate group structure) not stated in this instrument's own text.

**Q2: Which compliance route applies where a client's energy consumption is fully, partly, or not at all covered by ISO 50001 certification?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* Section 8 (obligation 10) states the general rule; the specific facts of a client's own ISO 50001 certification scope determine which duties in Chapter 3 of Part 4 of the 2014 Regulations still apply to the uncertified portion.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: this is an amending instrument; "substantive requirements" here means the duties and deemed-compliance routes it inserts into, or changes in, the Energy Savings Opportunity Scheme Regulations 2014.*

**1. Commencement.** FACT: "Made 23rd June 2026" and "Laid before Parliament 1st July 2026" and "These Regulations come into force on 22nd July 2026." *Source: The Energy Savings Opportunity Scheme (Amendment) Regulations 2026 (S.I. 2026/701), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/701.*

**2. Extent (jurisdictional scope).** FACT: "These Regulations extend to England and Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland." *Source: The Energy Savings Opportunity Scheme (Amendment) Regulations 2026 (S.I. 2026/701), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/701.* *Analytical inference:* this instrument, and the ESOS duties it amends, applies across the whole of the United Kingdom, not only in England and Wales.

**3. Expanded insolvency exclusion.** FACT: "Chapter 1 of Part 3 of the 2014 Regulations is amended to expand the exclusion for insolvent undertakings to include any undertakings subject to insolvency proceedings during the period starting with the qualification date and ending with the compliance date." *Source: The Energy Savings Opportunity Scheme (Amendment) Regulations 2026 (S.I. 2026/701), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/701.*

**4. Group-undertaking insolvency carve-out.** FACT: "This exclusion also extends to any group undertakings in respect of which the large undertaking in that group is subject to insolvency procedures, unless there is another large undertaking in that group which is solvent." *Source: The Energy Savings Opportunity Scheme (Amendment) Regulations 2026 (S.I. 2026/701), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/701.*

**5. Lead assessor's seven-day notification duty.** FACT: "Chapter 1 of Part 4 of the 2014 Regulations is amended to require lead assessors to notify their approval body of the completion of an ESOS assessment and to provide that approval body with contact details for the responsible undertaking." *Source: The Energy Savings Opportunity Scheme (Amendment) Regulations 2026 (S.I. 2026/701), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/701.* The operative provision states, verbatim: "Within the period of seven days beginning with the day after the day on which a notification is made under paragraph (2)(b), the lead assessor must" notify their approval body of the completion of the ESOS assessment, including the date of completion. *Source: The Energy Savings Opportunity Scheme (Amendment) Regulations 2026 (S.I. 2026/701), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/701.*

**6. Standardization of energy-consumption and energy-savings estimates to kilowatt hours.** FACT: "This Chapter is also amended to require all estimates of energy consumption or energy savings to be calculated in kWh." *Source: The Energy Savings Opportunity Scheme (Amendment) Regulations 2026 (S.I. 2026/701), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/701.*

**7. New ESOS action plan review duty.** FACT: "A new Chapter 3B is inserted into Part 4 of the 2014 Regulations, which requires participants to complete a review of the action plan measures identified in the previous compliance period and report where these were not met." *Source: The Energy Savings Opportunity Scheme (Amendment) Regulations 2026 (S.I. 2026/701), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/701.*

**8. Measures-taken-and-estimate duty on the previous compliance period.** FACT: "Regulation 27B of the 2014 Regulations is moved to fall under Chapter 3B of Part 4 and is amended so that responsible undertakings must identify all measures taken, and estimate the energy savings achieved by these measures, since the previous compliance date." *Source: The Energy Savings Opportunity Scheme (Amendment) Regulations 2026 (S.I. 2026/701), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/701.*

**9. Removal of Display Energy Certificate and Green Deal Assessment routes.** FACT: "Part 6 of the 2014 Regulations is amended to remove Display Energy Certificates and Green Deal Assessments as alternative routes to compliance." *Source: The Energy Savings Opportunity Scheme (Amendment) Regulations 2026 (S.I. 2026/701), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/701.*

**10. ISO 50001 deemed-compliance route, and its scope limit for partial certification.** FACT: "Where a participant’s total energy consumption or significant energy consumption (that is, the areas of energy consumption comprising 95% or more of that participant’s energy consumption) is compliant with ISO 50001 certification, they are deemed to have complied with the duty to appoint a lead assessor, carry out an ESOS audit and produce an ESOS report." *Source: The Energy Savings Opportunity Scheme (Amendment) Regulations 2026 (S.I. 2026/701), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/701.* FACT: "This regulation does not apply to a participant that is deemed to have complied with this Chapter by virtue of regulation 33A." *Source: The Energy Savings Opportunity Scheme (Amendment) Regulations 2026 (S.I. 2026/701), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/701.*

**11. New zero-energy-consumption exemption route.** FACT: "An additional route for compliance is inserted for undertakings whose energy consumption is zero kWh. Those undertakings are exempt from the requirement to complete an ESOS assessment, as well as the duties under Chapters 2A to 4 of Part 4 and Part 6A of the 2014 Regulations." *Source: The Energy Savings Opportunity Scheme (Amendment) Regulations 2026 (S.I. 2026/701), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/701.*

**12. Final progress update for later compliance periods.** FACT: "for compliance periods ending on or after 5th December 2027, an ESOS progress update during the period starting on the three year anniversary of the first day of the relevant compliance period and ending on the day before the four year anniversary of the first day of the relevant compliance period" *Source: The Energy Savings Opportunity Scheme (Amendment) Regulations 2026 (S.I. 2026/701), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/701.*

**Qualification accounting.** Per-year trajectory: CAPTURED via metadata.requirement_trajectory (the new final-progress-update duty attaches only to compliance periods ending on or after 5th December 2027; no earlier phase-in step is stated). Exceptions and carve-outs: CAPTURED above (obligation 11, the zero-energy-consumption exemption). Scope limits: CAPTURED above (obligation 10, the scope carve-out for a participant deemed to have complied by virtue of regulation 33A).

Obligations surveyed: 10; workspace-adjacent: 10; extracted as FACT: 10.

# 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a specific workspace-controlled facility's energy consumption is zero kWh (Section 8, obligation 11), fully or partly ISO 50001 certified (obligation 10), or neither, determines which compliance route it falls under; this brief's captured text does not itemize any specific facility.

# 11. Operational System Requirements

For a workspace that is itself an ESOS participant, or that tracks a client's ESOS status: (1) confirm which compliance route applies (general assessment, ISO 50001 deemed compliance, or the new zero-energy-consumption route), (2) if relying on the ISO 50001 route, confirm whether certification covers total, significant, or only partial energy consumption, since the uncertified portion still falls under Chapter 3 duties, and (3) if the current or next compliance period ends on or after 5th December 2027, calendar the new final-progress-update window (Section 6). *Operational implication:* none of these is triggered automatically; each depends on facts specific to the workspace's or client's own energy consumption and certification status.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

FACT: "This regulation does not apply to a participant that is deemed to have complied with this Chapter by virtue of regulation 33A." *Source: The Energy Savings Opportunity Scheme (Amendment) Regulations 2026 (S.I. 2026/701), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/701.* FACT: "An additional route for compliance is inserted for undertakings whose energy consumption is zero kWh. Those undertakings are exempt from the requirement to complete an ESOS assessment, as well as the duties under Chapters 2A to 4 of Part 4 and Part 6A of the 2014 Regulations." *Source: The Energy Savings Opportunity Scheme (Amendment) Regulations 2026 (S.I. 2026/701), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/701.* *Analytical inference:* a participant relying on the zero-energy-consumption route (regulation 33A) is exempted from several duties across Chapters 2A to 4 and Part 6A of the 2014 Regulations at once, which is a broader carve-out than the ISO 50001 route's own partial-certification limit.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 23rd June 2026: The Regulations are made. FACT: "Made 23rd June 2026" *Source: The Energy Savings Opportunity Scheme (Amendment) Regulations 2026 (S.I. 2026/701), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/701.*
- 1st July 2026: The Regulations are laid before Parliament. FACT: "Laid before Parliament 1st July 2026" *Source: The Energy Savings Opportunity Scheme (Amendment) Regulations 2026 (S.I. 2026/701), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/701.*
- 22nd July 2026: The Regulations come into force. FACT: "These Regulations come into force on 22nd July 2026." *Source: The Energy Savings Opportunity Scheme (Amendment) Regulations 2026 (S.I. 2026/701), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/701.*
- 5th December 2027: The new final-progress-update duty (Section 8, obligation 12) begins to apply to compliance periods ending on or after this date. FACT: "for compliance periods ending on or after 5th December 2027, an ESOS progress update during the period starting on the three year anniversary of the first day of the relevant compliance period and ending on the day before the four year anniversary of the first day of the relevant compliance period" *Source: The Energy Savings Opportunity Scheme (Amendment) Regulations 2026 (S.I. 2026/701), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/701.*

# 15. Sources

- The Energy Savings Opportunity Scheme (Amendment) Regulations 2026 (S.I. 2026/701), UK Government, legislation.gov.uk (Tier 1, primary binding text). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/701
