entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document analyzes Council Decision of 2 December 2005 (2006/61/EC) on the conclusion, on behalf of the European Community, of the UN-ECE Protocol on Pollutant Release and Transfer Registers (the "Protocol"), annexed to the Decision in full. *Source: Council Decision of 2 December 2005 (2006/61/EC), EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32006D0061.* FACT: "HAS DECIDED AS FOLLOWS: Article 1 The UN-ECE Protocol on Pollutant Release and Transfer Registers is hereby approved on behalf of the Community." *Source: Council Decision of 2 December 2005 (2006/61/EC), EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32006D0061.* FACT: "Regulation (EC) No 166/2006 of the European Parliament and the Council of 18 January 2006 concerning the establishment of a European Pollutant Release and Transfer Register ( 3 ) has incorporated the provisions of the Protocol into Community legislation." *Source: Council Decision of 2 December 2005 (2006/61/EC), EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32006D0061.* *Per the workspace's reading:* the Protocol's own facility-level reporting duties are already binding EU law through Regulation (EC) No 166/2006 (the European PRTR Regulation); this Council Decision is the EU's own act of approving the underlying international Protocol, not a separate compliance instrument layered on top of it.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "The objective of this Protocol is to enhance public access to information through the establishment of coherent, integrated, nationwide pollutant release and transfer registers (PRTRs) in accordance with the provisions of this Protocol, which could facilitate public participation in environmental decision-making as well as contribute to the prevention and reduction of pollution of the environment." *Source: Council Decision of 2 December 2005 (2006/61/EC), EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32006D0061.* FACT: "means one or more installations on the same site, or on adjoining sites, that are owned or operated by the same natural or legal person;" *Source: Council Decision of 2 December 2005 (2006/61/EC), EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32006D0061.* *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a specific workspace-operated site (a warehouse, depot, or terminal) is a "facility" carrying out an Annex I activity above the Annex I capacity or employee threshold, and whether it releases or transfers pollutants or waste above the Annex II thresholds (Section 8, obligation 9), determines whether that site's owner or operator is itself a duty holder under the national PRTR system implementing this Protocol.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

**MONITORING.** FACT: "transfers off-site hazardous waste exceeding two tons per year or other waste exceeding 2 000 tons per year, where the Party has opted for waste-specific reporting of transfers pursuant to paragraph 5(d);" *Source: Council Decision of 2 December 2005 (2006/61/EC), EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32006D0061.* *Operational implication:* a workspace operating or contracting a waste-handling or transfer site in a Party State should confirm whether its own off-site hazardous or other waste transfer volumes exceed these thresholds, since exceeding them triggers the facility owner or operator's reporting duty (Section 8, obligation 9).

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the duty holder under Article 7 of the Protocol (Section 8, obligation 9) is the owner or operator of an individual facility that meets the specified activity, threshold, and release or transfer conditions; the captured text names no obligation running to a freight forwarder that neither owns nor operates such a facility. *Analytical inference:* a workspace's practical exposure runs through whichever of its own or its clients' sites meets the facility definition, not through this Council Decision or the Protocol directly.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: "Regulation (EC) No 166/2006 of the European Parliament and the Council of 18 January 2006 concerning the establishment of a European Pollutant Release and Transfer Register ( 3 ) has incorporated the provisions of the Protocol into Community legislation." *Source: Council Decision of 2 December 2005 (2006/61/EC), EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32006D0061.* *Per the workspace's reading:* Regulation (EC) No 166/2006 (the European PRTR Regulation, not itself amended by this Decision) is the controlling EU instrument implementing the Protocol's facility-reporting duties; a workspace should check that regulation directly for the current Annex I/II thresholds rather than relying on the Protocol's own text for EU-facility compliance.

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

FACT: "A Meeting of the Parties is hereby established. Its first session shall be convened no later than two years after the entry into force of this Protocol." *Source: Council Decision of 2 December 2005 (2006/61/EC), EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32006D0061.* *Analytical inference:* this is an institutional milestone (the Meeting of the Parties' own first session), not a compliance deadline running to a facility operator; it is the required primary-deadline statement this brief's corpus states, named here for completeness (see Section 8, obligation 11) though it does not itself change a workspace's own reporting duty.

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does this Council Decision or the Protocol itself create a reporting duty a freight forwarder must comply with?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* Not directly. The duty in Article 7 of the Protocol runs to the owner or operator of a qualifying facility (Section 4); a workspace's exposure depends on whether it or a client operates such a facility.

**Q2: Which thresholds determine whether a workspace-operated site must report?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the specific Annex I activity/capacity/employee thresholds and Annex II pollutant/waste thresholds are not reproduced in this brief's captured text; a workspace should confirm the current thresholds directly against Regulation (EC) No 166/2006 or the Protocol's own Annexes.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: this Council Decision approves an international Protocol on behalf of the Community; "substantive requirements" here means both the Council Decision's own operative provisions and the Protocol's own Party-level obligations, plus the operational implications those carry for a freight forwarder that owns or operates a covered facility.*

**1. Approval of the Protocol on behalf of the Community.** FACT: "HAS DECIDED AS FOLLOWS: Article 1 The UN-ECE Protocol on Pollutant Release and Transfer Registers is hereby approved on behalf of the Community." *Source: Council Decision of 2 December 2005 (2006/61/EC), EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32006D0061.*

**2. Limit on the Commission's amendment-approval authorisation.** FACT: "The authorisation referred to in paragraph 1 shall be limited to those amendments that are consistent with, and do not entail any modification of, relevant Community legislation on the establishment of a European Pollutant Release and Transfer Register." *Source: Council Decision of 2 December 2005 (2006/61/EC), EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32006D0061.*

**3. Twelve-month non-acceptance notification duty.** FACT: "Whenever an amendment to the Annexes to the Protocol is not implemented in the relevant Community legislation within 12 months of the date of its circulation by the Depositary, the Commission shall, in writing, provide the Depositary with a notification of non-acceptance with respect to that amendment" *Source: Council Decision of 2 December 2005 (2006/61/EC), EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32006D0061.*

**4. Publication and adoption of this Decision.** FACT: "This Decision shall be published in the Official Journal of the European Union" *Source: Council Decision of 2 December 2005 (2006/61/EC), EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32006D0061.* FACT: "Done at Brussels, 2 December 2005." *Source: Council Decision of 2 December 2005 (2006/61/EC), EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32006D0061.*

**5. Objective of the Protocol.** FACT: "The objective of this Protocol is to enhance public access to information through the establishment of coherent, integrated, nationwide pollutant release and transfer registers (PRTRs) in accordance with the provisions of this Protocol, which could facilitate public participation in environmental decision-making as well as contribute to the prevention and reduction of pollution of the environment." *Source: Council Decision of 2 December 2005 (2006/61/EC), EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32006D0061.*

**6. "Facility" definition.** FACT: "means one or more installations on the same site, or on adjoining sites, that are owned or operated by the same natural or legal person;" *Source: Council Decision of 2 December 2005 (2006/61/EC), EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32006D0061.*

**7. General duty on each Party to implement the Protocol.** FACT: "Each Party shall take the necessary legislative, regulatory and other measures, and appropriate enforcement measures, to implement the provisions of this Protocol." *Source: Council Decision of 2 December 2005 (2006/61/EC), EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32006D0061.*

**8. Ten-year public data accessibility design requirement.** FACT: "Each Party shall design its register taking into account the possibility of its future expansion and ensuring that the reporting data from at least the 10 previous reporting years are publicly accessible." *Source: Council Decision of 2 December 2005 (2006/61/EC), EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32006D0061.*

**9. Scope of the register.** FACT: "Article 6 Scope of the register 1. Each Party shall ensure that its register includes the information on: (a) releases of pollutants required to be reported pursuant to Article 7(2); (b) off-site transfers required to be reported pursuant to Article 7(2); and (c) releases of pollutants from diffuse sources required pursuant to Article 7(4)." *Source: Council Decision of 2 December 2005 (2006/61/EC), EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32006D0061.*

**10. Facility owner/operator reporting thresholds and duty.** FACT: "transfers off-site hazardous waste exceeding two tons per year or other waste exceeding 2 000 tons per year, where the Party has opted for waste-specific reporting of transfers pursuant to paragraph 5(d);" *Source: Council Decision of 2 December 2005 (2006/61/EC), EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32006D0061.* FACT: "Each Party shall require the owner or operator of a facility referred to in paragraph 1 to submit the information specified in paragraphs 5 and 6, and in accordance with the requirements therein, with respect to those pollutants and wastes for which thresholds were exceeded." *Source: Council Decision of 2 December 2005 (2006/61/EC), EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32006D0061.*

**11. Confidentiality carve-out.** FACT: "Each Party may authorise the competent authority to keep information, held on the register, confidential where public disclosure of that information would adversely affect" *Source: Council Decision of 2 December 2005 (2006/61/EC), EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32006D0061.* in particular: "the confidentiality of commercial and industrial information, where such confidentiality is protected by law in order to protect a legitimate economic interest;" *Source: Council Decision of 2 December 2005 (2006/61/EC), EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32006D0061.*

**12. First session of the Meeting of the Parties (primary deadline, institutional not workspace-facing).** FACT: "A Meeting of the Parties is hereby established. Its first session shall be convened no later than two years after the entry into force of this Protocol." *Source: Council Decision of 2 December 2005 (2006/61/EC), EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32006D0061.*

**13. Protocol's own entry into force mechanism.** FACT: "This Protocol shall enter into force on the 19th day after the date of deposit of the 16th instrument of ratification, acceptance, approval or accession." *Source: Council Decision of 2 December 2005 (2006/61/EC), EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32006D0061.*

**14. Voting exception.** FACT: "Except as provided for in paragraph 2, each Party to this Protocol shall have one vote." *Source: Council Decision of 2 December 2005 (2006/61/EC), EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32006D0061.* *Analytical inference:* this is an institutional voting rule for Meetings of the Parties, not a compliance exception affecting a facility owner or operator's own reporting duty.

**Qualification accounting.** Per-year trajectory: No phase-in is stated in Articles 1 to 8 of the Protocol. Exceptions and carve-outs: CAPTURED above (obligation 14, the voting exception; a procedural, not compliance-substantive, exception, honestly labelled as such). Scope limits: CAPTURED above (obligation 2, the Commission's amendment-approval authorisation limit).

Obligations surveyed: 13; workspace-adjacent: 7; extracted as FACT: 7.

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

FACT: "Each Party shall require the owner or operator of a facility referred to in paragraph 1 to submit the information specified in paragraphs 5 and 6, and in accordance with the requirements therein, with respect to those pollutants and wastes for which thresholds were exceeded." *Source: Council Decision of 2 December 2005 (2006/61/EC), EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32006D0061.* *Operational implication:* a workspace that owns or operates a qualifying facility should confirm the specific information paragraphs 5 and 6 of Article 7 require (not reproduced in this brief's corpus) directly against the Protocol's own Annexes or Regulation (EC) No 166/2006.

# 11. Operational System Requirements

For a workspace operating or contracting a facility potentially in scope: (1) confirm whether the site undertakes an Annex I activity above the capacity or employee threshold, (2) confirm whether its pollutant releases or off-site waste transfers exceed the Annex II thresholds (Section 8, obligation 10), and (3) if information is withheld as confidential under the carve-out in Section 8 (obligation 11), confirm the register indicates what was withheld and why, per Article 12(3) of the Protocol. *Operational implication:* none of these is triggered automatically; each depends on facts about the specific site's own activity and emissions profile.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

FACT: "Each Party may authorise the competent authority to keep information, held on the register, confidential where public disclosure of that information would adversely affect" including "the confidentiality of commercial and industrial information, where such confidentiality is protected by law in order to protect a legitimate economic interest;" *Source: Council Decision of 2 December 2005 (2006/61/EC), EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32006D0061.* *Analytical inference:* a workspace-operated facility with genuinely confidential commercial or industrial information may have that information withheld from the public register, though the register must still indicate that something was withheld and why (Article 12(3) of the Protocol).

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 25 June 1998: The Community signs the Aarhus Convention. *Source: Council Decision of 2 December 2005 (2006/61/EC), EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32006D0061.*
- 21 May 2003: The Community signs the Protocol. FACT: "The Community signed the Protocol on 21 May 2003." *Source: Council Decision of 2 December 2005 (2006/61/EC), EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32006D0061.*
- 18 January 2006: Regulation (EC) No 166/2006 (the European PRTR Regulation) is adopted, incorporating the Protocol's provisions into Community legislation. FACT: "Regulation (EC) No 166/2006 of the European Parliament and the Council of 18 January 2006 concerning the establishment of a European Pollutant Release and Transfer Register ( 3 ) has incorporated the provisions of the Protocol into Community legislation." *Source: Council Decision of 2 December 2005 (2006/61/EC), EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32006D0061.*
- 2 December 2005: Council Decision 2006/61/EC is adopted at Brussels, approving the Protocol on behalf of the Community. FACT: "Done at Brussels, 2 December 2005." *Source: Council Decision of 2 December 2005 (2006/61/EC), EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32006D0061.*

# 15. Sources

- Council Decision of 2 December 2005 on the conclusion, on behalf of the European Community, of the UN-ECE Protocol on Pollutant Release and Transfer Registers (2006/61/EC), Official Journal of the European Union L 32/54, EUR-Lex (Tier 1, primary binding text). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32006D0061

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks Commission Regulation (EU) No 582/2011 as an EC type-approval implementing regulation: it lays down the detailed testing, on-board diagnostics (OBD), and in-service conformity requirements manufacturers must meet to receive Euro VI type-approval for heavy-duty engines and vehicles under Regulation (EC) No 595/2009. It exists to give a workspace operating or leasing EU-registered heavy-duty vehicles a single place to see which manufacturer-facing obligations this Regulation creates, which of them carry operational consequences for a vehicle already in service (OBD behaviour, driver-inducement speed limiting), and when those obligations took or take effect.

FACT: "This Regulation lays down measures for the implementation of Articles 4, 5, 6 and 12 of Regulation (EC) No 595/2009." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 582/2011, Article 1. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32011R0582

**What the workspace should expect to decide:** whether any heavy-duty vehicle in its own or a carrier's fleet is subject to the driver-inducement speed-limiting behaviour this Regulation requires manufacturers to build in, and whether that behaviour should factor into route or maintenance planning.

*Analytical inference:* this is a manufacturer- and approval-authority-facing implementing regulation, not a duty running to a vehicle operator; its relevance to the workspace is indirect, through the vehicles it buys, leases, or contracts for carriage.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 582/2011, Article 20. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32011R0582

*Operational implication:* the Regulation applies directly to engine and vehicle manufacturers seeking Euro VI type-approval, and to the approval authorities that grant it, across every EU Member State; a workspace does not itself apply for type-approval, but every EU-registered heavy-duty vehicle it operates, leases, or contracts for road carriage was type-approved under these requirements, including the OBD and driver-inducement behaviour described in Section 8 below.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the obligations in this Regulation run from the manufacturer to the approval authority (and, for in-service conformity, back to the manufacturer via Member State surveillance testing); none of the captured text states a duty running from the manufacturer or the approval authority to a vehicle operator, carrier, or freight forwarder directly.

FACT: "If the manufacturer chooses, during a period of 3 years after the dates specified in Article 8(1) and (2) of Regulation (EC) No 595/2009 OBD systems may comply with alternative provisions as specified in Annex X to this Regulation and referring to this paragraph." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 582/2011, Article 4(7). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32011R0582

*Analytical inference:* because this is a manufacturer election (an optional alternative-compliance pathway during a transitional window), a workspace's own practical leverage point in this chain is vehicle selection and maintenance record review, not compliance monitoring of the manufacturer.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: "In order to receive an EC type-approval of an engine system or engine family as a separate technical unit, EC type-approval of a vehicle with an approved engine system with regard to emissions and vehicle repair and maintenance information, or an EC type-approval of a vehicle with regard to emissions and vehicle repair and maintenance information the manufacturer shall, in accordance with the provisions of Annex I, demonstrate that the vehicles or engine systems are subject to the tests and comply with the requirements set out in Annexes III to VIII, X, XIII, and XIV." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 582/2011, Article 3(1). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32011R0582

*Per the workspace's reading:* this is the controlling type-approval gate every Euro VI heavy-duty engine or vehicle in the workspace's fleet passed through before it could be sold, registered, or put into service in the Union; Annexes X (OBD) and XIII (NOx control, driver inducement) are the two Annexes with the clearest operational bearing once the vehicle is in service.

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does this Regulation create a direct regulatory obligation on a freight forwarder or motor carrier operating Euro VI vehicles?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* No obligation in the captured text runs to a vehicle operator directly; every "shall" duty identified in Section 8 below runs to the manufacturer or the approval authority.

**Q2: Can this Regulation's requirements affect a vehicle already in the workspace's fleet during operation, not just at the point of purchase?**

FACT: "When the driver inducement system has determined that the severe inducement system shall be activated, the low-level inducement system shall remain activated until the vehicle speed has been limited to 20 km/h (creep mode)." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 582/2011, Annex XIII, Section 5.5.1. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32011R0582

*Operational implication:* yes; a Euro VI heavy-duty vehicle whose reagent (AdBlue/urea) dosing system is not maintained can be speed-limited to 20 km/h in service under this Regulation's own driver inducement design requirement, see Section 11 below.

**Q3: Is the workspace itself within this Regulation's own stated scope for any Annex?**

*Analytical inference:* No. Section 8's scope statement (Annex XIII, Section 2) scopes "any engine system" the manufacturer designs, constructs, and installs, not the workspace or its equipment.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: this Regulation's obligations run overwhelmingly to manufacturers and approval authorities, not to a vehicle operator; "workspace-adjacent" below means the obligation bears on vehicles the workspace buys, leases, or contracts for carriage, or on the compliance record a workspace might need to review, not that the workspace itself owes the duty.*

**1. Type-approval compliance-and-testing requirement (manufacturer).** FACT: "In order to receive an EC type-approval of an engine system or engine family as a separate technical unit, EC type-approval of a vehicle with an approved engine system with regard to emissions and vehicle repair and maintenance information, or an EC type-approval of a vehicle with regard to emissions and vehicle repair and maintenance information the manufacturer shall, in accordance with the provisions of Annex I, demonstrate that the vehicles or engine systems are subject to the tests and comply with the requirements set out in Annexes III to VIII, X, XIII, and XIV." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 582/2011, Article 3(1). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32011R0582

**2. OBD system equipment requirement (manufacturer).** FACT: "Manufacturers shall ensure that all engine systems and vehicles are equipped with an OBD system." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 582/2011, Article 4(1). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32011R0582

**3. OBD/DPF phase-in cutoff dates (statutory trajectory).** FACT: "If the manufacturer chooses, until 1 September 2014 in the case of new types of vehicles or engines and until 1 September 2015 for all new vehicles sold, registered or put into service within the Union, he may use alternative provisions for the monitoring of the DPF as set out in point 2.3.3.3 of Annex X." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 582/2011, Article 4(8). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32011R0582

*Operational implication:* a heavy-duty vehicle first registered before these cutoff dates may carry alternative (rather than the general) DPF-monitoring provisions; per-year trajectory: see the accounting note below.

**4. Recall and repair record-keeping duty (manufacturer).** FACT: "The manufacturer shall keep a record of every engine system or vehicle recalled and repaired or modified and of the workshop which performed the repair." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 582/2011, Article 12(6). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32011R0582

*Operational implication:* this is the record a workspace should ask for when a manufacturer-issued recall touches a vehicle it operates.

**5. Remedial-measures submission deadline (manufacturer, 60 working days).** FACT: "On request of the approval authority and following in-service testing in accordance with Article 12 the manufacturer shall submit the plan of remedial measures to the approval authority no later than 60 working days after receipt of the notification from the approval authority." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 582/2011, Article 13(1). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32011R0582

**6. Entry into force.** FACT: "This Regulation shall enter into force on the 20th day following its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 582/2011, Article 20. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32011R0582

**7. Jurisdictional scope and binding effect.** FACT: "This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 582/2011, Article 20. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32011R0582

**8. OBD in-use-performance statement exemption during the phase-in period.** FACT: "During the phase-in period set out in Article 4(7), the manufacturer shall be exempted from providing the statement required by Section 6.4.1." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 582/2011, Annex X, Section 6.4.4. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32011R0582

**9. NOx control engine-system scope and durability duty (manufacturer).** FACT: "Any engine system falling within the scope of this Annex shall be designed, constructed and installed so as to be capable of meeting these requirements throughout the normal life of the engine under normal conditions of use." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 582/2011, Annex XIII, Section 2. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32011R0582

**Qualification accounting.** Per-year trajectory: CAPTURED (see metadata.requirement_trajectory: the Article 4(8) phase-in cutoffs of 1 September 2014 for new types and 1 September 2015 for all new vehicles). Exceptions and carve-outs: No exceptions are stated in Articles 1 to 20 or Annexes X and XIII (the pool's only two "except" occurrences, in Annex III Section 2.4, are themselves negated: "shall not be permitted except to the extent..."). Scope limits: CAPTURED above (obligation 9, the Annex XIII "falling within the scope of this Annex" statement).

Obligations surveyed: 10; workspace-adjacent: 9; extracted as FACT: 9.

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

FACT: "An approval authority shall not assign the same number to another vehicle type." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 582/2011, Article 8(1). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32011R0582

*Operational implication:* every EC type-approval number a workspace sees on a heavy-duty vehicle's documentation is unique to that vehicle type; the same number is never reused across a different approved type.

# 11. Operational System Requirements

*Note: because every substantive duty in this Regulation runs to the manufacturer or approval authority, "operational system requirements" here means the on-board vehicle behaviour this Regulation requires manufacturers to design in, behaviour a workspace's drivers and maintenance staff will encounter in service.*

**1. Driver inducement creep-mode speed limiting.** FACT: "When the driver inducement system has determined that the severe inducement system shall be activated, the low-level inducement system shall remain activated until the vehicle speed has been limited to 20 km/h (creep mode)." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 582/2011, Annex XIII, Section 5.5.1. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32011R0582

*Operational implication:* a vehicle whose reagent dosing system triggers the severe inducement level will be speed-limited to 20 km/h until the underlying reagent/dosing fault is corrected; a workspace should treat a persistent AdBlue/reagent warning as an operational, not merely a maintenance, priority.

**2. Driver inducement deactivation condition.** FACT: "The driver inducement system shall be deactivated when the conditions for its activation have ceased to exist." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 582/2011, Annex XIII, Section 5.6. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32011R0582

*Operational implication:* correcting the underlying reagent or dosing fault (not a manual override) is what lifts the speed limitation described above.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 25 May 2011: Commission Regulation (EU) No 582/2011 adopted.
- 1 September 2014: Article 4(8) alternative DPF-monitoring phase-in cutoff for new types of vehicles or engines.
- 1 September 2015: Article 4(8) alternative DPF-monitoring phase-in cutoff for all new vehicles sold, registered, or put into service within the Union.

*Source for timeline entries: Commission Regulation (EU) No 582/2011, Articles 4(8) and 20. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32011R0582*

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks Regulation (EU) 2019/943 (recast) as the internal-market-for-electricity regulation: it sets the fundamental principles, wholesale-market design rules, and cross-border rules for the EU's electricity system, administered through Member State regulatory authorities, transmission system operators (TSOs), the ENTSO for Electricity, and ACER. It exists to give a workspace a single place to see whether this Regulation creates any duty running to it directly, and what the Regulation's own stated objectives are for demand response, energy storage, and market integration that could bear indirectly on electricity costs at a workspace's own depots, warehouses, or facilities.

FACT: "This Regulation aims to: (a) set the basis for an efficient achievement of the objectives of the Energy Union and in particular the climate and energy framework for 2030 by enabling market signals to be delivered for increased efficiency, higher share of renewable energy sources, security of supply, flexibility, sustainability, decarbonisation and innovation;" *Source: Regulation (EU) 2019/943, Article 1(a). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32019R0943

*Analytical inference:* this is a wholesale electricity market structure regulation addressed to Member States, regulatory authorities, TSOs, and electricity undertakings; the captured text states no duty running to a freight forwarder, carrier, or logistics operator as such.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2019/943, Article 71. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32019R0943

*Operational implication:* the Regulation is directly applicable across every EU Member State, but its own stated addressees are Member States, national regulatory authorities, TSOs, the ENTSO for Electricity, ACER, and electricity undertakings; a workspace's relevance to it is indirect, through the wholesale electricity price signals and market structure it establishes for the electricity a workspace's own facilities purchase.

FACT: "set fundamental principles for well-functioning, integrated electricity markets, which allow all resource providers and electricity customers non-discriminatory market access, empower consumers, ensure competitiveness on the global market as well as demand response, energy storage and energy efficiency, and facilitate aggregation of distributed demand and supply, and enable market and sectoral integration and market-based remuneration of electricity generated from renewable sources;" *Source: Regulation (EU) 2019/943, Article 1(b). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32019R0943

*Analytical inference:* demand response, energy storage, and aggregation of distributed demand and supply are named as objectives of this Regulation's market design; the captured text does not itself state a mechanism by which a workspace could participate, so this remains a stated objective rather than a workspace-facing right or duty.

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does this Regulation create a direct regulatory obligation on a freight forwarder or motor carrier?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* No. Every "shall" duty identified in Section 8 below runs to a Member State, a national regulatory authority, a transmission system operator, or an electricity undertaking; none runs to a vehicle operator, carrier, or freight forwarder.

**Q2: Could this Regulation's market-design objectives eventually create a workspace-facing participation mechanism (for example, if a workspace's facility has on-site generation, storage, or demand-response capability)?**

*Analytical inference:* Possibly, in principle, given the stated objective of facilitating "aggregation of distributed demand and supply" (Section 2 above), but this item's own captured pool states no operative mechanism, eligibility rule, or registration process by which a workspace could act on this; a workspace-facing pathway, if any, is not established in the text this brief is grounded on.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: this Regulation's obligations run overwhelmingly to Member States, regulatory authorities, transmission system operators, and electricity undertakings, not to a vehicle or logistics operator; "workspace-adjacent" below is scored narrowly given how little of this Regulation's own text bears on a freight forwarder's operations.*

**1. Balancing-market imbalance price area rule.** FACT: "Each imbalance price area shall be equal to a bidding zone, except in the case of a central dispatching model where an imbalance price area may constitute a part of a bidding zone." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2019/943, Article 6(6). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32019R0943

**2. Bidding zone review 12-month joint-proposal deadline.** FACT: "On the basis of the methodology and assumptions approved pursuant to paragraph 5, the transmission system operators participating in the bidding zone review shall submit a joint proposal to the relevant Member States or their designated competent authorities to amend or maintain the bidding zone configuration no later than 12 months after approval of the methodology and assumptions pursuant to paragraph 5." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2019/943, Article 14(6). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32019R0943

**3. National resource adequacy assessment regional scope.** FACT: "National resource adequacy assessments shall have a regional scope and shall be based on the methodology referred in Article 23(3) in particular in points (b) to (m) of Article 23(5)." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2019/943, Article 24(1). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32019R0943

**4. Information-provision duty on electricity undertakings.** FACT: "The owners of the undertakings or their representatives and, in the case of legal persons, the natural persons authorised to represent the undertaking by law or by their instrument of incorporation, shall supply the information requested." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2019/943, Article 65(4). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32019R0943

**5. Member State penalties duty for infringements.** FACT: "Without prejudice to paragraph 2 of this Article, the Member States shall lay down the rules on penalties applicable to infringements of this Regulation, the network codes adopted pursuant to Article 59, and the guidelines adopted pursuant to Article 61 and shall take all measures necessary to ensure that they are implemented. The penalties provided for shall be effective, proportionate and dissuasive." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2019/943, Article 66(1). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32019R0943

**6. Entry into force.** FACT: "This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2019/943, Article 71(1). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32019R0943

**7. Application date.** FACT: "It shall apply from 1 January 2020." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2019/943, Article 71(2). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32019R0943

**8. Binding effect and jurisdictional scope.** FACT: "This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2019/943, Article 71. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32019R0943

**Qualification accounting.** Per-year trajectory: No phase-in is stated in Articles 1 to 71 beyond the single application date fixed in obligation 7 above; recorded via metadata.requirement_trajectory (the two-step adoption/application sequence, with no further per-year phase-in stated). Exceptions and carve-outs: CAPTURED above (obligation 1, the Article 6(6) central-dispatching-model exception to the imbalance-price-area rule). Scope limits: CAPTURED above (obligation 3, the Article 24(1) "regional scope" statement).

Obligations surveyed: 8; workspace-adjacent: 4; extracted as FACT: 8.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 5 June 2019: Regulation (EU) 2019/943 adopted. FACT: "Done at Brussels, 5 June 2019." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2019/943, closing formula. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32019R0943
- 1 January 2020: Regulation applies from this date (Article 71(2)), except for the Articles the Regulation itself names as applying from the date of entry into force.

*Source for timeline entries: Regulation (EU) 2019/943, Article 71. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32019R0943*

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks Commission Decision 2007/205/EC, an administrative implementing decision that establishes the common reporting format Member States must use for their first report under Directive 2004/42/EC (limitation of VOC emissions from paints, varnishes, and vehicle refinishing products). It exists to give a workspace a single place to see that this Decision itself creates no direct duty on a private operator, while the reporting format's own Annex reveals substantive facts about the underlying Directive's licensing and inspection regime, including the parts of that regime that touch vehicle refinishing and vintage-vehicle restoration.

FACT: "For the purposes of drawing up the report to be submitted to the Commission pursuant to Article 7 of Directive 2004/42/EC, and covering the period from 1 January until 31 December 2007, Member States shall use the format set out in the Annex to this Decision." *Source: Commission Decision 2007/205/EC, Article 1. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32007D0205

*Analytical inference:* this Decision's own operative text is a format-and-deadline instruction to Member States; the substantive VOC-emissions rules it reports on live in Directive 2004/42/EC, which this pool does not itself carry in full.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "This Decision is addressed to the Member States." *Source: Commission Decision 2007/205/EC, Article 2. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32007D0205

*Operational implication:* the Decision addresses only Member States; a workspace operating a vehicle refinishing installation, or handling vintage vehicles subject to Directive 2004/42/EC's individual-license regime for restoration and maintenance products, is relevant only as a SUBJECT of the national monitoring and inspection programme this Decision's Annex asks Member States to describe, not as an addressee of this Decision itself.

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does this Decision create a direct regulatory obligation on a freight forwarder or logistics operator?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* No. The only "shall" duties in the captured text (Article 1's format instruction and the Article 7 reporting deadline) run to Member States, not to a private operator.

**Q2: Does the underlying reporting regime this Decision documents touch a vehicle refinishing or classic/vintage-vehicle operation?**

FACT: "wholesalers, retailers, professional end-users of regulated products or other operators, including for instance vehicle refinishing installations no longer covered by Council Directive 1999/13/EC" *Source: Commission Decision 2007/205/EC, Annex, point 2.3(3). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32007D0205

*Operational implication:* yes; the Annex's own inspection-scope question names vehicle refinishing installations as one of the operator categories Member States may inspect under Directive 2004/42/EC, alongside manufacturers, importers, wholesalers, and retailers of the regulated products.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: this Decision's own operative text (Articles 1 and 2) creates only Member-State-facing format and deadline duties; the obligations below also include substantive facts about the underlying Directive 2004/42/EC regime that this Decision's own reporting-format Annex documents, since that Annex is the only place in this item's pool where the regime's actual mechanics (inspection scope, individual licenses) are described.*

**1. Common reporting format duty (Member States).** FACT: "For the purposes of drawing up the report to be submitted to the Commission pursuant to Article 7 of Directive 2004/42/EC, and covering the period from 1 January until 31 December 2007, Member States shall use the format set out in the Annex to this Decision." *Source: Commission Decision 2007/205/EC, Article 1. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32007D0205

**2. First-report submission deadline (Member States).** FACT: "Pursuant to Article 7 of Directive 2004/42/EC in connexion with Annex I thereto, Member States shall prepare and submit to the Commission the first report on the implementation of that Directive by 30 June 2008 at the latest." *Source: Commission Decision 2007/205/EC, recital 2 (citing Directive 2004/42/EC, Article 7 and Annex I). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32007D0205

**3. Addressee statement.** FACT: "This Decision is addressed to the Member States." *Source: Commission Decision 2007/205/EC, Article 2. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32007D0205

**4. Inspection scope naming vehicle refinishing installations.** FACT: "wholesalers, retailers, professional end-users of regulated products or other operators, including for instance vehicle refinishing installations no longer covered by Council Directive 1999/13/EC" *Source: Commission Decision 2007/205/EC, Annex, point 2.3(3). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32007D0205

**5. Individual-license regime for vintage vehicles of historical and cultural value.** FACT: "Which authorities are in charge of designating the buildings and/or vintage vehicles of particular historical and cultural value?" *Source: Commission Decision 2007/205/EC, Annex, point 5.2(2). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32007D0205

*Operational implication:* a workspace handling classic or vintage vehicles for restoration or maintenance may fall within the scope of Directive 2004/42/EC's Article 3(3) individual-license regime for restricted-VOC-content products, administered by the authority each Member State designates for this purpose; this Decision's own pool does not name which authority in any specific Member State, only that the reporting format asks each Member State to identify it.

**6. Individual-license use restriction (quantity and purpose).** FACT: "sold only in ‘strictly limited’ quantities; (b) used only for the purpose of restoration and maintenance of designated buildings and/or vehicles" *Source: Commission Decision 2007/205/EC, Annex, point 5.2(5). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32007D0205

**7. Inspection scope limited to the most important producers/importers.** FACT: "inspections limited to the most important producers/importers" *Source: Commission Decision 2007/205/EC, Annex, point 2.3(4)(2). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32007D0205

**8. Member States' own national penalty-rules self-report question.** FACT: "What are the rules on penalties applicable to infringement of the national provisions adopted pursuant to Article 10 of Directive 2004/42/EC?" *Source: Commission Decision 2007/205/EC, Annex, point 2.7. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32007D0205

*Analytical inference:* this is a REPORTING QUESTION asking each Member State to describe its own national penalty rules under Article 10 of Directive 2004/42/EC; it is not itself a penalty provision, and this Decision's own pool does not state what those national penalty rules are.

**Qualification accounting.** Per-year trajectory: No phase-in is stated in Articles 1 to 2 of this Decision or the Annex; the only date is the single, non-recurring 30 June 2008 reporting deadline in obligation 2 above. Exceptions and carve-outs: No exceptions are stated in Articles 1 to 2 of this Decision or its Annex (the pool contains no exact-word "except" or "exempt" occurrence; the Annex's "Exemptions granted pursuant to Article 3(2)" heading is a plural-form reference to the underlying Directive's own derogation regime, not itself an exception clause in this Decision). Scope limits: CAPTURED above (obligation 7, the "inspections limited to the most important producers/importers" language).

Obligations surveyed: 8; workspace-adjacent: 4; extracted as FACT: 8.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

FACT: "Which authorities are in charge of designating the buildings and/or vintage vehicles of particular historical and cultural value?" *Source: Commission Decision 2007/205/EC, Annex, point 5.2(2). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32007D0205

*Analytical inference:* the Annex's Section 4 heading ("Exemptions granted pursuant to Article 3(2) of Directive 2004/42/EC") and Section 5 ("Individual licences granted pursuant to Article 3(3) of Directive 2004/42/EC") both point to derogation and individual-license mechanisms in the underlying Directive that this Decision's own pool does not itself state in operative-text form; a workspace with a specific vintage-vehicle or restoration-product question should confirm the current derogation/license criteria against Directive 2004/42/EC directly rather than this reporting-format Decision.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 22 March 2007: Commission Decision 2007/205/EC adopted. FACT: "Done at Brussels, 22 March 2007." *Source: Commission Decision 2007/205/EC, closing formula. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32007D0205
- 30 June 2008: deadline for Member States to submit their first implementation report to the Commission.

*Source for timeline entries: Commission Decision 2007/205/EC, closing formula and recital 2. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32007D0205*

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks Directive 2003/4/EC, the EU instrument implementing the Aarhus Convention's public-access pillar: it gives any natural or legal person, including a workspace, a right to request environmental information held by or for an EU public authority, and it sets the deadlines, permissible exceptions, and charging rules that govern how that right is exercised. It exists to give a workspace a single place to see that this Directive is a tool it can use directly to obtain environmental information relevant to a route, port, facility, or regulatory question, not merely a duty running to Member States.

FACT: "to guarantee the right of access to environmental information held by or for public authorities and to set out the basic terms and conditions of, and practical arrangements for, its exercise" *Source: Directive 2003/4/EC, Article 1(a). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32003L0004

**What the workspace should expect to decide:** whether to file an information request with a relevant public authority (for example, about a port's environmental permits or emissions monitoring data) and, if so, how to time it against the 1- and 2-month response deadlines in Section 8 below.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "Member States shall ensure that public authorities are required, in accordance with the provisions of this Directive, to make available environmental information held by or for them to any applicant at his request and without his having to state an interest." *Source: Directive 2003/4/EC, Article 3(1). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32003L0004

*Operational implication:* a workspace is an "applicant" for the purposes of this Directive; it can request environmental information from any EU public authority without having to state a reason or interest, and Article 4's emissions carve-out (Section 8, obligation 4) means a request specifically for emissions data cannot be refused on most confidentiality grounds.

FACT: "This Directive is addressed to the Member States." *Source: Directive 2003/4/EC, Article 13. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32003L0004

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the Directive's own duties (transposition, guidance, review reporting) run to Member States and the Commission; a workspace's own right of access under Article 3 is exercised against the national implementing law each Member State adopted, not against this Directive's text directly, except to the extent EU direct-effect doctrine may apply to a Member State that failed to transpose it correctly, which is a fact-specific legal question outside this brief's scope.

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

FACT: "No later than 14 February 2004, the Commission shall forward to the Member States a guidance document setting out clearly the manner in which it wishes the Member States to report." *Source: Directive 2003/4/EC, Article 9(1). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32003L0004

*Operational implication:* this is a Commission-to-Member-State guidance deadline (already elapsed relative to this Directive's own text, which is dated 2003); it is carried here because the export record for this item names it as a forward event, and it is also reflected in Section 14's timeline below.

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Can a workspace itself invoke this Directive to obtain environmental information?**

*Analytical inference:* Yes, in principle -- Article 3(1) (Section 2 above) frames the right as running to "any applicant" without a stated-interest requirement, and Article 2(6) defines "public" (and by extension "applicant") to include a legal person; a workspace filing a request in its own corporate capacity fits this definition on the captured text's own terms.

**Q2: Does this Directive create a compliance obligation, deadline, or penalty running to a freight forwarder?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* No. Every "shall" duty identified in Section 8 below runs to a Member State, a public authority, or the Commission; none runs to a private applicant. The only deadlines that could ever bind a workspace are the response-time deadlines in Article 3(2), and those run to the PUBLIC AUTHORITY answering the workspace's own request, not to the workspace itself.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: this Directive's own duties run overwhelmingly to Member States, public authorities, and the Commission; "workspace-adjacent" below means the obligation bears directly on a workspace's own ability to request and receive environmental information, not that the workspace itself owes the duty.*

**1. Right of access without stated interest.** FACT: "Member States shall ensure that public authorities are required, in accordance with the provisions of this Directive, to make available environmental information held by or for them to any applicant at his request and without his having to state an interest." *Source: Directive 2003/4/EC, Article 3(1). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32003L0004

**2. One-month response deadline.** FACT: "as soon as possible or, at the latest, within one month after the receipt by the public authority referred to in paragraph 1 of the applicant's request" *Source: Directive 2003/4/EC, Article 3(2)(a). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32003L0004

**3. Two-month extended response deadline for large or complex requests.** FACT: "within two months after the receipt of the request by the public authority if the volume and the complexity of the information is such that the one-month period referred to in (a) cannot be complied with." *Source: Directive 2003/4/EC, Article 3(2)(b). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32003L0004

**4. Emissions-information carve-out from most confidentiality exceptions.** FACT: "Member States may not, by virtue of paragraph 2(a), (d), (f), (g) and (h), provide for a request to be refused where the request relates to information on emissions into the environment." *Source: Directive 2003/4/EC, Article 4(2). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32003L0004

*Operational implication:* a public authority may not refuse a workspace's request for information specifically about emissions into the environment on the basis of commercial confidentiality, personal-data confidentiality, or environmental-protection grounds (though it may still refuse on the other Article 4(1)/(2) grounds not listed in this carve-out, such as internal communications or material in course of completion).

**5. Partial-disclosure severability rule.** FACT: "Environmental information held by or for public authorities which has been requested by an applicant shall be made available in part where it is possible to separate out any information falling within the scope of paragraphs 1(d) and (e) or 2 from the rest of the information requested." *Source: Directive 2003/4/EC, Article 4(4). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32003L0004

**6. Charges capped at a reasonable amount.** FACT: "Public authorities may make a charge for supplying any environmental information but such charge shall not exceed a reasonable amount." *Source: Directive 2003/4/EC, Article 5(2). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32003L0004

**7. Four-year state-of-the-environment reporting cycle (statutory trajectory).** FACT: "Member States shall take the necessary measures to ensure that national, and, where appropriate, regional or local reports on the state of the environment are published at regular intervals not exceeding four years." *Source: Directive 2003/4/EC, Article 7(3). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32003L0004

**8. Member State review-report deadlines to the Commission.** FACT: "Not later than 14 February 2009, Member States shall report on the experience gained in the application of this Directive. They shall communicate the report to the Commission not later than 14 August 2009." *Source: Directive 2003/4/EC, Article 9(1). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32003L0004

**9. Commission guidance-document deadline to Member States.** FACT: "No later than 14 February 2004, the Commission shall forward to the Member States a guidance document setting out clearly the manner in which it wishes the Member States to report." *Source: Directive 2003/4/EC, Article 9(1). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32003L0004

**10. National transposition deadline.** FACT: "Member States shall bring into force the laws, regulations and administrative provisions necessary to comply with this Directive by 14 February 2005." *Source: Directive 2003/4/EC, Article 10. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32003L0004

**11. Entry into force.** FACT: "This Directive shall enter into force on the day of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union." *Source: Directive 2003/4/EC, Article 12. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32003L0004

**12. Addressees and jurisdictional scope.** FACT: "This Directive is addressed to the Member States." *Source: Directive 2003/4/EC, Article 13. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32003L0004

**Qualification accounting.** Per-year trajectory: CAPTURED (see metadata.requirement_trajectory: the recurring four-year state-of-the-environment reporting cycle of obligation 7 above). Exceptions and carve-outs: No exceptions are stated in Articles 3 to 13 using the literal words except or exempt (Article 4's own heading, "Exceptions", and its refusal grounds never use either literal word in this pool's captured text). Scope limits: CAPTURED above (obligation 5, the Article 4(4) "falling within the scope of paragraphs 1(d) and (e) or 2" severability rule).

Obligations surveyed: 12; workspace-adjacent: 8; extracted as FACT: 12.

# 11. Operational System Requirements

*Note: because most substantive duties in this Directive run to Member States and public authorities, "operational system requirements" here means the practical access mechanism a workspace would encounter when exercising its Article 3 right.*

FACT: "the designation of information officers" *Source: Directive 2003/4/EC, Article 3(5)(c). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32003L0004

*Operational implication:* Member States must designate named information officers as one of the practical arrangements for exercising the right of access; a workspace filing a request should expect to be directed to such an officer or to a public register of environmental information (Article 3(5)(c)) rather than a generic contact point.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

FACT: "Member States may not, by virtue of paragraph 2(a), (d), (f), (g) and (h), provide for a request to be refused where the request relates to information on emissions into the environment." *Source: Directive 2003/4/EC, Article 4(2). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32003L0004

*Analytical inference:* this emissions carve-out is the single most workspace-relevant edge case in this Directive for a sustainability-intelligence use: it means a public authority cannot lean on commercial or personal-data confidentiality to withhold emissions data a workspace requests, though the other listed grounds (internal communications, material in course of completion, national defence, course of justice) remain available refusal grounds outside the carve-out.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 28 January 2003: Directive 2003/4/EC adopted. FACT: "Done at Brussels, 28 January 2003." *Source: Directive 2003/4/EC, closing formula. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32003L0004
- 14 February 2004: deadline for the Commission to forward a guidance document to Member States on reporting (Article 9(1)).
- 14 February 2005: national transposition deadline (Article 10), and repeal of Directive 90/313/EEC takes effect (Article 11).
- 14 February 2009: deadline for Member States to report on their own experience applying this Directive (Article 9(1)).
- 14 August 2009: deadline for Member States to communicate that report to the Commission (Article 9(1)).

*Source for timeline entries: Directive 2003/4/EC, Articles 9, 10, 11, and the closing formula. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32003L0004*

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) No 1047/2013, a narrow, single-purpose correction: it replaces one manufacturer's 2010 average specific CO2 emissions figure in a table annexed to an earlier delegated regulation. It exists to give a workspace a single place to see that this instrument creates no new duty of any kind; it is a data correction internal to the EU's light-commercial-vehicle CO2 target-setting mechanism.

FACT: "COMMISSION DELEGATED REGULATION (EU) No 1047/2013 of 21 August 2013 amending Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) No 114/2013 for the purpose of correcting the 2010 average specific CO 2 emissions specified for the manufacturer Piaggio." *Source: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) No 1047/2013, title. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32013R1047

*Analytical inference:* this instrument is addressed to a technical data-table entry, not to any class of duty-holder; it is included in this corpus because it is a formally adopted EU regulation under the CO2 emission-performance-standards framework for light commercial vehicles (Regulation (EU) No 510/2011), a framework that shapes the vehicles a workspace's own light-commercial fleet may include, though this specific instrument states no duty running to a workspace.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States." *Source: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) No 1047/2013, Article 2. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32013R1047

*Operational implication:* the Regulation is directly applicable across every EU Member State, but its only operative effect is to correct one data-table entry; it creates no compliance duty, deadline, or penalty a workspace could be subject to.

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does this Regulation create a direct regulatory obligation on a freight forwarder or motor carrier?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* No. The only operative provision (Article 1) replaces a single figure in an annexed table; Article 2 states only the entry-into-force and binding-effect rules common to EU regulations. No obligation in the captured text runs to a vehicle operator, carrier, or freight forwarder.

**Q2: Does correcting this figure change any obligation the manufacturer or a fleet operator already had?**

*Analytical inference:* The captured text does not itself state that the correction changes any other party's obligation; it only replaces the recorded 2010 average emissions value used in the underlying derogation-eligibility calculation under Regulation (EU) No 510/2011 and Delegated Regulation (EU) No 114/2013, neither of which this pool's own text restates in full.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: this instrument's entire operative content is a single data-table correction; none of the three obligations below creates a duty running to a vehicle operator, carrier, or freight forwarder.*

**1. Data-table correction.** FACT: "In the list in Annex III to Delegated Regulation (EU) No 114/2013, the entry in the second column, with the heading ‘Average emissions, (g/km)’, for the make ‘Piaggio’ is replaced by ‘177,00’." *Source: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) No 1047/2013, Article 1. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32013R1047

**2. Entry into force.** FACT: "This Regulation shall enter into force on the 20th day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union." *Source: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) No 1047/2013, Article 2. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32013R1047

**3. Binding effect and jurisdictional scope.** FACT: "This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States." *Source: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) No 1047/2013, Article 2. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32013R1047

**Qualification accounting.** Per-year trajectory: No phase-in is stated in Articles 1 to 2 (this is a single, non-recurring data correction with no phase-in schedule of its own). Exceptions and carve-outs: No exceptions are stated in Articles 1 to 2 (the pool contains no exact-word "except" or "exempt" occurrence anywhere in its 2,270 characters). Scope limits: No scope limits are stated in Articles 1 to 2 (the pool contains no "scope", "does not apply", "applies only", or "limited to" occurrence).

Obligations surveyed: 3; workspace-adjacent: 0; extracted as FACT: 3.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 21 August 2013: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) No 1047/2013 adopted. FACT: "Done at Brussels, 21 August 2013." *Source: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) No 1047/2013, closing formula. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32013R1047

*Source for timeline entry: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) No 1047/2013, closing formula. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32013R1047*

# 15. Sources
