entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks Commission Regulation (EU) 2024/2462 of 19 September 2024, which amends Annex XVII of the REACH Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006 to add a new entry restricting undecafluorohexanoic acid (PFHxA), its salts, and PFHxA-related substances. FACT: "COMMISSION REGULATION (EU) 2024/2462 of 19 September 2024 amending Annex XVII to Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006 of the European Parliament and of the Council as regards undecafluorohexanoic acid (PFHxA), its salts and PFHxA-related substances (Text with EEA relevance)" *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2024/2462, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024R2462*

FACT: "Done at Brussels, 19 September 2024." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2024/2462, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024R2462*

FACT: "This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union" *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2024/2462, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024R2462*

*Analytical inference:* the Regulation's own text does not restate the calendar day this produces; this document states the phased restriction dates the enacting Annex itself gives (10 April 2026, 10 October 2026, 10 October 2027, 10 October 2029, Section 8) rather than compute the entry-into-force day from the twentieth-day rule.

This document is scoped to the captured Regulation's own enacting text and recitals (the Annex XVII amendment and its stated reasoning); it does not include the earlier Annex XV restriction dossier, the RAC/SEAC opinion documents in full, or the pending PFAS-in-firefighting-foams / PFAS-in-all-other-uses restriction dossiers referenced in Section 6, none of which are in this item's captured pool.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

This Regulation is a targeted REACH restriction, not a horizontal PFAS ban: it adds one new entry (79) to Annex XVII of Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006 covering PFHxA, its salts, and PFHxA-related substances in specific product categories. FACT: "the Commission considers it necessary to adopt a Union-wide restriction for the placing on the market and use of PFHxA, its salts and PFHxA-related substances in textiles, leather, furs and hides in clothing (such as outdoor clothing like rain jackets); related accessories (such as handbags) and footwear for the general public; paper and cardboard used as food contact materials; mixtures for the general public; cosmetic products; and some firefighting foams applications." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2024/2462, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024R2462*

*Operational implication:* a workspace moving textiles, leather goods, footwear, food-contact paper/cardboard, general-public mixtures, cosmetic products, or firefighting foam through the EU should treat this Regulation as applicable to those specific cargo categories, not to freight movements generally.

FACT: "This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2024/2462, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024R2462*

*Analytical inference:* because the Regulation is directly applicable in all Member States without national transposition, the restriction dates in Section 8 apply uniformly across the EU rather than on a Member-State-by-Member-State timetable.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

**WINDOW CLOSING.** The broadest general-public restriction (textiles, footwear, food-contact paper and cardboard, mixtures, and cosmetic products) takes effect 10 October 2026 (Section 8, obligation 1); a workspace handling any of these categories should confirm supplier compliance with the concentration limits before that date. *Operational implication:* goods above the concentration limits placed on the market on or after that date are restricted regardless of manufacture date, subject only to the pre-market grandfather derogation in Section 12.

**MONITORING.** The firefighting-foam restriction for training, testing, and public fire services (Section 8, obligation 4) already took effect 10 April 2026; a workspace supporting firefighting-foam logistics for those uses should confirm this restriction is already reflected in supplier documentation.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

FACT: "proposing to restrict the manufacture, use and placing on the market of PFHxA, its salts and PFHxA-related substances on their own, and to restrict their use in the production of and placing on the market in another substance, as a constituent, in a mixture or in an article or their use in another substance, in a mixture or in an article, with a general transition period of 18 months." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2024/2462, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024R2462*

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the duty-holder class under this restriction (and under REACH generally) is the person who manufactures, uses, or places the restricted substance, mixture, or article on the market -- not, on this captured text, a freight forwarder acting purely as carrier or logistics intermediary. Whether any specific workspace activity (for example, import clearance performed in the workspace's own name, or private-label distribution) meets REACH's own "placing on the market" definition is a fact-specific legal question outside this brief's scope and requires counsel review.

*Analytical inference:* the workspace's practical exposure is therefore indirect: verifying that clients and suppliers who ARE duty holders (manufacturers, importers, distributors) can demonstrate compliance with the concentration limits before the applicable restriction date, rather than the workspace itself holding a compliance duty.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: "the Agency’s Committee for Risk Assessment (‘RAC’) adopted its opinion concluding that it has not been demonstrated that the restriction on PFHxA, its salts and PFHxA-related substances as proposed by Germany is the most appropriate Union-wide measure to address the identified risks." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2024/2462, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024R2462*

FACT: "the Agency’s Committee for Socio-Economic Analysis (‘SEAC’) adopted its opinion concluding that it has not been demonstrated that the restriction on PFHxA, its salts and PFHxA-related substances as proposed by Germany is the most appropriate Union-wide measure to address the identified risks, taking into account its socio-economic benefits and costs." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2024/2462, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024R2462*

*Per the workspace's reading:* both Agency committees found Germany's original, broader restriction proposal not fully justified on the available evidence, which is why the enacted restriction (Section 8) is narrower and more targeted than the original 2019 Annex XV dossier described in the recitals.

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

FACT: "The Commission notes that uses of PFHxA, its salts and PFHxA-related substances not covered by this targeted restriction, are also included in two other pending restriction dossiers, notably PFAS in firefighting foams" *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2024/2462, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024R2462*

*Operational implication:* a workspace tracking PFAS exposure beyond this Regulation's own targeted scope should also watch the separate, still-pending PFAS-in-firefighting-foams and PFAS-in-all-other-uses restriction dossiers named above; this captured pool does not include either dossier's own text or current status.

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does this Regulation create a direct compliance duty on a freight forwarder itself?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* On the captured text, the restriction's duty holders are those who manufacture, use, or place the restricted substances, mixtures, or articles on the market (Section 4). Whether a specific workspace activity places it within that duty-holder class requires counsel review of the workspace's own role in each transaction.

**Q2: Does the restriction apply to goods already placed on the market before the applicable date?**

FACT: "By way of derogation from paragraph 1, that paragraph shall not apply to articles and mixtures which were placed on the market before 10 October 2026." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2024/2462, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024R2462*

*Analytical inference:* the parallel derogation for the 2027 restriction (Section 12) uses the same "placed on the market before" test, so the operative question for any shipment is the date the specific article or mixture was placed on the market, not the date it is carried.

**Q3: Does the firefighting-foam restriction reach every public fire service use?**

FACT: "Shall not, from 10 April 2026 be placed on the market, or used, in a concentration equal to or greater than 25 ppb for the sum of PFHxA and its salts, or 1 000 ppb for the sum of PFHxA-related substances, in: (a) firefighting foams and firefighting foam concentrates for training and for testing, except functional testing of the firefighting systems provided that all releases are contained; (b) firefighting foams and firefighting foam concentrates for public fire services, except where those services intervene at industrial fires at establishments covered by Directive 2012/18/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council ( *1 ) and they use the foams and the equipment for that purpose only." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2024/2462, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024R2462*

*Analytical inference:* no, the restriction on public-fire-service use carries its own built-in exception for industrial fires at Seveso-covered establishments where the foam and equipment are used for that purpose only (Section 8, obligation 4; Section 12).

# 8. Substantive Requirements

**1. General-public restriction, from 10 October 2026.** FACT: "Shall not, from 10 October 2026 be placed on the market, or used, in a concentration equal to or greater than 25 ppb for the sum of PFHxA and its salts, or 1 000 ppb for the sum of PFHxA-related substances, measured in homogeneous material, in the following: (a) textiles, leather, furs and hides in clothing and related accessories for the general public; (b) footwear for the general public; (c) paper and cardboard used as food contact materials within the scope of Regulation (EC) No 1935/2004; (d) mixtures for the general public; (e) cosmetic products as defined in Article 2(1), point (a), of Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2024/2462, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024R2462*

**2. Other textiles/leather restriction, from 10 October 2027.** FACT: "Shall not, from 10 October 2027 be placed on the market, or used, in a concentration equal to or greater than 25 ppb for the sum of PFHxA and its salts, or 1 000 ppb for the sum of PFHxA-related substances, measured in homogeneous material, in textiles, leather, furs and hides, other than in clothing and related accessories referred to in paragraph 1, for the general public." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2024/2462, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024R2462*

*Analytical inference:* recital 17 explains the one-year-longer transition for this category: possible functional losses where alternatives do not yet provide sufficient oil and stain repellence for uses outside clothing and related accessories.

**3. PPE / medical device / construction-textile exemption.** FACT: "Paragraphs 1 and 2 shall not apply to the following: (a) personal protective equipment intended to protect users against risks within the scope of risk category III, points (a), (c) to (f), (h), and (l) of Annex I to Regulation (EU) 2016/425; (b) devices within the scope of Regulation (EU) 2017/745; (c) devices within the scope of Regulation (EU) 2017/746; (d) textiles used as construction textiles." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2024/2462, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024R2462*

**4. Firefighting-foam restriction, training/testing/public fire services, from 10 April 2026.** FACT: "Shall not, from 10 April 2026 be placed on the market, or used, in a concentration equal to or greater than 25 ppb for the sum of PFHxA and its salts, or 1 000 ppb for the sum of PFHxA-related substances, in: (a) firefighting foams and firefighting foam concentrates for training and for testing, except functional testing of the firefighting systems provided that all releases are contained; (b) firefighting foams and firefighting foam concentrates for public fire services, except where those services intervene at industrial fires at establishments covered by Directive 2012/18/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council ( *1 ) and they use the foams and the equipment for that purpose only." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2024/2462, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024R2462*

**5. Firefighting-foam restriction, civil aviation, from 10 October 2029.** FACT: "Shall not, from 10 October 2029 be placed on the market, or used, in firefighting foams and firefighting foam concentrates for civil aviation (including in civilian airports) in a concentration equal to or greater than 25 ppb for the sum of PFHxA and its salts, or 1 000 ppb for the sum of PFHxA-related substances." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2024/2462, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024R2462*

**6. PFHxS carve-out.** FACT: "Paragraphs 1, 2, 4 and 5 shall not apply to substances having a perfluoroalkyl group C 6 F 13 - directly attached to a sulphur atom that are prohibited in Annex I to Regulation (EU) 2019/1021 of the European Parliament and of the Council" *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2024/2462, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024R2462*

*Analytical inference:* this carve-out exists because those sulphur-attached substances are separately prohibited under the POPs Regulation (EU) 2019/1021, not because they are considered safe.

**7. Pre-market grandfather derogation, 2026 restriction.** FACT: "By way of derogation from paragraph 1, that paragraph shall not apply to articles and mixtures which were placed on the market before 10 October 2026." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2024/2462, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024R2462*

**8. Pre-market grandfather derogation, 2027 restriction.** FACT: "By way of derogation from paragraph 2, that paragraph shall not apply to articles which were placed on the market before 10 October 2027." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2024/2462, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024R2462*

**Penalty summary.** GAP: no verbatim penalty, fine, or sanction statement running to a manufacturer, importer, distributor, or freight forwarder appears anywhere in this Regulation's own captured text (the enacting articles and the Annex XVII entry, paragraphs 1 to 9); this instrument states only the restriction, its exemptions, and its derogations, with no separate enforcement or penalty clause of its own.

**Qualification accounting.** Per-year trajectory: CAPTURED (see metadata.requirement_trajectory: four dated restriction steps from 10 April 2026 through 10 October 2029). Exceptions and carve-outs: CAPTURED above (obligation 4's "except" clauses). Scope limits: CAPTURED above (obligation 3's "within the scope of risk category III" / "within the scope of Regulation (EU) 2017/745" language).

Obligations surveyed: 9; workspace-adjacent: 8; extracted as FACT: 8.

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

FACT: "For the use of PFHxA, its salts and PFHxA-related substances in firefighting foams, Germany proposed a reporting obligation for a natural or legal person benefitting from the proposed derogations." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2024/2462, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024R2462*

GAP: no registration or reporting obligation for suppliers, users, or freight intermediaries appears in the enacted Annex XVII entry itself (paragraphs 1 to 9); the reporting duty Germany originally proposed for parties benefitting from firefighting-foam derogations, quoted above, was not carried into the final targeted restriction the Commission adopted.

*Analytical inference:* a workspace should not assume any ongoing reporting duty exists under this specific Regulation; if a reporting obligation applies to a workspace's firefighting-foam-related activity, it would have to come from a different, non-captured instrument.

# 11. Operational System Requirements

FACT: "the application of the restriction should be deferred for 18 months for firefighting foams used in training, testing and public fire services; 24 months for textiles, leather, furs and hides in clothing and related accessories and footwear for the general public, paper and cardboard used as food contact materials, mixtures for general public and cosmetic products; 36 months for textiles, leather, furs and hides other than in clothing and related accessories for the general public; and 5 years for firefighting foams used in civil aviation." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2024/2462, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024R2462*

*Operational implication:* a workspace should maintain a compliance calendar keyed to these four dates (10 April 2026; 10 October 2026; 10 October 2027; 10 October 2029, Section 8) rather than a single "in force" date, since each product category phases in separately, and should request supplier attestations of the 25 ppb / 1 000 ppb concentration limits ahead of each applicable date for the product categories the workspace moves.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

FACT: "Paragraphs 1 and 2 shall not apply to the following: (a) personal protective equipment intended to protect users against risks within the scope of risk category III, points (a), (c) to (f), (h), and (l) of Annex I to Regulation (EU) 2016/425; (b) devices within the scope of Regulation (EU) 2017/745; (c) devices within the scope of Regulation (EU) 2017/746; (d) textiles used as construction textiles." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2024/2462, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024R2462*

FACT: "Paragraphs 1, 2, 4 and 5 shall not apply to substances having a perfluoroalkyl group C 6 F 13 - directly attached to a sulphur atom that are prohibited in Annex I to Regulation (EU) 2019/1021 of the European Parliament and of the Council" *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2024/2462, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024R2462*

FACT: "By way of derogation from paragraph 1, that paragraph shall not apply to articles and mixtures which were placed on the market before 10 October 2026." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2024/2462, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024R2462*

FACT: "By way of derogation from paragraph 2, that paragraph shall not apply to articles which were placed on the market before 10 October 2027." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2024/2462, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024R2462*

FACT: "The following substances are excluded from this designation: (a) C 6 F 14 ; (b) C 6 F 13 -C(=O)OH, C 6 F 13 -C(=O)O-X′ or C 6 F 13 -CF 2 -X′ (where X′ = any group, including salts); (c) any substance having a perfluoroalkyl group C 6 F 13 - directly attached to an oxygen atom at one of the non-terminal carbon atoms." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2024/2462, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024R2462*

*Analytical inference:* the substance-identity exclusions above (certain short-chain and oxygen-linked perfluoroalkyl substances) determine which chemistries trigger the restriction at all; a workspace relying on a supplier's chemical-identity declaration should confirm which side of this line a specific treatment falls on before relying on either the restriction or an exemption.

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

FACT: "given that alternatives are widely available and already in use to replace PFHxA, its salts and PFHxA-related substances in firefighting foams used for training and testing, for public fire services and for civil aviation, the Commission considers that restricting those uses should not be delayed." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2024/2462, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024R2462*

FACT: "alternatives for water repellent properties appear to be available." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2024/2462, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024R2462*

*Analytical inference:* the availability of alternatives for the fastest-moving restriction categories (firefighting foam training/testing/public fire services, general-public textiles) is part of why the Commission set the shortest transition periods for those categories and the longest for civil-aviation foam and non-clothing textiles, where alternatives were less established at the time of adoption.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 19 September 2024: Regulation adopted (from the instrument title and its closing "Done at Brussels" clause).
- 10 April 2026: restriction on PFHxA, its salts, and PFHxA-related substances in firefighting foams and firefighting foam concentrates for training, testing, and public fire services takes effect (with the stated exemption for industrial fires at Seveso-covered establishments).
- 10 October 2026: restriction takes effect for textiles, leather, furs and hides in clothing and related accessories, footwear, food-contact paper and cardboard, general-public mixtures, and cosmetic products.
- 10 October 2027: restriction extends to textiles, leather, furs and hides other than in clothing and related accessories, for the general public.
- 10 October 2029: restriction takes effect for firefighting foams and firefighting foam concentrates used in civil aviation.

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2020/2180 of 18 December 2020, a short amending act that extends the reference period during which Member States may authorise rail-infrastructure charge relief under Regulation (EU) 2020/1429. FACT: "COMMISSION DELEGATED REGULATION (EU) 2020/2180 of 18 December 2020 extending the reference period of Regulation (EU) 2020/1429 of the European Parliament and of the Council establishing measures for a sustainable rail market in view of the COVID-19 outbreak (Text with EEA relevance)" *Source: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2020/2180, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020R2180*

FACT: "Done at Brussels, 18 December 2020." *Source: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2020/2180, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020R2180*

FACT: "This Regulation shall enter into force on the day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union" *Source: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2020/2180, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020R2180*

This is a historical, time-bound COVID-19 relief measure: the extended reference period it created ended 30 June 2021 (Section 8), years before this document's own generation date. It is tracked here for completeness and audit-trail purposes, not as an active compliance concern.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

This Regulation replaces Article 1 of Regulation (EU) 2020/1429 to extend the window during which the underlying relief mechanism applies. FACT: "This Regulation lays down temporary rules on the levying of charges for the use of railway infrastructure as set out in Chapter IV of Directive 2012/34/EU. It applies to the use of railway infrastructure for domestic and international rail services covered by that Directive, during the period from 1 March 2020 until 30 June 2021 (“the reference period”)." *Source: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2020/2180, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020R2180*

*Operational implication:* the "applies to" language above scopes the underlying Regulation (EU) 2020/1429 itself (the charge-relief mechanism), not this short amending Regulation; this amending act's only substantive effect is to move that mechanism's end date from 31 December 2020 to 30 June 2021.

FACT: "Regulation (EU) 2020/1429 enables Member States to authorise infrastructure managers to reduce, waive or defer charges for accessing rail infrastructure." *Source: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2020/2180, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020R2180*

*Analytical inference:* the underlying mechanism is permissive on Member States ("enables"), not a duty on any railway undertaking, infrastructure manager, or freight forwarder; whether any charge relief was actually granted on a specific corridor during the reference period depends on the relevant Member State's and infrastructure manager's own decision, which this captured text does not itself record.

FACT: "This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States." *Source: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2020/2180, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020R2180*

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

**MONITORING.** No immediate action arises: the reference period this Regulation extended ended 30 June 2021 (Section 8), and the captured text creates no ongoing duty on a freight forwarder. This item is retained for historical/audit-trail completeness.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the parties positioned to act under this Regulation are Member States (who may authorise relief) and infrastructure managers (who may reduce, waive, or defer charges); a freight forwarder or railway undertaking is, on this captured text, a potential beneficiary of relief actually granted, not a duty holder under the Regulation itself. Whether a specific historical shipment's rail-infrastructure charges reflected any relief granted under this mechanism during the reference period is a fact-specific question outside this brief's captured text.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: "The COVID-19 pandemic has led to a sharp drop in rail traffic because of a significant fall in demand and direct measures taken by the Member States to contain the pandemic." *Source: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2020/2180, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020R2180*

FACT: "These circumstances are beyond the control of railway undertakings that have continuously faced considerable liquidity problems, major losses and in some cases are risking insolvency." *Source: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2020/2180, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020R2180*

FACT: "It thus appears that the reduction in the level of rail traffic as compared to the level in the corresponding period in the previous years, for which 2019 provides the reference values in accordance with Article 5(1) and (2) of Regulation (EU) 2020/1429, is persisting and that this situation is the result of the impact of the COVID-19 outbreak." *Source: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2020/2180, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020R2180*

*Analytical inference:* the Commission's stated basis for extending the reference period was persisting rail-traffic reduction attributable to COVID-19, measured against 2019 reference values under the underlying Regulation's own Article 5(1) and (2), not a new or separate finding specific to this amending act.

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

FACT: "Such positive effects will likely materialise no earlier than from the second half of 2021." *Source: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2020/2180, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020R2180*

*Analytical inference:* this forecast is now historical rather than forward-looking: the "second half of 2021" the recital anticipated has long since passed, and the captured text records no further extension of the reference period beyond 30 June 2021 (Section 8).

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Is this Regulation still in force / operative today?**

*Analytical inference:* the reference period it extends ended 30 June 2021 (Section 8); the captured text states no further extension, so the operative relief window described here is closed as of this document's generation date.

**Q2: Does this Regulation create a direct duty on a freight forwarder?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* no duty-holder language naming a freight forwarder, carrier, or logistics intermediary appears in the captured text; the mechanism runs from Member States to infrastructure managers (Section 4).

# 8. Substantive Requirements

**1. Extended reference-period applicability clause (replaces Article 1 of Regulation (EU) 2020/1429).** FACT: "This Regulation lays down temporary rules on the levying of charges for the use of railway infrastructure as set out in Chapter IV of Directive 2012/34/EU. It applies to the use of railway infrastructure for domestic and international rail services covered by that Directive, during the period from 1 March 2020 until 30 June 2021 (“the reference period”)." *Source: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2020/2180, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020R2180*

*Operational implication:* the "applies to" language scopes the underlying Regulation (EU) 2020/1429's own relief mechanism (Section 2), not a duty this amending Regulation itself imposes on any freight forwarder, railway undertaking, or infrastructure manager.

**2. Underlying permissive relief mechanism.** FACT: "Regulation (EU) 2020/1429 enables Member States to authorise infrastructure managers to reduce, waive or defer charges for accessing rail infrastructure." *Source: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2020/2180, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020R2180*

**3. Original (pre-extension) reference period.** FACT: "This possibility had been granted from 1 March 2020 until 31 December 2020 (‘the reference period’)." *Source: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2020/2180, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020R2180*

**4. Extension rationale and new end date.** FACT: "It is therefore necessary to extend the reference period established in Article 1 of the Regulation until the end of June 2021." *Source: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2020/2180, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020R2180*

**Penalty summary.** GAP: no verbatim penalty, fine, or sanction statement appears anywhere in this Regulation's captured text; this is a relief-mechanism extension, not an enforcement instrument.

**Qualification accounting.** Per-year trajectory: No phase-in is stated in Articles 1 to 2. Exceptions and carve-outs: No exceptions are stated in Articles 1 to 2. Scope limits: No scope limits are stated in Articles 1 to 2.

Obligations surveyed: 5; workspace-adjacent: 4; extracted as FACT: 4.

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

GAP: no registration or reporting obligation for railway undertakings, infrastructure managers, or freight intermediaries appears anywhere in this Regulation's captured text.

# 11. Operational System Requirements

*Operational implication:* because the reference period this Regulation extended has already closed (30 June 2021, Section 8), no ongoing monitoring is required; a workspace reconciling historical rail-infrastructure invoices from the 1 March 2020 to 30 June 2021 window may reference this Regulation to confirm the relief-eligible window's correct end date.

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

FACT: "This delegated Regulation is foreseen to enter into force after the end of the reference period currently envisaged in Article 1 of Regulation (EU) 2020/1429. In order to avoid legal uncertainty this Regulation should be adopted under the urgency procedure detailed under Article 7 of the Regulation" *Source: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2020/2180, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020R2180*

*Analytical inference:* the urgency procedure was invoked because this amending Regulation was adopted close to the original 31 December 2020 end date, so ordinary adoption timing would have left a gap between the original reference period's expiry and this extension's entry into force.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 1 March 2020: original and extended reference period start date (Article 1 of Regulation (EU) 2020/1429, as replaced).
- 31 December 2020: original reference period end date, before this extension.
- 18 December 2020: this amending Regulation adopted.
- 30 June 2021: extended reference period end date (Article 1 of Regulation (EU) 2020/1429, as replaced by this Regulation).

*Source for timeline entries: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2020/2180, EUR-Lex (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020R2180).*

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks Commission Decision 2006/944/EC of 14 December 2006, an EU institutional decision allocating Kyoto Protocol greenhouse-gas emission budgets among the Community and its Member States for the Protocol's first quantified emission limitation and reduction commitment period. FACT: "COMMISSION DECISION of 14 December 2006 determining the respective emission levels allocated to the Community and each of its Member States under the Kyoto Protocol pursuant to Council Decision 2002/358/EC (notified under document number C(2006) 6468) (2006/944/EC)" *Source: Commission Decision 2006/944/EC, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32006D0944*

FACT: "Done at Brussels, 14 December 2006." *Source: Commission Decision 2006/944/EC, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32006D0944*

*Analytical inference:* this is a Member-State-to-Member-State GHG accounting instrument, not a private-party compliance instrument; it creates no direct duty on a freight-forwarding workspace. It is tracked here for the sustainability-intelligence platform's institutional-history coverage of EU/Kyoto carbon-accounting mechanisms, the same family of mechanism later instruments (EU ETS, CBAM) build on.

This document is scoped to the captured Decision's own recitals and three operative articles; it does not include the full Annex (the per-Member-State emission-level table beyond the figures quoted in Section 8), Council Decision 2002/358/EC, Commission Decision 2005/166/EC, or the Kyoto Protocol itself, none of which are in this item's captured pool.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "HAS ADOPTED THIS DECISION: Article 1 The emission levels in terms of tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent allocated to the Community and to Member States for the first quantified emission limitation and reduction commitment period under the Kyoto Protocol are set out in the Annex." *Source: Commission Decision 2006/944/EC, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32006D0944*

*Legal Confirmation Required:* "applies to the workspace" in the ordinary sense of this document's own section title does not hold here: the Decision allocates emission budgets between the Community and Member States as sovereign accounting parties; it does not name or address any private operator, carrier, or freight forwarder. Whether any specific downstream instrument that DOES bind private operators (a national ETS implementing measure, for example) traces back to this allocation is outside this brief's captured text.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

**MONITORING.** No immediate action arises. This is a historical accounting decision covering the Kyoto Protocol's first commitment period; the captured text states no ongoing duty running to a freight-forwarding workspace.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

FACT: "This Decision is addressed to the Member States." *Source: Commission Decision 2006/944/EC, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32006D0944*

*Analytical inference:* the addressee class is exhaustively "the Member States" (Article 3); a freight forwarder, carrier, or logistics intermediary is not a duty holder under this Decision on the captured text, and holds no assigned-amount-unit account of its own under the mechanism described in Section 8.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: "These emission levels are calculated on the basis of the revised base-year emissions data submitted by Member States pursuant to Article 23 of Commission Decision 2005/166/EC of 10 February 2005 laying down rules implementing Decision 280/2004/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council concerning a mechanism for monitoring Community greenhouse gas emissions and for implementing the Kyoto Protocol" *Source: Commission Decision 2006/944/EC, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32006D0944*

*Analytical inference:* the calculation method traces to a separate implementing instrument (Commission Decision 2005/166/EC) this brief's pool does not itself carry; the resulting per-Member-State figures are reported in Section 8's Annex excerpt rather than re-derived here.

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

FACT: "Any changes in the final emission levels of the Community and its Member States resulting from the review of the emission levels pursuant to Article 8 of the Kyoto Protocol should be specified through an amendment to this Decision." *Source: Commission Decision 2006/944/EC, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32006D0944*

*Analytical inference:* this recital describes the Decision's own amendment mechanism (a future review under Kyoto Protocol Article 8 could trigger a formal amendment to this Decision); the captured text records no such amendment having in fact issued, and no further Kyoto-Protocol-specific event beyond the first commitment period is stated in this pool.

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does this Decision create a direct duty on a freight forwarder or carrier?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* no. On the captured text, the sole addressee class is the Member States (Section 4); no private-operator duty-holder language appears anywhere in the pool.

**Q2: Does this Decision allocate anything to a private entity?**

FACT: "In recognition of Denmark’s special situation, resulting from its unusually low base-year emissions and having one of the highest quantified emission reduction obligations pursuant to Annex II to Decision 2002/358/EC, the Community should forward 5 million assigned amount units to Denmark." *Source: Commission Decision 2006/944/EC, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32006D0944*

*Analytical inference:* no; the 5 million assigned-amount-unit transfer described above runs from the Community to Denmark's own Kyoto Protocol registry account -- a Member State to Member State (via the Community) transfer, not a transfer to any private party.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: this Decision has no requirement running to a freight-forwarding workspace; "substantive requirements" here means the Decision's own stated obligations between the Community and its Member States, retained for the sustainability-intelligence platform's institutional-history coverage of the EU/Kyoto carbon-accounting mechanism.*

**1. Emission-level allocation (Article 1).** FACT: "HAS ADOPTED THIS DECISION: Article 1 The emission levels in terms of tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent allocated to the Community and to Member States for the first quantified emission limitation and reduction commitment period under the Kyoto Protocol are set out in the Annex." *Source: Commission Decision 2006/944/EC, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32006D0944*

**2. Assigned-amount-unit issuance and Denmark transfer (Article 2).** FACT: "The difference of 11 393 397 tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent between the emission levels of the Community and the sum of the emission levels of the Member States listed in Annex II to Decision 2002/358/EC shall be issued as assigned amount units by the Community. The Commission shall instruct the Central Administrator of the Community registry to transfer five million (5 000 000) of these assigned amount units to the Party to the Kyoto Protocol holding account in the registry of Denmark." *Source: Commission Decision 2006/944/EC, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32006D0944*

**3. Cyprus/Malta exception to the accession commitment mechanism.** FACT: "Annex B to the Kyoto Protocol sets quantified emission limitation or reduction commitments for the purpose of determining the emission levels allocated to the Member States that acceded to the Community after 25 April 2002, except Cyprus and Malta which do not yet have quantified emission limitation or reduction commitments under the Kyoto Protocol." *Source: Commission Decision 2006/944/EC, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32006D0944*

**Penalty summary.** GAP: no verbatim penalty, fine, or sanction statement appears anywhere in this Decision's captured text; this is an inter-governmental accounting allocation, not an enforcement instrument.

**Qualification accounting.** Per-year trajectory: No phase-in is stated in Articles 1 to 3. Exceptions and carve-outs: CAPTURED above (obligation 3, the Cyprus/Malta exception). Scope limits: No scope limits are stated in Articles 1 to 3.

Obligations surveyed: 3; workspace-adjacent: 3; extracted as FACT: 3.

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

GAP: no registration or reporting obligation for a freight forwarder, carrier, or logistics intermediary appears anywhere in this Decision's captured text; the only reporting referenced (Member States' base-year emissions data submitted pursuant to Article 23 of Decision 2005/166/EC, Section 5) runs from Member States to the Commission, not from any private operator.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 14 December 2006: Decision adopted (Done at Brussels clause and instrument title).
- 16.12.2006: Decision published in the Official Journal of the European Union, L 358/87 (OJ header metadata; the captured text states no separate entry-into-force clause of its own, consistent with a Decision addressed to Member States taking effect on notification rather than a published in-force date).

*Source for timeline entries: Commission Decision 2006/944/EC, EUR-Lex (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32006D0944).*

# 15. Sources

|---|---|---|---|

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2023/2122 of 12 October 2023, which amends the EU ETS Monitoring and Reporting Regulation (Implementing Regulation (EU) 2018/2066) to add new monitoring and reporting rules for a separate, parallel emissions trading system covering fuels used in buildings, road transport, and additional sectors ("ETS2"). FACT: "COMMISSION IMPLEMENTING REGULATION (EU) 2023/2122 of 12 October 2023 amending Implementing Regulation (EU) 2018/2066 as regards updating the monitoring and reporting of greenhouse gas emissions pursuant to Directive 2003/87/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council (Text with EEA relevance)" *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2023/2122, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023R2122*

FACT: "Done at Brussels, 12 October 2023." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2023/2122, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023R2122*

FACT: "This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union" *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2023/2122, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023R2122*

FACT: "It shall apply from 1 January 2024. However, Article 1, points (24), (25)(a)(iii), (25)(d), (27), (30)(a), (31), (33), (34)(d) and (35) shall apply from 1 July 2024." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2023/2122, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023R2122*

This document is scoped to the captured amending Regulation's own recitals and the operative text quoted below (the new Chapters VIIa/VIIb and Annexes IIa, Xa, and Xb it inserts into Implementing Regulation (EU) 2018/2066); it does not include the full text of the underlying Implementing Regulation (EU) 2018/2066 as consolidated, Directive 2003/87/EC, or Directives (EU) 2023/958 and (EU) 2023/959, none of which are in this item's captured pool.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "The amendment also introduces a separate but parallel emissions trading system applied to fuels used for combustion in the buildings and road transport sectors as well as in additional sectors which correspond to industrial activities not covered by Annex I to Directive 2003/87/EC (‘buildings, road transport and additional sectors’)." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2023/2122, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023R2122*

*Operational implication:* the new "road transport" leg of this parallel scheme (ETS2) monitors and reports emissions from fuels used in road transport combustion; a workspace operating or contracting road freight in the EU should treat this as the monitoring-and-reporting backbone for a carbon cost that its road-transport fuel suppliers will increasingly pass through, even though the workspace itself is not the duty holder described in Section 8.

FACT: "This Regulation shall apply to the monitoring and reporting of greenhouse gas emissions specified in relation to the activities listed in Annexes I and III to Directive 2003/87/EC, to activity data from stationary installations, to aviation activities and to released fuel amounts from activities referred to in Annex III to that Directive. It shall apply to emissions, activity data and released fuel amounts occurring from 1 January 2021." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2023/2122, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023R2122*

FACT: "This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2023/2122, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023R2122*

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

**COST ALERT.** The new ETS2 monitoring and reporting scheme for buildings, road transport, and additional sectors started 1 January 2025 (Section 8); a workspace with EU road-freight fuel exposure should confirm whether its fuel suppliers are registered "regulated entities" under this framework and how any resulting carbon cost is being passed through, since the reporting chain (Section 10) traces fuel from regulated entities down to end users. *Operational implication:* this is a cost-pass-through and data-traceability concern, not a workspace compliance deadline of the workspace's own.

**MONITORING.** Competent authorities must report to the Commission by 30 June 2026 on the practical application of one specific measurement-derogation method (Section 6); this may refine, but on the captured text does not yet change, the tiered monitoring requirements described in Section 8.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the duty-holder classes on the captured text are "regulated entities" (upstream fuel suppliers who release fuel for consumption in the buildings/road-transport/additional-sectors scheme), "operators" of stationary installations, aircraft operators, and Member States (for penalties and reporting to the Commission). A freight forwarder acting purely as a logistics intermediary is not named as a duty holder in the captured text; whether a specific workspace activity (owning fuel storage, importing fuel, or operating its own aircraft or vessels) places it within the "regulated entity", "operator", "aircraft operator", or "shipping company" classes is a fact-specific question requiring counsel review.

*Analytical inference:* Annex Xb (Section 10) shows the reporting chain naming "the aircraft operator and shipping company" as possible downstream fuel recipients a regulated entity must identify -- a workspace that itself operates aircraft or vessels could appear in a regulated entity's own downstream reporting, even without being a regulated entity itself.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: "In order to reduce administrative burden, this reporting should be an extension of the reporting of fuels with zero emissions factor, without establishing a separate reporting mechanism." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2023/2122, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023R2122*

FACT: "Therefore, in order to facilitate the reporting of emissions of aircraft operators to Member States, and subsequently to the ICAO Secretariat, it is appropriate to establish a preliminary emission factor solely for the purpose of a calculation for deciding about the inclusion of aircraft operators in CORSIA." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2023/2122, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023R2122*

*Analytical inference:* both provisions above concern aviation-specific monitoring refinements (sustainable aviation fuel reporting and the CORSIA inclusion-threshold calculation) that sit alongside, not inside, the road-transport-facing ETS2 provisions in Section 8; they are relevant to a workspace that itself operates aircraft, not to road-freight operations.

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

1. FACT: "The competent authorities shall report to the Commission by 30 June 2026 on the practical application and levels of uncertainty of the method referred to in that point." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2023/2122, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023R2122* *Operational implication:* this is a Member-State-to-Commission reporting duty about a specific tier-derogation method's practical application, not a workspace-facing deadline; its outcome could refine (tighten or relax) the tiered monitoring requirements in Section 8 after 30 June 2026.

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Is a freight forwarder itself a "regulated entity" under this framework?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* on the captured text, a regulated entity is the party that releases fuel for consumption in the buildings/road-transport/additional-sectors scheme (typically an upstream fuel supplier); a freight forwarder that purchases fuel or contracts road haulage is, absent additional facts, a downstream consumer rather than a regulated entity itself. Confirming a specific workspace's status requires review of its own fuel-handling activities against Directive 2003/87/EC's own "regulated entity" definition, which is not in this item's captured pool.

**Q2: Does this Regulation create a direct penalty risk for a freight forwarder?**

FACT: "In order to ensure the accurate monitoring and reporting of emissions covered by Chapter IVa of Directive 2003/87/EC, Member States shall establish measures against fraud and determine the penalties to be imposed in the event of fraud which are commensurate with their purpose and which have an adequate deterrent effect." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2023/2122, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023R2122* *Analytical inference:* no, on the captured text the duty to establish fraud measures and penalties runs to Member States, targeted at fraud in the monitoring and reporting of emissions covered by the ETS2 scheme -- not a penalty stated to run directly against a freight forwarder.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

**1. Amended monitoring-and-reporting scope (Article 2 of the underlying Regulation, as replaced).** FACT: "This Regulation shall apply to the monitoring and reporting of greenhouse gas emissions specified in relation to the activities listed in Annexes I and III to Directive 2003/87/EC, to activity data from stationary installations, to aviation activities and to released fuel amounts from activities referred to in Annex III to that Directive. It shall apply to emissions, activity data and released fuel amounts occurring from 1 January 2021." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2023/2122, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023R2122*

**2. New parallel ETS2 scheme for buildings, road transport, and additional sectors.** FACT: "The amendment also introduces a separate but parallel emissions trading system applied to fuels used for combustion in the buildings and road transport sectors as well as in additional sectors which correspond to industrial activities not covered by Annex I to Directive 2003/87/EC (‘buildings, road transport and additional sectors’)." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2023/2122, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023R2122*

**3. ETS2 monitoring/reporting start date and permit deadline.** FACT: "The monitoring and reporting for the new emissions trading system for buildings, road transport and additional sectors will start on 1 January 2025. However, pursuant to Article 30f(4) of Directive 2003/87/EC, regulated entities are to report historical emissions for 2024 and, pursuant to Article 30b of that Directive, those entities are to submit their monitoring plans in order to apply for a greenhouse gas permit which needs to be issued by 1 January 2025." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2023/2122, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023R2122*

**4. Monitoring plan submission timing for a regulated entity.** FACT: "At the latest 4 months before a regulated entity commences the activity covered by Annex III to Directive 2003/87/EC, it shall submit to the competent authority a monitoring plan for approval, unless the competent authority has set an alternative time limit for this submission." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2023/2122, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023R2122*

**5. Operator biomass-fraction data duty.** FACT: "the operator shall provide to the competent authority data on the biomass fraction of the carbon content of the output streams." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2023/2122, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023R2122*

**6. Member State fraud-prevention and penalty duty.** FACT: "In order to ensure the accurate monitoring and reporting of emissions covered by Chapter IVa of Directive 2003/87/EC, Member States shall establish measures against fraud and determine the penalties to be imposed in the event of fraud which are commensurate with their purpose and which have an adequate deterrent effect." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2023/2122, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023R2122*

**7. Fuel-supplier-chain reporting (Annex Xa, operator-level).** FACT: "Together with the information contained in the annual emission report pursuant to Annex X to this Regulation, the operator shall submit a report with the following information for each purchased fuel as defined in Article 3(af) of Directive 2003/87/EC: (a) name, address and unique permit number of the fuel supplier which is registered as regulated entity. In cases where the fuel supplier is not a regulated entity, the operators shall submit, where available, a list of all suppliers of fuels, from direct fuel suppliers up to the regulated entity, including their name, address and unique permit number;" *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2023/2122, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023R2122*

**8. Downstream fuel-recipient reporting (Annex Xb, regulated-entity-level).** FACT: "Together with the information contained in the annual emission report pursuant to Annex X to this Regulation, the regulated entity shall submit a report with the following information for each purchased fuel as defined in Article 3, point (af), of Directive 2003/87/EC: (a) name, address and unique permit number of the operator and, where relevant, the aircraft operator and shipping company, to whom the fuel is released." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2023/2122, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023R2122*

**9. This amending Regulation's own application dates.** FACT: "It shall apply from 1 January 2024. However, Article 1, points (24), (25)(a)(iii), (25)(d), (27), (30)(a), (31), (33), (34)(d) and (35) shall apply from 1 July 2024." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2023/2122, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023R2122*

**10. Biogas double-counting derogation (exception).** FACT: "By way of derogation from paragraphs 1 and 2 of this Article and Article 30, except for the purposes of Article 43(4), the operator shall not use analyses or estimation methods in accordance with paragraph 2 of this Article to determine the biomass fraction of natural gas received from a gas grid to which biogas is added." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2023/2122, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023R2122*

**11. Scope-factor tier requirement.** FACT: "Article 75i Applicable tiers for the scope factor 1. When defining the relevant tiers for fuel streams, to determine the scope factor, each regulated entity shall apply the highest tier as defined in Annex IIa." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2023/2122, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023R2122*

**Penalty summary.** FACT: "In order to ensure the accurate monitoring and reporting of emissions covered by Chapter IVa of Directive 2003/87/EC, Member States shall establish measures against fraud and determine the penalties to be imposed in the event of fraud which are commensurate with their purpose and which have an adequate deterrent effect." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2023/2122, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023R2122* *Legal Confirmation Required:* the captured text states a duty on Member States to set commensurate, adequately deterrent penalties for fraud; it does not itself state a specific penalty amount or range, which would be set by each Member State's own implementing measures, not captured in this pool.

**Qualification accounting.** Per-year trajectory: CAPTURED (see metadata.requirement_trajectory: entry into force, 1 January 2024 general application, 1 July 2024 ETS2 provisions application, 1 January 2025 ETS2 monitoring/reporting start, 30 June 2026 competent-authority review report). Exceptions and carve-outs: CAPTURED above (obligation 10, the biogas double-counting derogation's unnegated "except for the purposes of Article 43(4)"). Scope limits: CAPTURED above (obligation 11, the unnegated "scope factor" tier requirement).

Obligations surveyed: 11; workspace-adjacent: 11; extracted as FACT: 11.

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

FACT: "The monitoring and reporting for the new emissions trading system for buildings, road transport and additional sectors will start on 1 January 2025. However, pursuant to Article 30f(4) of Directive 2003/87/EC, regulated entities are to report historical emissions for 2024 and, pursuant to Article 30b of that Directive, those entities are to submit their monitoring plans in order to apply for a greenhouse gas permit which needs to be issued by 1 January 2025." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2023/2122, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023R2122*

FACT: "At the latest 4 months before a regulated entity commences the activity covered by Annex III to Directive 2003/87/EC, it shall submit to the competent authority a monitoring plan for approval, unless the competent authority has set an alternative time limit for this submission." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2023/2122, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023R2122*

FACT: "Together with the information contained in the annual emission report pursuant to Annex X to this Regulation, the operator shall submit a report with the following information for each purchased fuel as defined in Article 3(af) of Directive 2003/87/EC: (a) name, address and unique permit number of the fuel supplier which is registered as regulated entity. In cases where the fuel supplier is not a regulated entity, the operators shall submit, where available, a list of all suppliers of fuels, from direct fuel suppliers up to the regulated entity, including their name, address and unique permit number;" *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2023/2122, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023R2122*

FACT: "Together with the information contained in the annual emission report pursuant to Annex X to this Regulation, the regulated entity shall submit a report with the following information for each purchased fuel as defined in Article 3, point (af), of Directive 2003/87/EC: (a) name, address and unique permit number of the operator and, where relevant, the aircraft operator and shipping company, to whom the fuel is released." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2023/2122, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023R2122*

*Operational implication:* the reporting chain runs regulated entity (upstream fuel supplier) -> Annex Xb report naming downstream operators/aircraft operators/shipping companies -> those parties' own Annex Xa reports naming their fuel suppliers back up the chain; a workspace that is itself named in either direction of this chain should expect to receive or provide the name/address/permit-number data described above, even without being a regulated entity itself.

# 11. Operational System Requirements

*Operational implication:* a workspace with EU road-freight fuel exposure should (1) confirm whether its principal road-transport fuel suppliers are registered ETS2 "regulated entities" and hold the required greenhouse gas permit (due 1 January 2025, Section 8), (2) watch for the competent authorities' 30 June 2026 report on the tier-derogation method (Section 6), which could affect the granularity of cost data fuel suppliers can offer, and (3) expect to appear, where relevant, in a regulated entity's or operator's own Annex Xa/Xb chain-of-custody reporting (Section 10) if the workspace itself operates aircraft or vessels or holds a direct fuel-supply relationship.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

FACT: "By way of derogation from paragraphs 1 and 2 of this Article and Article 30, except for the purposes of Article 43(4), the operator shall not use analyses or estimation methods in accordance with paragraph 2 of this Article to determine the biomass fraction of natural gas received from a gas grid to which biogas is added." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2023/2122, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023R2122*

FACT: "For de minimis fuel streams, the regulated entity may determine released fuel amounts and each calculation factor by using conservative estimates instead of using tiers, unless a defined tier is achievable without additional effort." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2023/2122, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023R2122*

*Analytical inference:* both provisions above reduce monitoring burden in specific, narrow cases (a gas-grid biogas double-counting scenario, and de minimis fuel streams generally); neither creates a broader carve-out from the ETS2 scheme's own scope described in Section 8.

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

FACT: "In order to reduce administrative burden, this reporting should be an extension of the reporting of fuels with zero emissions factor, without establishing a separate reporting mechanism." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2023/2122, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023R2122*

FACT: "Therefore, in order to facilitate the reporting of emissions of aircraft operators to Member States, and subsequently to the ICAO Secretariat, it is appropriate to establish a preliminary emission factor solely for the purpose of a calculation for deciding about the inclusion of aircraft operators in CORSIA." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2023/2122, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023R2122*

*Analytical inference:* a workspace tracking sustainable aviation fuel uptake or CORSIA compliance for its own aircraft operations should read these two provisions together with the EU's own SAF-attribution rules under Directive (EU) 2023/958, which this brief's captured pool does not itself include.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 12 October 2023: Regulation adopted (Done at Brussels clause and instrument title).
- 18.10.2023: Regulation published in the Official Journal of the European Union (OJ header metadata; entry into force follows on the twentieth day after this date per Article 2).
- 1 January 2024: general application date of this amending Regulation.
- 1 July 2024: the new ETS2 monitoring provisions (Chapters VIIa/VIIb) and Annexes Xa/Xb become applicable.
- 1 January 2025: ETS2 monitoring and reporting for buildings, road transport, and additional sectors starts; greenhouse gas permits for regulated entities are due to be issued by this date.
- 30 June 2026: competent authorities are due to report to the Commission on the practical application and levels of uncertainty of the tier-derogation method described in Section 6.

*Source for timeline entries: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2023/2122, EUR-Lex (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023R2122).*

metadata.what_is_it: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2023/2122 of 12 October 2023, amending the EU ETS Monitoring and Reporting Regulation to add new monitoring and reporting rules for a parallel emissions trading system (ETS2) covering fuels used in buildings road transport and additional sectors, alongside biomass-accounting and aviation monitoring updates to the existing EU ETS.
metadata.why_matters: ETS2 monitoring and reporting for road-transport fuel started 1 January 2025; a workspace with EU road-freight fuel exposure should expect its fuel suppliers to be registered regulated entities under this framework and should track how the resulting carbon cost and chain-of-custody reporting flow through to the workspace even though the workspace itself is not the named duty holder.
key_data: ETS2 monitoring and reporting for buildings road transport and additional sectors starts 1 January 2025
Greenhouse gas permits for regulated entities must be issued by 1 January 2025
ETS2 regulated-entity provisions apply from 1 July 2024
Competent authorities must report to the Commission by 30 June 2026 on one tier-derogation method
Member States must set fraud penalties that are commensurate and have an adequate deterrent effect
metadata.cost_mechanism: Upstream fuel suppliers registered as ETS2 regulated entities surrender allowances for fuel released for consumption in road transport and buildings which is expected to be reflected in the price of the fuel sold to downstream users including road-freight operators.

The new ETS2 monitoring chapters (VIIa/VIIb) and Annexes Xa/Xb become applicable
ETS2 monitoring and reporting for buildings road transport and additional sectors starts and greenhouse gas permits must be issued
