entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks The Harbour Works (Environmental Impact Assessment) Regulations 1999 (UK SI 1999/3445), which set the environmental impact assessment process a developer follows before carrying out harbour works below the low water mark of medium tides in England, Wales, and Scotland. FACT: "The Harbour Works (Environmental Impact Assessment) Regulations 1999" *Source: The Harbour Works (Environmental Impact Assessment) Regulations 1999, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/1999/3445*

FACT: "These Regulations may be cited as the Harbour Works (Environmental Impact Assessment) Regulations 1999, and shall come into force on 1st February 2000." *Source: The Harbour Works (Environmental Impact Assessment) Regulations 1999, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/1999/3445*

FACT: "These Regulations shall not extend to Northern Ireland." *Source: The Harbour Works (Environmental Impact Assessment) Regulations 1999, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/1999/3445*

This document is scoped to the captured Regulations' own Parts I, II, and the Part III amendments to the Harbours Act 1964 quoted below; it does not include the full Schedules 1 through 3 (the detailed environmental-statement content list and the Harbours Act 1964 procedural schedule), Council Directive 85/337/EEC, or Council Directive 97/11/EC, none of which are in this item's captured pool.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "Scope 3. This Part applies to harbour works below the low water mark of medium tides, being works which are— (a) not subject to planning control pursuant to the Town and Country Planning Act 1990" *Source: The Harbour Works (Environmental Impact Assessment) Regulations 1999, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/1999/3445*

*Operational implication:* a workspace with UK port or harbour infrastructure exposure -- new berths, dredging, land reclamation, or other below-low-water-mark works -- should treat any such project as falling within this EIA process unless one of the exclusions in Regulation 3 (planning control, an existing harbour order, or another named consent route) applies.

FACT: "Harbour works constituting a project which is of a description mentioned in Annex II to the Directive shall be treated for the purposes of this Part as not falling within that Annex unless— (a) the area of the harbour works exceeds 1 hectare, (b) any part of the harbour works is to be carried out in a sensitive area, or (c) the appropriate Authority determines that the harbour works constituting the project shall be treated for the purposes of this Part as falling within that Annex." *Source: The Harbour Works (Environmental Impact Assessment) Regulations 1999, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/1999/3445*

*Analytical inference:* the 1-hectare area threshold and the "sensitive area" test are the practical screening line: a harbour works project under 1 hectare, outside a sensitive area, and not itself flagged by the appropriate Authority, sits outside the Annex II EIA requirement even where the underlying Directive's Annex II would otherwise capture it.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

**MONITORING.** No new near-term deadline arises from this instrument on its own; it is a long-standing, in-force procedural framework (commenced 1st February 2000). A workspace planning harbour works should build the Regulation 7 notice-and-consultation timeline (Section 8) into its project schedule from the outset, since it adds firm minimum periods (14, 42, and 7 days) before consent can be granted.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

FACT: "“developer” means any person who proposes to carry out or who carries out harbour works;" *Source: The Harbour Works (Environmental Impact Assessment) Regulations 1999, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/1999/3445*

*Analytical inference:* "developer" is defined broadly enough to capture any person proposing or carrying out harbour works, including a port operator, harbour authority, or a workspace client undertaking its own port infrastructure project; the duty holder is not limited to a named category of entity.

FACT: "“the appropriate Authority” means— (a) as regards harbour works relating to fishery harbours in England, the Minister of Agriculture, Fisheries and Food; (b) as regards harbour works relating to fishery harbours in Wales, the National Assembly for Wales; (c) as regards any other harbour works in England or Wales, the Secretary of State for the Environment, Transport and the Regions; (d) as regards harbour works in Scotland, the Scottish Ministers;" *Source: The Harbour Works (Environmental Impact Assessment) Regulations 1999, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/1999/3445*

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a specific workspace activity (planning, financing, or operationally directing a harbour works project on a client's behalf) itself places the workspace within the "developer" duty-holder class, as opposed to acting purely as a logistics or advisory intermediary to a client who is the developer, is a fact-specific question requiring counsel review.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: "the appropriate Authority shall give the opinion requested under paragraph (1) as soon as reasonably practicable." *Source: The Harbour Works (Environmental Impact Assessment) Regulations 1999, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/1999/3445*

*Operational implication:* a developer uncertain whether a proposed harbour works project needs an environmental statement can request the appropriate Authority's opinion before committing to the full Regulation 5/6 application process; the captured text sets no fixed response deadline, only "as soon as reasonably practicable."

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

GAP: no forward-looking event, scheduled review, or pending amendment is stated anywhere in this instrument's captured text; it is a long-standing, unamended-in-this-pool procedural framework.

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does a proposed harbour works project automatically require an environmental statement?**

*Analytical inference:* no; the Annex II screening threshold (Section 2) means only projects exceeding 1 hectare, located in a sensitive area, or specifically flagged by the appropriate Authority require the full process; smaller projects outside a sensitive area may fall outside it.

**Q2: Is a workspace penalised directly for a harbour authority's or developer's non-compliance?**

FACT: "A person who issues a certificate purporting to comply with regulation 7(4) which contains a statement which he knows to be false or misleading in a material particular, or who recklessly issues a certificate purporting to comply with regulation 7(4) which contains a statement which is false or misleading in a material particular shall be guilty of an offence and liable on summary conviction to a fine not exceeding level 3 on the standard scale." *Source: The Harbour Works (Environmental Impact Assessment) Regulations 1999, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/1999/3445* *Legal Confirmation Required:* the penalty runs to the person who issues a false or misleading certificate or who fails to comply with a served notice (Section 8); whether a specific workspace role in a harbour works project could expose it to either duty requires counsel review of the workspace's own role.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

**1. Commencement.** FACT: "These Regulations may be cited as the Harbour Works (Environmental Impact Assessment) Regulations 1999, and shall come into force on 1st February 2000." *Source: The Harbour Works (Environmental Impact Assessment) Regulations 1999, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/1999/3445*

**2. Scope (below-low-water-mark harbour works).** FACT: "Scope 3. This Part applies to harbour works below the low water mark of medium tides, being works which are— (a) not subject to planning control pursuant to the Town and Country Planning Act 1990" *Source: The Harbour Works (Environmental Impact Assessment) Regulations 1999, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/1999/3445* *Operational implication:* this "applies to" clause is the Part II applicability test; a project outside it (subject to planning control, or already authorised by a harbour order or other named consent route) falls outside this instrument's own process.

**3. Annex II 1-hectare / sensitive-area screening threshold.** FACT: "Harbour works constituting a project which is of a description mentioned in Annex II to the Directive shall be treated for the purposes of this Part as not falling within that Annex unless— (a) the area of the harbour works exceeds 1 hectare, (b) any part of the harbour works is to be carried out in a sensitive area, or (c) the appropriate Authority determines that the harbour works constituting the project shall be treated for the purposes of this Part as falling within that Annex." *Source: The Harbour Works (Environmental Impact Assessment) Regulations 1999, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/1999/3445*

**4. Screening-opinion response timing.** FACT: "the appropriate Authority shall give the opinion requested under paragraph (1) as soon as reasonably practicable." *Source: The Harbour Works (Environmental Impact Assessment) Regulations 1999, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/1999/3445*

**5. Developer notification / approval-block duty.** FACT: "the developer shall notify the appropriate Authority of the application, and (ii) the approval shall not be granted and the developer shall not commence the proposed harbour works, unless paragraph (3) or (7) applies or the appropriate Authority consents to the carrying out of the proposed harbour works under regulation 10(2)." *Source: The Harbour Works (Environmental Impact Assessment) Regulations 1999, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/1999/3445*

**6. Developer public-notice duty (14-day pre-notice period).** FACT: "Not less than 14 days before the developer provides the information to be supplied under regulation 5(9) or 6(11) to the appropriate Authority, he shall publish a notice in a local newspaper circulating in the locality of the harbour where the harbour works are proposed to be carried out, stating" *Source: The Harbour Works (Environmental Impact Assessment) Regulations 1999, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/1999/3445*

**7. Document-inspection availability window (42-day minimum).** FACT: "the latest date on which they will be available (being a date not less than 42 days later than the date on which the notice is published);" *Source: The Harbour Works (Environmental Impact Assessment) Regulations 1999, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/1999/3445*

**8. Public representation window (7 days).** FACT: "that any person who wishes to make representations concerning the proposed harbour works should do so in writing, within a period of 7 days beginning with the day after the date specified in accordance with sub-paragraph (e), to the appropriate Authority." *Source: The Harbour Works (Environmental Impact Assessment) Regulations 1999, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/1999/3445*

**9. Posted-notice duty at harbour authority offices.** FACT: "the developer shall also post at a place to which members of the public have access at the offices of the harbour authority for the harbour where the harbour works are proposed to be carried out or if there is no such place, shall post outside the offices of the said harbour authority, a notice containing the information specified in paragraph (1)." *Source: The Harbour Works (Environmental Impact Assessment) Regulations 1999, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/1999/3445*

**10. EEA cross-border consultation timing.** FACT: "send to the other EEA State as soon as possible, and no later than the date of publication of that notice, the particulars mentioned in paragraph (3) and, if it thinks fit, the information mentioned in paragraph (4)" *Source: The Harbour Works (Environmental Impact Assessment) Regulations 1999, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/1999/3445*

**11. Penalty for false or misleading certification.** FACT: "A person who issues a certificate purporting to comply with regulation 7(4) which contains a statement which he knows to be false or misleading in a material particular, or who recklessly issues a certificate purporting to comply with regulation 7(4) which contains a statement which is false or misleading in a material particular shall be guilty of an offence and liable on summary conviction to a fine not exceeding level 3 on the standard scale." *Source: The Harbour Works (Environmental Impact Assessment) Regulations 1999, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/1999/3445*

**12. Penalty for failure to comply with a served notice.** FACT: "A person who fails without reasonable excuse to comply with a notice served upon him under regulation 11(1) or 12(1) shall be guilty of an offence and liable on summary conviction to a fine not exceeding level 3 on the standard scale." *Source: The Harbour Works (Environmental Impact Assessment) Regulations 1999, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/1999/3445*

**13. Revocation-with-savings exception for pending applications.** FACT: "Except in relation to an application or notice referred to in paragraph (2) or an application for a harbour revision order or harbour empowerment order referred to in paragraph (3), the following Regulations are hereby revoked" *Source: The Harbour Works (Environmental Impact Assessment) Regulations 1999, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/1999/3445*

**14. Northern Ireland territorial-extent limit.** FACT: "These Regulations shall not extend to Northern Ireland." *Source: The Harbour Works (Environmental Impact Assessment) Regulations 1999, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/1999/3445*

**Qualification accounting.** Per-year trajectory: No phase-in is stated in Sections 1 to 15 of these Regulations. Exceptions and carve-outs: CAPTURED above (obligation 13, the revocation-with-savings exception). Scope limits: CAPTURED above (obligation 2, the "Scope" heading and applicability clause; also obligation 14, the Northern Ireland territorial-extent limit).

Obligations surveyed: 14; workspace-adjacent: 14; extracted as FACT: 14.

# 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

GAP: this instrument regulates a project-approval process, not a product; no product-specific compliance status is stated anywhere in the captured text.

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

FACT: "Not less than 14 days before the developer provides the information to be supplied under regulation 5(9) or 6(11) to the appropriate Authority, he shall publish a notice in a local newspaper circulating in the locality of the harbour where the harbour works are proposed to be carried out, stating" *Source: The Harbour Works (Environmental Impact Assessment) Regulations 1999, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/1999/3445*

FACT: "the developer shall also post at a place to which members of the public have access at the offices of the harbour authority for the harbour where the harbour works are proposed to be carried out or if there is no such place, shall post outside the offices of the said harbour authority, a notice containing the information specified in paragraph (1)." *Source: The Harbour Works (Environmental Impact Assessment) Regulations 1999, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/1999/3445*

FACT: "send to the other EEA State as soon as possible, and no later than the date of publication of that notice, the particulars mentioned in paragraph (3) and, if it thinks fit, the information mentioned in paragraph (4)" *Source: The Harbour Works (Environmental Impact Assessment) Regulations 1999, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/1999/3445*

*Operational implication:* a developer's core registration-and-notice burden under this instrument is the newspaper notice, the posted notice at the harbour authority's offices, and (where a transboundary environmental effect is possible) the cross-border EEA State consultation package -- not a filing with a central regulator.

# 11. Operational System Requirements

*Operational implication:* a workspace planning or advising on UK harbour works should build a project timeline around the minimum periods in Section 8: at least 14 days of lead time before the environmental statement is provided, a document-inspection window of at least 42 days, a 7-day public representation window following that, and a 42-day minimum posting period for the notice displayed at the harbour authority's own offices -- each is a floor, not a target, so a compressed schedule risks falling short of the statutory minimum.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

FACT: "Except in relation to an application or notice referred to in paragraph (2) or an application for a harbour revision order or harbour empowerment order referred to in paragraph (3), the following Regulations are hereby revoked" *Source: The Harbour Works (Environmental Impact Assessment) Regulations 1999, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/1999/3445*

FACT: "These Regulations shall not extend to Northern Ireland." *Source: The Harbour Works (Environmental Impact Assessment) Regulations 1999, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/1999/3445*

*Analytical inference:* the revocation-with-savings clause means an application or notice made under the predecessor 1988/1989/1996 Regulations before 1st February 2000 continues under those earlier Regulations rather than this instrument; a workspace reviewing a historical harbour works file from that transition window should confirm which regime actually governed it.

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

GAP: no adjacent industry research, alternative-technology discussion, or comparative-instrument analysis appears anywhere in this instrument's captured text; it is a procedural EIA framework, not a technology or market document.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 1st February 2000: Regulations come into force (Regulation 1(1)); Part II does not apply to applications or notices made before this date, and Part III does not apply to harbour revision or empowerment order applications made before this date.
- 1999: Regulations enacted (legislation.gov.uk identifier year, from the given export timeline row).

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks Commission Regulation (EU) 2022/586 of 8 April 2022, which amends Annex XIV to Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006 (REACH) to add five substances to the REACH authorisation list. It exists to give a freight forwarder or logistics operator that handles, stores, or transports any of the five newly listed substances (or goods containing them) a single record of what the authorisation regime now requires and by when.

FACT: Done at Brussels, 8 April 2022. *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2022/586 of 8 April 2022, EUR-Lex CELEX 32022R0586. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022R0586

*Analytical inference:* this is a narrow, substance-specific REACH Annex XIV amendment rather than a general chemicals rule; its relevance to any given workspace turns on whether the workspace's own supply chain touches one of the five substances named below.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

This Regulation adds five substances to REACH's Annex XIV authorisation list because each was found, under Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008, to meet one or more of the hazard criteria in Article 57 of Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006 (toxic for reproduction, carcinogenic, or having endocrine-disrupting properties of equivalent concern).

FACT: The substance tetraethyllead meets the criteria for classification as toxic for reproduction (category 1A) in accordance with Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008 *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2022/586, recital 1. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022R0586

*Legal Confirmation Required:* Annex XIV listing under REACH means the substance's placing on the market and use are prohibited after a set sunset date unless a specific authorisation has been granted; whether a given workspace's own supply chain includes any of the five substances named in this Regulation requires the workspace's own chemical-inventory review, which is outside this brief's corpus.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

FACT: Tetraethyllead EC No: 201-075-4 CAS No: 78-00-2 Toxic for reproduction (category 1A) 1 November 2023 1 May 2025 *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2022/586, Annex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022R0586

*Operational implication:* the sunset date for all five substances added by this Regulation (1 May 2025) has already passed relative to the current date; a workspace whose supply chain includes any of the five substances should treat this as a completed compliance milestone to confirm (authorisation obtained, or the substance no longer placed on the market or used) rather than a forward deadline.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

FACT: This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States. *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2022/586, Article 2. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022R0586

*Legal Confirmation Required:* as an EU Regulation, this instrument is directly applicable without national transposition; the Article 58 authorisation duty it triggers runs to manufacturers, importers, and downstream users of the five listed substances under Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006, not to a carrier or freight forwarder as such. Whether a specific workspace's handling of goods containing one of these substances creates a downstream-user duty under REACH is a fact-specific question outside this brief's scope and requires counsel review.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: They have furthermore been prioritised for inclusion in that Annex by the European Chemicals Agency (“the Agency”) in its recommendation of 1 October 2019 *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2022/586, recital 6. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022R0586

FACT: The Agency conducted a public consultation on its draft recommendation where interested parties were invited to submit comments. *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2022/586, recital 7. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022R0586

*Per the workspace's reading:* the European Chemicals Agency's own recommendation and public-consultation process (recitals 6-7) is the controlling procedural authority behind which substances the Commission selects for Annex XIV listing in this and future amending Regulations.

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

This Regulation's own recitals name five further substance groups the Commission considered for Annex XIV listing in this same exercise but decided to postpone, each for a stated reason. These are the clearest signal in this corpus of what a future Annex XIV amendment may add.

FACT: The Commission is assessing what could be the most appropriate regulatory approach regarding those substances. It is therefore appropriate to postpone their inclusion in Annex XIV to Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006. *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2022/586, recital 13 (2-methoxyethanol / 2-ethoxyethanol). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022R0586

FACT: The Commission is assessing what could be the most appropriate regulatory approach regarding those substances. It is therefore appropriate to postpone the inclusion of those substances in Annex XIV to Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006. *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2022/586, recital 14 (HHPA / MHHPA anhydrides). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022R0586

FACT: In order to ensure a consistent regulatory approach, the outcome of those initiatives should be taken into consideration prior to taking a decision on the inclusion of “Dechlorane Plus”™ in Annex XIV to Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006. It is therefore appropriate to postpone the inclusion of that substance in Annex XIV to Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006. *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2022/586, recital 15 ("Dechlorane Plus"). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022R0586

FACT: Therefore, in view of the ongoing discussions on restriction of use of lead and its compounds as well as possible adoption of more stringent measures at the workplace, it is appropriate to postpone a decision on the inclusion of those substances in Annex XIV to Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006. *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2022/586, recital 16 (seven lead compounds in recycled PVC). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022R0586

FACT: That restriction is to cover the uses of Bisphenol A that would fall under the authorisation regime. It is therefore appropriate to postpone the inclusion of that substance in Annex XIV to Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006. *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2022/586, recital 17 (Bisphenol A). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022R0586

*Analytical inference:* none of these five postponed substance groups carries a stated future decision date in this corpus; a workspace whose supply chain touches any of them (PVC articles, Bisphenol A, the two solvents, the two anhydrides, or "Dechlorane Plus") should treat a future Annex XIV amendment as reasonably likely but undated.

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does this Regulation create a direct duty on a freight forwarder or carrier?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* No source in this brief's corpus states a duty running to a carrier, freight forwarder, or logistics intermediary as such. The Article 58 authorisation duty (Section 8) runs to manufacturers, importers, and downstream users of the five listed substances.

**Q2: Does the workspace need to know which of its shipments contain any of the five listed substances?**

*Analytical inference:* Yes, as a practical matter, if the workspace or its customers manufacture, import, or use any of the five substances (Section 9); this Regulation does not itself require the workspace to conduct that inventory, but REACH's underlying authorisation regime makes the inventory a prerequisite to knowing whether the regime applies at all.

**Q3: Are exemptions or a phase-in period available for any of the five substances?**

FACT: In accordance with the information available, it is not appropriate to set exemptions based on those provisions. *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2022/586, recital 10. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022R0586

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the Commission considered and declined to set exemptions under Article 58(1), point (e), for any of the five substances added by this Regulation; no other exemption mechanism is stated in this corpus.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

**1. Annex XIV amendment (the operative change).** FACT: Annex XIV to Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006 is amended in accordance with the Annex to this Regulation. *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2022/586, Article 1. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022R0586

**2. Authorisation/sunset-date mechanism (general Article 58 rule this Regulation applies).** FACT: a date from which the placing on the market and the use of the substance is to be prohibited unless an authorisation is granted should be set as required by Article 58(1), point (c)(i), of Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006 *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2022/586, recital 9. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022R0586

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this mechanism runs from Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006 (REACH) itself; this amending Regulation applies it to the five newly listed substances rather than creating a new mechanism of its own.

**3. Specific application and sunset dates for the five substances.** FACT: Tetraethyllead EC No: 201-075-4 CAS No: 78-00-2 Toxic for reproduction (category 1A) 1 November 2023 1 May 2025 *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2022/586, Annex (entry 55, Tetraethyllead; the same two dates, 1 November 2023 and 1 May 2025, apply to all five newly listed entries 55 through 59). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022R0586

*Operational implication:* after 1 May 2025, placing any of the five substances on the market or using them is prohibited unless a specific authorisation has been granted under Article 60 of Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006; this brief's corpus does not itself state whether any authorisation application was filed or granted for a specific substance.

**4. No exemptions set.** FACT: In accordance with the information available, it is not appropriate to set exemptions based on those provisions. *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2022/586, recital 10. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022R0586

**5. No review periods set.** FACT: it is not appropriate to set review periods referred to in Article 58(1), point (d), of that Regulation at this stage *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2022/586, recital 12. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022R0586

*Analytical inference:* the Commission declined to set Article 58(1)(d) review periods for the five substances "at this stage" (recital 12), because the available information on their uses was limited at the time of adoption; this corpus does not state whether a review period has since been added by a later amendment.

**6. Entry into force.** FACT: This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2022/586, Article 2. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022R0586

**7. Binding and directly applicable in all Member States.** FACT: This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States. *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2022/586, Article 2. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022R0586

**8. Penalty or enforcement mechanism against a private operator.** GAP: no source in this brief's corpus states a fine, penalty, or enforcement mechanism running to a manufacturer, importer, downstream user, carrier, or freight forwarder for non-compliance with the Article 58 authorisation requirement; enforcement and penalties for REACH non-compliance are established by Member States under Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006's own Title XV, which this Regulation's own text does not restate.

**Qualification accounting.** Per-year trajectory: CAPTURED (see metadata.requirement_trajectory: the two-step transitional arrangement, latest application date 1 November 2023 to sunset date 1 May 2025, uniform across all five newly listed substances). Exceptions and carve-outs: No exceptions are stated in Articles 1 to 2 of this Regulation; recital 10 records the Commission's decision not to set exemptions under Article 58(1), point (e), of Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006. Scope limits: No scope limits are stated in Articles 1 to 2 of this Regulation.

Obligations surveyed: 8; workspace-adjacent: 8; extracted as FACT: 7.
Shortfall: obligation 8 (a penalty or enforcement mechanism against a private operator) was surveyed and found genuinely absent from the captured text; recorded as a GAP claim rather than a FACT under this section.

# 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

The Annex to this Regulation lists all five substances together with their EC/CAS numbers, the Article 57 hazard property triggering listing, and the two transitional dates (latest application date and sunset date), identical across all five entries.

*No content for this section as of the export date: the captured text names no adjacent industry research body or alternative-substance program distinct from the European Chemicals Agency's own Article 58 recommendation and consultation process already covered in Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis above.*

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks The Renewable Transport Fuel Obligations (Amendment) Order 2020 (UK Statutory Instrument 2020 No. 1541), a narrow amending Order that raises the per-litre shortfall multiplier a UK renewable transport fuel obligation ("RTFO") supplier pays for a shortfall in its obligation, and makes a consequential adjustment to how a related civil penalty figure is calculated.

FACT: The Renewable Transport Fuel Obligations (Amendment) Order 2020 *Source: The Renewable Transport Fuel Obligations (Amendment) Order 2020, UK SI 2020/1541. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2020/1541

FACT: Made 15th December 2020 *Source: The Renewable Transport Fuel Obligations (Amendment) Order 2020, signature line. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2020/1541

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: This instrument amends the Renewable Transport Fuel Obligations Order 2007 *Source: The Renewable Transport Fuel Obligations (Amendment) Order 2020, Explanatory Note. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2020/1541

FACT: It amends a step of the calculation used to determine the amount a supplier must pay to discharge any shortfall in their renewable transport fuel obligation in accordance with article 21 of the RTFO Order. *Source: The Renewable Transport Fuel Obligations (Amendment) Order 2020, Explanatory Note. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2020/1541

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the duty this Order amends runs to an "obligated supplier" under the Renewable Transport Fuel Obligations Order 2007's own definition of a supplier of relevant fossil fuel or bioblend, not to a carrier or freight forwarder as such; whether a specific workspace is itself an RTFO-obligated supplier (as opposed to a purchaser of fuel from one) is a fact-specific question outside this brief's scope.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

FACT: The amendment increases the multiplier that will be applied to any shortfall in a supplier’s main renewable transport fuel obligation (as defined in article 4(6) of the RTFO Order) from £0.30 to £0.50 for obligation periods beginning on or after 1st January 2021. *Source: The Renewable Transport Fuel Obligations (Amendment) Order 2020, Explanatory Note. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2020/1541

*Operational implication:* an obligated supplier with any obligation-period shortfall arising from 1st January 2021 onward pays at the higher £0.50 multiplier rather than the prior £0.30; this is a completed rate change (both dates are already in the past relative to the current date) rather than a forward deadline, but it remains the operative rate for any obligation period since that date.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

FACT: The Secretary of State makes the following Order in exercise of the powers conferred by sections 124(1), 128(1), 129(3)(a) and 192(4)(a) of the Energy Act 2004 *Source: The Renewable Transport Fuel Obligations (Amendment) Order 2020, preamble. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2020/1541

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this Order is delegated legislation made under the Energy Act 2004 and amends the Renewable Transport Fuel Obligations Order 2007 (S.I. 2007/3072); it is binding as a UK Statutory Instrument on any person who is an obligated supplier under the 2007 Order, and does not itself create a separate duty on a downstream fuel purchaser, carrier, or freight forwarder.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: An impact assessment, in the form of a cost benefit analysis, on the effect that this Order will have on the costs of business and the voluntary sector is available from the Low Carbon Fuels Division *Source: The Renewable Transport Fuel Obligations (Amendment) Order 2020, Explanatory Note. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2020/1541

*Analytical inference:* the Explanatory Memorandum and its annexed impact assessment (cost-benefit analysis) are the controlling supporting documents for this Order's own policy rationale, though this brief's corpus captures only the Order and its own Explanatory Note, not the Memorandum or impact assessment documents themselves.

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does this Order create a new obligation, or does it amend the rate of an existing one?**

*Analytical inference:* it amends the rate (Section 8, obligation 2) of an obligation that already existed under the Renewable Transport Fuel Obligations Order 2007; no new category of obligated party is created by this Order.

**Q2: Does the higher £0.50 multiplier apply retroactively to obligation periods before 1st January 2021?**

FACT: Multiply the main obligation shortfall by— (a) in the case of a main obligation shortfall arising in respect of an obligation period ending on or before 31st December 2020, £0.30; (b) in any other case, £0.50, (“sum B”). *Source: The Renewable Transport Fuel Obligations (Amendment) Order 2020, article 2(2). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2020/1541

*Legal Confirmation Required:* no; the amended text itself splits treatment by obligation-period end date (on or before 31st December 2020 stays at £0.30; any other case is £0.50), so the change is prospective from the stated obligation-period boundary, not retroactive.

**Q3: Does this Order change the amount of the article 23 civil penalty itself?**

FACT: (8A) In order to establish the value of an RTF certificate in accordance with paragraph (8), were the fuel to which it relates to fall within the main obligation shortfall under paragraph (7) of article 21, the multiplier for the purpose of calculating sum B referred to in Step 4 of that paragraph is £0.30. *Source: The Renewable Transport Fuel Obligations (Amendment) Order 2020, article 2(3). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2020/1541

*Legal Confirmation Required:* no; the Explanatory Note states this consequential amendment exists specifically "to ensure the amount of any civil penalty payable in accordance with that article is unchanged" despite the main-obligation multiplier increase, by fixing the civil-penalty-calculation multiplier at the prior £0.30 rate.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

**1. Citation and commencement.** FACT: This Order may be cited as the Renewable Transport Fuel Obligations (Amendment) Order 2020 and comes into force on 31st December 2020. *Source: The Renewable Transport Fuel Obligations (Amendment) Order 2020, article 1. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2020/1541

**2. Main-obligation shortfall multiplier increase.** FACT: Multiply the main obligation shortfall by— (a) in the case of a main obligation shortfall arising in respect of an obligation period ending on or before 31st December 2020, £0.30; (b) in any other case, £0.50, (“sum B”). *Source: The Renewable Transport Fuel Obligations (Amendment) Order 2020, article 2(2). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2020/1541

**3. Consequential civil-penalty calculation multiplier held at £0.30.** FACT: (8A) In order to establish the value of an RTF certificate in accordance with paragraph (8), were the fuel to which it relates to fall within the main obligation shortfall under paragraph (7) of article 21, the multiplier for the purpose of calculating sum B referred to in Step 4 of that paragraph is £0.30. *Source: The Renewable Transport Fuel Obligations (Amendment) Order 2020, article 2(3). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2020/1541

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this new paragraph (8A) exists only to keep the article 23 civil-penalty figure unchanged while the main-obligation multiplier (obligation 2 above) rises; the two multipliers now diverge by design.

**4. Effective date of the higher multiplier.** FACT: The amendment increases the multiplier that will be applied to any shortfall in a supplier’s main renewable transport fuel obligation (as defined in article 4(6) of the RTFO Order) from £0.30 to £0.50 for obligation periods beginning on or after 1st January 2021. *Source: The Renewable Transport Fuel Obligations (Amendment) Order 2020, Explanatory Note. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2020/1541

**5. The underlying obligation this Order amends.** FACT: It amends a step of the calculation used to determine the amount a supplier must pay to discharge any shortfall in their renewable transport fuel obligation in accordance with article 21 of the RTFO Order. *Source: The Renewable Transport Fuel Obligations (Amendment) Order 2020, Explanatory Note. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2020/1541

**Qualification accounting.** Per-year trajectory: CAPTURED (see metadata.requirement_trajectory: the two-tier obligation-period boundary at 31st December 2020/1st January 2021, with no further step or per-year phase-in stated). Exceptions and carve-outs: No exceptions are stated in Articles 1 to 2 of this Order. Scope limits: No scope limits are stated in Articles 1 to 2 of this Order.

Obligations surveyed: 7; workspace-adjacent: 5; extracted as FACT: 5.

# 11. Operational System Requirements

*Operational implication:* an obligated supplier's shortfall-payment and civil-penalty calculation workflows should key off article 21(7)'s obligation-period end date (on or before 31st December 2020 versus any other case) to select the correct multiplier, since the article 23 civil-penalty multiplier is now fixed at £0.30 independent of the main-obligation multiplier.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 15th December 2020: The Renewable Transport Fuel Obligations (Amendment) Order 2020 made and signed by the Parliamentary Under Secretary of State for Transport.
- 31st December 2020: The Order comes into force; also the last obligation-period end date carrying the prior £0.30 main-obligation shortfall multiplier.
- 1st January 2021: The start of the first obligation period carrying the increased £0.50 main-obligation shortfall multiplier.

*Analytical inference:* all three dates above are already historical relative to the current export date; no forward monitoring action is required for this specific rate change.

*Source for timeline entries: The Renewable Transport Fuel Obligations (Amendment) Order 2020, articles 1-2 and Explanatory Note, UK SI 2020/1541 (https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2020/1541).*

# 15. Sources

# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks Decision No 1/2023 of the Joint Committee established by the Agreement between the European Union and the Swiss Confederation on the linking of their greenhouse gas emissions trading systems ("the Agreement"), which replaces Annex I (essential criteria) and Annex IV (sensitivity-level definitions) to that Agreement. It exists to give a workspace with EU or Swiss aviation, or stationary-installation, ETS exposure a single record of what the linked EU-Switzerland ETS now requires.

FACT: HAS ADOPTED THIS DECISION: Article 1 Annexes I and IV to the Agreement are replaced by the text set out in Annexes I and IV in the Appendix to this Decision. *Source: Decision No 1/2023, EUR-Lex CELEX 22024D0301. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:22024D0301

FACT: Done at Zürich, on 15 November 2023. *Source: Decision No 1/2023, signature line. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:22024D0301

*Analytical inference:* this document tracks only the substantive content this Decision restates (Section 8); it is not itself the underlying Directive 2003/87/EC or CO2 Act/Ordinance text.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: The adoption of Decision No 2/2019 of the Joint Committee ( 2 ) fulfilled the conditions for linking set out in the Agreement and enabled the Agreement to enter into force on 1 January 2020. *Source: Decision No 1/2023, recital 1. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:22024D0301

FACT: On 1 January 2021, a new trading period started in the emissions trading system of the European Union and the emissions trading system of Switzerland. *Source: Decision No 1/2023, recital 3. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:22024D0301

FACT: As from 1 January 2020, flights from an aerodrome situated in the territory of the European Economic Area (“EEA”) to aerodromes situated in the territory of Switzerland shall be covered by the EU ETS, while flights from aerodromes situated in the territory of Switzerland to aerodromes situated in the territory of the EEA shall be excluded from the EU ETS, pursuant to Article 25a of Directive 2003/87/EC. *Source: Decision No 1/2023, Appendix, Annex I, Part B, point 2. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:22024D0301

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the linked EU-Switzerland ETS applies directly to aircraft operators and stationary installations covered by the EU ETS or the ETS of Switzerland; whether a specific workspace's own flights or installations fall within either scheme is a fact-specific question outside this brief's scope, but a workspace operating air cargo flights between an EEA aerodrome and a Swiss aerodrome (or vice versa) is squarely within the cross-border rule quoted above.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

FACT: The new trading period introduced regulatory changes to both emissions trading systems. *Source: Decision No 1/2023, recital 4. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:22024D0301

FACT: Decision No 1/2022 of the Joint Committee of 9 December 2022 has amended Annex IV to the Agreement with respect to security markings. *Source: Decision No 1/2023, recital 6. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:22024D0301

*Operational implication:* this Decision is a Joint Committee amendment reconciling both ETS's existing rules with regulatory changes already introduced from the 2021 trading period onward; the substantive obligations it restates (Section 8) are not new duties as of this Decision, but the Decision is the current authoritative statement of them.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this Decision is adopted by the Joint Committee under Article 13(2) of the Agreement between the EU and Switzerland; it binds both Parties' own ETS legislation (Directive 2003/87/EC on the EU side, the CO2 Act and CO2 Ordinance on the Swiss side) to the essential criteria set out in the replaced Annex I, rather than creating a duty running directly to a private operator independent of each Party's own domestic ETS legislation.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: The EU legislation provides that, by 15 May each year and starting in 2017, the Commission is to publish the total number of allowances in circulation (TNAC). *Source: Decision No 1/2023, Appendix, Annex I, Part A, point 5. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:22024D0301

*Analytical inference:* the EU's Market Stability Reserve mechanism (referenced here as the authoritative EU-side allowance-supply-management tool) is not itself amended by this Decision, but Annex I as replaced continues to treat its Swiss equivalent (an auction-volume reduction mechanism under Article 19(5) of the CO2 Act) as an essential-criteria match.

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does an aircraft operator based in the EEA that only overflies Switzerland (without landing) fall within this cross-border rule?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* No source in this brief's corpus addresses overflight without arrival or departure at a Swiss or EEA aerodrome; the cross-border rule (Section 2) is stated only in terms of flights that arrive at or depart from a covered aerodrome.

**Q2: Are humanitarian, search-and-rescue, or small-aircraft cargo flights covered by this ETS?**

FACT: Flights related to search and rescue, fire-fighting flights, humanitarian flights and emergency medical service flights. *Source: Decision No 1/2023, Appendix, Annex I, Part B, point 2 (Limitations of coverage, item 3). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:22024D0301

*Legal Confirmation Required:* these and the other numbered categories in Section 12 are excluded from the general coverage rule; whether a specific workspace flight qualifies for one of these categories is a fact-specific question outside this brief's scope.

**Q3: Does the aviation cap allocation percentage (15%/3%/82%) apply identically to both the EU ETS and the ETS of Switzerland?**

FACT: The allowances in the cap shall be allocated as follows: — 15 % shall be auctioned — 3 % shall be set aside in a special reserve — 82 % shall be allocated free of charge. *Source: Decision No 1/2023, Appendix, Annex I, Part B, point 4. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:22024D0301

*Analytical inference:* the essential-criteria structure requires the Swiss cap allocation to mirror this EU-side percentage split (auctioned/reserved/free), per the "at least as stringent" and "similar level of stringency" language used throughout Annex I.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

**1. Mandatory participation.** FACT: Participation in the ETS shall be mandatory for the installations carrying out the activities and emitting the greenhouse gases (“GHG”) listed below. *Source: Decision No 1/2023, Appendix, Annex I, Part A, point 1. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:22024D0301

**2. Activities and GHG coverage cross-reference.** FACT: The ETS shall cover at least the activities set out in: — Annex I to Directive 2003/87/EC, as in force on the date of entry into force of this Agreement. — Article 40(1) of and Annex 6 to the CO 2 Ordinance, as in force on 1 January 2022. *Source: Decision No 1/2023, Appendix, Annex I, Part A, point 2. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:22024D0301

**3. Cap and linear reduction factor.** FACT: A cap shall be set for the ETS, which is at least as stringent as the one in: — Articles 9 and 9a of Directive 2003/87/EC, as in force on the date of entry into force of this Agreement. The linear reduction factor of 1,74 % per year will increase to 2,2 % per year as from 2021 and will apply to all sectors in accordance with Directive (EU) 2018/410, as in force on the date of entry into force of this Agreement. *Source: Decision No 1/2023, Appendix, Annex I, Part A, point 4. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:22024D0301

*Analytical inference:* the 2,2 % linear reduction factor applies from 2021 onward under both the EU and Swiss ETS, so a workspace's own allowance-supply forecasting should use the same annual tightening rate on both sides of the linked system.

**4. Free allocation basis.** FACT: Free allocation shall be calculated on the basis of benchmarks and adjustment factors. Allowances which are not allocated free of charge shall be auctioned or invalidated. *Source: Decision No 1/2023, Appendix, Annex I, Part A, point 10. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:22024D0301

**5. Penalties equivalence requirement.** FACT: The ETS shall provide for penalties in the same circumstances and of the same magnitude as those set out in: — Article 16 of Directive 2003/87/EC, as in force on the date of entry into force of this Agreement. *Source: Decision No 1/2023, Appendix, Annex I, Part A, point 11. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:22024D0301

**6. Monitoring and reporting equivalence requirement.** FACT: Monitoring and reporting in the ETS shall at least be as stringent as in: — Article 14 of and Annex IV to Directive 2003/87/EC — Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2018/2066 of 19 December 2018 on the monitoring and reporting of greenhouse gas emissions pursuant to Directive 2003/87/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council and amending Commission Regulation (EU) No 601/2012, as in force on 1 January 2021. *Source: Decision No 1/2023, Appendix, Annex I, Part A, point 12. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:22024D0301

**7. Verification and accreditation equivalence requirement.** FACT: Verification and accreditation in the ETS shall at least be as stringent as in: — Article 15 of and Annex V to Directive 2003/87/EC — Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2018/2067 of 19 December 2018 on the verification of data and on the accreditation of verifiers pursuant to Directive 2003/87/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council, as in force on the date of entry into force of this Agreement. *Source: Decision No 1/2023, Appendix, Annex I, Part A, point 13. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:22024D0301

**8. Aviation cap allocation percentages.** FACT: The allowances in the cap shall be allocated as follows: — 15 % shall be auctioned — 3 % shall be set aside in a special reserve — 82 % shall be allocated free of charge. *Source: Decision No 1/2023, Appendix, Annex I, Part B, point 4. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:22024D0301

**9. Aviation benchmark rate.** FACT: The annual benchmark is 0,000642186914222035 allowances per tonne-kilometre. *Source: Decision No 1/2023, Appendix, Annex I, Part B, point 7. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:22024D0301

*Operational implication:* an aircraft operator's free allocation of aviation allowances is calculated by multiplying its own reported tonne-kilometre data for the reference year by this benchmark rate.

**10. Aircraft-operator account-opening deadline.** FACT: The application by the aircraft operator or an authorised representative of the aircraft operator shall be addressed to the national administrator (FOEN for Switzerland) within 30 working days from the approval of the monitoring plan of the aircraft operator or its transferral from an EU (EEA) Member State to the Swiss authorities. *Source: Decision No 1/2023, Appendix, Annex I, Part C. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:22024D0301

**11. Entry into force.** FACT: This Decision shall enter into force on the date of its adoption. *Source: Decision No 1/2023, Article 2. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:22024D0301

**Aviation scope, exceptions and limits (qualification support).** FACT: 1. Scope of coverage Flights which arrive at, or depart from, an aerodrome situated in the territory of Switzerland, except flights which depart from an aerodrome situated in the territory of the EEA. *Source: Decision No 1/2023, Appendix, Annex I, Part B, point 1. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:22024D0301

**Qualification accounting.** Per-year trajectory: CAPTURED (see metadata.requirement_trajectory: the linear reduction factor step from 1,74% to 2,2% per year effective 2021, and the no-international-credits rule effective the same date). Exceptions and carve-outs: CAPTURED via the FACT claim immediately above declaring this section, whose source_span contains the unnegated word "except" ("...except flights which depart from an aerodrome situated in the territory of the EEA."). Scope limits: CAPTURED via the same claim's source_span, which also opens with the word "Scope" ("1. Scope of coverage Flights which arrive at, or depart from...").

Obligations surveyed: 12; workspace-adjacent: 11; extracted as FACT: 11.
Shortfall: obligation 12 of the twelve surveyed (the EU Market Stability Reserve / Swiss auction-volume-reduction mechanism, Section 5) is a market-management mechanism affecting allowance supply generally rather than a duty running to an individual operator, so it is not counted toward workspace-adjacent or extracted-as-FACT for this section, though it is grounded elsewhere in this brief (Section 5).

# 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

FACT: 1. Scope of coverage Flights which arrive at, or depart from, an aerodrome situated in the territory of Switzerland, except flights which depart from an aerodrome situated in the territory of the EEA. *Source: Decision No 1/2023, Appendix, Annex I, Part B, point 1. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:22024D0301

*Operational implication:* for air cargo operations specifically, coverage turns on the aerodrome pair a flight arrives at or departs from (Switzerland versus EEA), not on the cargo carried; the numbered exclusions in Section 12 (military/customs/police, humanitarian, small aircraft, low-emission operators) are the only stated carve-outs from that aerodrome-pair rule.

# 11. Operational System Requirements

*Operational implication:* an aircraft operator newly attributed to Switzerland's administration should track the 30-working-day account-opening deadline (Section 8, obligation 10) from the date its monitoring plan is approved or its file is transferred from an EU/EEA Member State, and should use the same tonne-kilometre reference-year methodology (Section 8, obligation 9) the EU ETS uses to calculate its own free allocation.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

FACT: 1. Scope of coverage Flights which arrive at, or depart from, an aerodrome situated in the territory of Switzerland, except flights which depart from an aerodrome situated in the territory of the EEA. *Source: Decision No 1/2023, Appendix, Annex I, Part B, point 1. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:22024D0301

FACT: Military, customs and police flights. *Source: Decision No 1/2023, Appendix, Annex I, Part B, point 2 (Limitations of coverage, item 2). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:22024D0301

FACT: Flights related to search and rescue, fire-fighting flights, humanitarian flights and emergency medical service flights. *Source: Decision No 1/2023, Appendix, Annex I, Part B, point 2 (Limitations of coverage, item 3). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:22024D0301

FACT: Flights performed by aircraft with a certified maximum take-off mass of less than 5 700 kilograms. *Source: Decision No 1/2023, Appendix, Annex I, Part B, point 2 (Limitations of coverage, item 9). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:22024D0301

FACT: Flights of commercial aircraft operators with total annual emissions lower than 10 000 tonnes on flights covered by the ETS of Switzerland or fewer than 243 flights per period for three consecutive four-month periods within the scope of the ETS of Switzerland, if the operators are not covered by the EU ETS. *Source: Decision No 1/2023, Appendix, Annex I, Part B, point 2 (Limitations of coverage, item 10). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:22024D0301

FACT: Flights of non-commercial aircraft operators covered by the ETS of Switzerland with total annual emissions lower than 1 000 tonnes in accordance with the respective derogation applied in the EU ETS, if the operators are not covered by the EU ETS. *Source: Decision No 1/2023, Appendix, Annex I, Part B, point 2 (Limitations of coverage, item 11). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:22024D0301

FACT: No entitlements to use international credits are provided for in Union law from 2021 onwards. No entitlements to use international credits are provided for in Swiss law from 2021 onwards. *Source: Decision No 1/2023, Appendix, Annex I, Part A, point 8 and Part B, point 9. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:22024D0301

*Operational implication:* a freight-forwarding workspace's own air cargo operators most likely to qualify for an exclusion are the low-emission-operator categories (items 10 and 11 above, quantified by annual tonnes or flight count) rather than the military/humanitarian/small-aircraft categories, which target a different operator profile.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 1 January 2020: The Agreement between the EU and Switzerland on linking their ETS enters into force, following Decision No 2/2019 of the Joint Committee.
- 1 January 2021: A new trading period starts in both the EU ETS and the ETS of Switzerland, introducing regulatory changes that this Decision's Annex I amendment reflects.
- 9 December 2022: Decision No 1/2022 of the Joint Committee amends Annex IV to the Agreement with respect to security markings.
- 15 November 2023: Decision No 1/2023 adopted at Zürich, replacing Annexes I and IV; the Decision enters into force on this same date, its own date of adoption.

*Source for timeline entries: Decision No 1/2023, recitals 1, 3 and 6, and the Decision's own signature line and Article 2, EUR-Lex CELEX 22024D0301 (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:22024D0301).*

metadata.what_is_it: A Joint Committee Decision replacing the essential-criteria Annex (Annex I) and the sensitivity-level definitions Annex (Annex IV) of the Agreement linking the EU and Swiss emissions trading systems, restating equivalence requirements for participation, caps, penalties, monitoring, verification, and aviation coverage on both sides of the linked ETS.
metadata.why_matters: A workspace operating air cargo flights between an EEA aerodrome and a Swiss aerodrome (or a stationary installation covered by either ETS) needs the current, linked essential criteria for cap, penalties, monitoring, verification, and aviation-specific coverage exclusions this Decision restates.

aviation cap allocated 15 percent auctioned / 3 percent reserve / 82 percent free
aviation benchmark 0.000642186914222035 allowances per tonne-kilometre
30 working day aircraft-operator account-opening deadline
metadata.cost_mechanism: Penalties for ETS non-compliance are set at the same magnitude as Article 16 of Directive 2003/87/EC on the EU side, and at an equivalent level under Article 21 of the Swiss CO2 Act; the captured text does not itself restate the numeric penalty figure from Article 16.

steps.label: Linear reduction factor increases from 1,74% to 2,2% per year, applying to all sectors
No entitlements to use international credits under either Union or Swiss law from this date

requirement_trajectory.note: Both steps take effect at the same 1 January 2021 trading-period boundary; no further per-year step is stated in this corpus.

metadata.enforcement_body: European Commission and national competent authorities on the EU side; the Federal Office of the Environment (FOEN) and Swiss competent authorities on the Swiss side.

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks The Motor Fuel (Composition and Content) and the Biofuel (Labelling) (Amendment) (No. 2) Regulations 2021 (UK SI 2021/894), which amends the Motor Fuel (Composition and Content) Regulations 1999 and the Biofuel (Labelling) Regulations 2004 to introduce a "premium 95 grade petrol" fuel category with its own minimum ethanol content, a winter exemption from that content requirement, refinery/blending-facility shortage provisions, and a bioethanol-blend labelling duty.

FACT: The Motor Fuel (Composition and Content) and the Biofuel (Labelling) (Amendment) (No. 2) Regulations 2021 *Source: The Motor Fuel (Composition and Content) and the Biofuel (Labelling) (Amendment) (No. 2) Regulations 2021, UK SI 2021/894. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2021/894

FACT: Made 22nd July 2021 *Source: same instrument, signature line. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2021/894

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: premium 95 grade petrol ” means petrol that has a research octane number of at least 95 but less than 97 measured in accordance with the test method referred to in Table 1 of Schedule AA1 *Source: same instrument, regulation 3(2)(h). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2021/894

FACT: Premium 95 grade petrol will not comply with a specified requirement unless, in addition to the requirements of paragraphs (2) or (3), it has a minimum ethanol content of 5.5% by volume measured in accordance with the test method referred to in Table 1 of Schedule AA1. *Source: same instrument, regulation 4(f). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2021/894

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the ethanol-content duty runs to a person who blends, distributes, or sells premium 95 grade petrol under the amended 1999 Regulations, not to a carrier or freight forwarder as such; whether a specific workspace's own fuel-supply operations fall within that duty-holder class is a fact-specific question outside this brief's scope.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

FACT: (1A) Paragraph (1) does not apply to premium 95 grade petrol which is sold during the period beginning on 1st September 2021 and ending on 1st November 2021 if that petrol complies with the winter petrol requirement, except for the minimum ethanol content specified in regulation 3(8). *Source: same instrument, regulation 6 (inserting paragraph (1A) into regulation 5 of the 1999 Regulations). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2021/894

*Operational implication:* the winter exemption window (1st September 2021 to 1st November 2021) is already historical relative to the current date, but the underlying mechanism (a seasonal exemption from the ethanol-content requirement, conditioned on meeting the winter petrol requirement) is the operative structure a workspace should expect to recur in any future seasonal amendment of the same kind.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

FACT: The amendments to the Motor Fuel (Composition and Content) Regulations 1999( 3 ) made by Part 2 extend to Great Britain. *Source: same instrument, regulation 1(4). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2021/894

FACT: The amendments to the Biofuel (Labelling) Regulations 2004( 4 ) made by Part 3 extend to the United Kingdom. *Source: same instrument, regulation 1(5). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2021/894

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this Statutory Instrument is made under the Clean Air Act 1993 and is directly binding within its stated extent (Great Britain for the Motor Fuel amendments, the United Kingdom for the Biofuel Labelling amendments); it does not itself create a duty on a carrier or freight forwarder who merely transports fuel rather than blending, distributing, or selling it to the ultimate consumer.

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does the winter exemption (Section 3) apply automatically, or only if the petrol otherwise meets the winter petrol requirement?**

FACT: (1A) Paragraph (1) does not apply to premium 95 grade petrol which is sold during the period beginning on 1st September 2021 and ending on 1st November 2021 if that petrol complies with the winter petrol requirement, except for the minimum ethanol content specified in regulation 3(8). *Source: same instrument, regulation 6. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2021/894

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the exemption is conditional ("if that petrol complies with the winter petrol requirement"), not automatic; a workspace relying on it should confirm the petrol otherwise meets that requirement.

**Q2: What must a distributor do if a refinery or blending-facility shortage prevents it from meeting the minimum ethanol content?**

FACT: A person must, within 2 working days beginning with date on which the relevant period begins, notify the Secretary of State that they are distributing, or will distribute, premium 95 grade petrol pursuant to paragraph (7) *Source: same instrument, regulation 8 (inserting paragraph (9) into regulation 6 of the 1999 Regulations). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2021/894

*Operational implication:* the shortage-relief mechanism (Section 8) requires prompt notification, a subsequent remediation report, and is capped in frequency (Section 8); a workspace relying on it should track all three obligations, not just the initial notification.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

**1. Two-tier commencement.** FACT: Except as specified in paragraph (3), these Regulations come into force 21 days after the day on which the Regulations are made. *Source: same instrument, regulation 1(2). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2021/894

FACT: Regulations 3(2)(h), 4(d) and (f), 5, 6 and 8(b) and Part 5 come into force on 1st September 2021. *Source: same instrument, regulation 1(3). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2021/894

FACT: Coming into force Regulations 1, 2, 3(1), (2)(a) to (g) and (3), 4(a) to (c) and (e), 7, 8(a) and 9 to 14 12th August 2021 Regulations 3(2)(h), 4(d) and (f), 5, 6, 8(b) and 15 1st September 2021 *Source: same instrument, header block (stating the same two commencement dates the operative regulation 1(2)/(3) formula produces). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2021/894

*Legal Confirmation Required:* a person distributing or selling premium 95 grade petrol must comply with the ethanol-content and labelling duties below (obligations 4, 6-9) from the dates this obligation states; whether a specific workspace is itself a duty-holder under any given obligation is a fact-specific question outside this brief's scope.

**2. Territorial extent.** FACT: The amendments to the Motor Fuel (Composition and Content) Regulations 1999( 3 ) made by Part 2 extend to Great Britain. *Source: same instrument, regulation 1(4). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2021/894

FACT: The amendments to the Biofuel (Labelling) Regulations 2004( 4 ) made by Part 3 extend to the United Kingdom. *Source: same instrument, regulation 1(5). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2021/894

**3. Premium 95 grade petrol definition.** FACT: premium 95 grade petrol ” means petrol that has a research octane number of at least 95 but less than 97 measured in accordance with the test method referred to in Table 1 of Schedule AA1 *Source: same instrument, regulation 3(2)(h). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2021/894

**4. Minimum ethanol content requirement.** FACT: Premium 95 grade petrol will not comply with a specified requirement unless, in addition to the requirements of paragraphs (2) or (3), it has a minimum ethanol content of 5.5% by volume measured in accordance with the test method referred to in Table 1 of Schedule AA1. *Source: same instrument, regulation 4(f). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2021/894

**5. Winter exemption from the ethanol-content requirement.** FACT: (1A) Paragraph (1) does not apply to premium 95 grade petrol which is sold during the period beginning on 1st September 2021 and ending on 1st November 2021 if that petrol complies with the winter petrol requirement, except for the minimum ethanol content specified in regulation 3(8). *Source: same instrument, regulation 6. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2021/894

**6. Shortage notification deadline.** FACT: A person must, within 2 working days beginning with date on which the relevant period begins, notify the Secretary of State that they are distributing, or will distribute, premium 95 grade petrol pursuant to paragraph (7) *Source: same instrument, regulation 8. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2021/894

**7. Post-shortage remediation report deadline.** FACT: A person who distributes petrol pursuant to paragraph (7) must, before the end of the period of 30 days beginning with the date on which the relevant period ends or, where consent is given under paragraph (11) to distribute for a longer period, beginning with the date on which that period ends, provide the Secretary of State with details of the measures that have been taken to prevent a reoccurrence of the issue mentioned in paragraph (7). *Source: same instrument, regulation 8. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2021/894

**8. Shortage-relief frequency limit.** FACT: A person must not distribute premium 95 grade petrol pursuant to paragraph (7) more than 3 times in any 12 month period as a consequence of an issue occurring at the same refinery or blending facility. *Source: same instrument, regulation 8. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2021/894

**9. Bioethanol-blend labelling requirement.** FACT: A person must not sell, or offer for sale, to the ultimate consumer any blend containing more than 5% but not more than 10% by volume of bioethanol, unless the words “Suitable for most petrol vehicles: check before use” are displayed prominently on any dispenser from which such blend is sold or offered for sale to the ultimate consumer. *Source: same instrument, regulation 13 (amending regulation 3 of the Biofuel (Labelling) Regulations 2004). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2021/894

**Qualification accounting.** Per-year trajectory: No phase-in is stated in Regulations 1 to 15 of this instrument beyond the two fixed commencement dates already stated as substantive requirement 1; the ethanol-content and labelling duties take effect on those dates with no further year-over-year step. Exceptions and carve-outs: CAPTURED via the FACT claim declaring this section for the winter exemption above, whose source_span contains the unnegated word "except" ("...except for the minimum ethanol content specified in regulation 3(8)."). Scope limits: CAPTURED via the same claim's source_span, which contains the unnegated phrase "does not apply" ("Paragraph (1) does not apply to premium 95 grade petrol...").

Obligations surveyed: 11; workspace-adjacent: 9; extracted as FACT: 9.
Shortfall: two of the eleven surveyed obligations (the five-yearly statutory-review requirement, Section 5, and the draft-affirmative parliamentary procedure this instrument itself was made under) are process/self-review duties running to the Secretary of State or Parliament rather than to a fuel distributor, retailer, or blender, so they are not counted toward workspace-adjacent or extracted-as-FACT for this section, though the review requirement is grounded elsewhere in this brief (Section 5).

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: The first report must be published before the end of the period of five years beginning with the date on which this regulation comes into force. *Source: same instrument, regulation 15(2) (Part 5, Review). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2021/894

*Analytical inference:* this Part 5 review clause is the authoritative mechanism by which the Department for Transport itself must reassess these Regulations' own regulatory provision; it does not create any duty on a fuel distributor or retailer.

# 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

FACT: premium 95 grade petrol ” means petrol that has a research octane number of at least 95 but less than 97 measured in accordance with the test method referred to in Table 1 of Schedule AA1 *Source: same instrument, regulation 3(2)(h). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2021/894

*Operational implication:* "premium 95 grade petrol" (research octane number 95 to under 97) is a NEW product category this instrument creates, distinct from ordinary unleaded petrol (research octane number at least 95 under Schedule AA1, Table 1) and from super unleaded petrol; a workspace's fuel-inventory classification should track it separately given its own distinct ethanol-content rule (Section 8).

# 11. Operational System Requirements

*Operational implication:* a distributor invoking the shortage-relief mechanism (Section 8, obligations 6-8) should maintain a compliance calendar tracking the 2-working-day notification deadline, the 30-day post-period remediation-report deadline, and the running count of uses within any rolling 12-month period against the 3-times cap.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

FACT: (1A) Paragraph (1) does not apply to premium 95 grade petrol which is sold during the period beginning on 1st September 2021 and ending on 1st November 2021 if that petrol complies with the winter petrol requirement, except for the minimum ethanol content specified in regulation 3(8). *Source: same instrument, regulation 6. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2021/894

FACT: A person must not distribute premium 95 grade petrol pursuant to paragraph (7) more than 3 times in any 12 month period as a consequence of an issue occurring at the same refinery or blending facility. *Source: same instrument, regulation 8. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2021/894

*Legal Confirmation Required:* both the winter exemption and the shortage-relief mechanism are conditional exceptions to the general minimum-ethanol-content rule (Section 8, obligation 4); neither removes the underlying rule for petrol outside their own stated conditions.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 22nd July 2021: The Motor Fuel (Composition and Content) and the Biofuel (Labelling) (Amendment) (No. 2) Regulations 2021 made and signed by the Parliamentary Under Secretary of State for Transport.
- 12th August 2021: Most of these Regulations come into force (21 days after the making date).
- 1st September 2021: Regulations 3(2)(h), 4(d) and (f), 5, 6, 8(b) and Part 5 come into force, including the minimum-ethanol-content requirement and the winter exemption's own start date.
- 1st November 2021: The winter exemption's own end date; from this date the general minimum-ethanol-content requirement resumes applying to premium 95 grade petrol without the seasonal exception.

*Source for timeline entries: The Motor Fuel (Composition and Content) and the Biofuel (Labelling) (Amendment) (No. 2) Regulations 2021, regulations 1 and 6, UK SI 2021/894 (https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2021/894).*

# 15. Sources

metadata.what_is_it: A UK Statutory Instrument that creates a new premium 95 grade petrol product category with its own minimum 5.5% ethanol content requirement, a seasonal exemption from that requirement, refinery/blending-facility shortage provisions, and a bioethanol-blend labelling duty for fuel dispensers.

winter exemption from 1st September 2021 to 1st November 2021
shortage notification deadline 2 working days
post-shortage remediation report deadline 30 days
shortage relief capped at 3 times per 12 month period
